questions.stem: Why was Keith Stonehouse left with a $1,000 bill?
questions.stemZh: 为什么Keith Stonehouse最后要支付一张1000美元的账单？
questions.answerText: His son had ordered food from several restaurants.

explain.定位: A man was left with a $1,000 bill, after his 6-year-old son ordered a virtual buffet of food from several restaurants last weekend. 上周末，一名男子的6岁儿子从多家餐馆点了一桌虚拟盛宴，结果他留下了一张1000美元的 账单。
explain.信号: after 因果链。新闻首句用 after his 6-year-old son ordered... 直接交代了账单产生的原 因：after 前面是结果（$1,000 bill），后面是原因（儿子点餐）。
explain.替换: his 6-year-old son ordered a virtual buffet of food from several restaurants ↔ His son had ordered food from several restaurants. 概括式同义替换
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 录音确实出现了 'online food ordering account'，但用该账户点餐的是儿子，不是父亲； A 把动作主体从 son 偷换成 He，属于典型的主体张冠李戴。 借用原文：his father's online food ordering account B) 原词陷阱 录音提到父亲 'let his son use his cell phone to play a game'，但儿子实际上没玩游戏， 而是去点餐了；B 把 'play a game' 偷换成 'pay for playing a game'，动作和目的都错 了。 借用原文：let his son use his cell phone to play a game D) 未提及 录音从未提到 'five-star restaurant'，也未说父亲外出就餐；D 用高档餐厅制造生活常识诱 惑，属于录音中找不到依据的干扰。

optionsZh: 他曾使用自己的网上点餐账户购买餐食。
他的儿子曾用他的手机支付玩游戏的费用。
他的儿子曾从几家餐馆订餐。
他曾在一家著名的五星级餐厅用餐。
options: He had bought meals with his online food ordering account.
His son had used his cell phone to pay for playing a game.
His son had ordered food from several restaurants.
He had dined out at a famous five-star restaurant.

questions.stem: What does the news report say Keith Stonehouse is planning to do?
questions.stemZh: 新闻报道说Keith Stonehouse计划做什么？

explain.定位: The father is planning to change his password. 这位父亲打算更改他的密码。
explain.信号: planning to 直接对应题干。is planning to change his password 中的 'planning to' 与 题干 'is planning to do' 完全同构，后面接的 'change his password' 即为答案动作。
explain.替换: change his password ↔Change his password. 原词复现 + 主语省略
explain.排除: A) 未提及 录音中没有出现 'teach his son a lesson' 或任何惩罚、教育的表述；A 是利用家长的'常识 反应'编造的合理但无依据选项。 C) 原词陷阱 录音确实提到 'invited some neighbors over to eat some of it'，但目的是分享食物，不 是 'ask his neighbors for help'；C 盗用 'neighbors' 一词并改变了动作性质。 借用原文：invited some neighbors over to eat some of it D) 原词陷阱 录音提到 'Most of the food went into the family's refrigerators'，但完全没有 'buy a bigger refrigerator' 的计划；D 用 'refrigerator' 这个原词做诱饵，把'已有冰箱'偷换成'要 买更大的冰箱'。 借用原文：refrigerators

optionsZh: 给他的儿子一个教训。
更改他的密码。
向邻居求助。
买一台更大的冰箱。
questions._leakedNextScript: Animal behaviour experts looked at more than 100 research papers. They examined how visitors affected the behaviour of more than 250 species in zoos. They found that elephants socialised more with each other during public feeding times. After public feeding times, they were more likely to search for food and less likely to be inactive. In the presence of many visitors, elephants were less likely to use repetitive behaviours which often indicate boredom.

questions.stem: What did animal behaviour experts do according to the news report?
questions.stemZh: 根据新闻报道，动物行为专家做了什么？
questions.answerText: They examined how visitors affected animal behaviour in zoos.

explain.定位: They examined how visitors affected the behaviour of more than 250 species in zoos. 他们研究了游客如何影响动物园里250多个物种的行为。
explain.信号: 直接陈述研究内容的动作句。Paragraph 1 开头先说专家 looked at more than 100 research papers，紧接着 They examined how visitors affected the behaviour of more than 250 species in zoos. 用 examined 直接回答题干；对新闻细节题，这种紧跟主题引 入的动作句就是答案落点。
explain.替换: They examined how visitors affected the behaviour of more than 250 species in zoos. ↔ They examined how visitors affected animal behaviour in zoos. 具体数量概括为 animal，研究对象一致
explain.排除: B) 原词陷阱 录音提到 during public feeding times 与 After public feeding times，但这是在说大象 的行为变化，B 项把 public feeding times 改成 'the best time to feed animals'，既偷换 概念又答非所问。 借用原文：public feeding times C) 偷换概念 some species appear to show good adaptability to the changing conditions of visitors 讲的是适应游客变化，C 项改成 'adapted themselves to life in zoos'，对象从 visitors 变成 zoos，属于偷换概念。 借用原文：good adaptability to the changing conditions of visitors D) 原词陷阱 repetitive behaviours which often indicate boredom 只是研究中的一个发现细节，D 项 把它上升为专家的研究主题 'what behaviours indicated animal boredom'。 借用原文：repetitive behaviours which often indicate boredom

optionsZh: 他们研究了游客如何影响动物园中动物的行为。
他们研究了在公众场合喂食动物的最佳时间。
他们研究了动物如何适应动物园生活。
他们研究了哪些行为表明动物感到无聊。
options: They examined how visitors affected animal behaviour in zoos.
They studied when the best time to feed animals in public was.
They studied how animals adapted themselves to life in zoos.
They examined what behaviours indicated animal boredom.

questions.stem: Why have some animal species likely become used to the presence of humans?
questions.stemZh: 为什么有些动物物种很可能已经习惯了人类的存在？
questions.answerText: They have been born and raised in zoos.

explain.定位: Some animal species have been born and raised in zoos, and so have likely become used to the presence of humans. 有些动物物种在动物园出生、长大，因此可能已经习惯了人类的存在。
explain.信号: 因果连词 and so 把原因和结果钉在一起。题干中的 'become used to the presence of humans' 与答案句后半句完全对应，前半句 'have been born and raised in zoos' 由 and so 引出，正是问题要的 why。
explain.替换: have been born and raised in zoos ↔They have been born and raised in zoos. 原因部分被原样截取，主语由 Some animal species 换成 They
explain.排除: A) 张冠李戴 elephants socialised more with each other 是 Paragraph 1 中关于大象的发现，与题干 问的 'some animal species' 习惯人类无关，且 zookeepers 在录音中从未出现。 借用原文：socialised more with each other B) 答非所问 录音确实提到 some species appear to show good adaptability to the changing conditions of visitors，但这是习惯人类之后表现出的能力，是结果；题干问 why，B 项答 非所问。 借用原文：good adaptability to the changing conditions of visitors C) 未提及录音只说 born and raised in zoos 导致习惯人类存在，从未提到 as pets。 1 Denver is suspending its popular electric bike incentive program. The program was launched in April. It allowed Denver residents to apply for $400 in government funds before buying an electric bike from a participating shop. Residents who met certain income qualifications could qualify for $1,200. More than 3,000 Denver residents applied for incentives within the first 3 weeks. 丹佛暂停了广受欢迎的电动自行车激励计划。该计划于4月启动，允许丹佛居民在从参与计划的商店购买 电动自行车之前，申请400美元的政府补助。符合特定收入条件的居民可获得1,200美元。启动后的前3周 内，超过3,000名丹佛居民申请了补助。 2 The city then changed the program to limit the number of applications each month. On Monday, the city announced the pause. "We're honored to be a part of transforming the way Denver wants to move around," said Grace Rink, Denver's chief climate officer. "We exhausted three years' worth of funding in six months." The city said the program has put 4,400 electric bikes on the streets of Denver and invested $8.6 million into the local economy. The city has provided 2,200 incentives to lower-income residents that represent 68% of the program funding. The city expects to resume the program early next year. It also plans design changes to make participation easier and increase access to the program. 随后，该市对计划进行了调整，限制每月的申请数量。周一，该市宣布暂停该计划。丹佛首席气候官格蕾 丝·林克说：“我们很荣幸能够参与改变丹佛人出行的方式。”她说：“我们在6个月内用尽了原本可供3年使 用的资金。”该市表示，这项计划已让4,400辆电动自行车行驶在丹佛街头，并向当地经济投入了860万美 元。该市已向低收入居民提供2,200项补助，占计划资金的68%。该市预计明年年初恢复该计划，同时还 计划进行设计调整，以便居民更容易参与并扩大计划的覆盖范围。

optionsZh: 它们既与动物园饲养员交往，也彼此交往。
它们表现出与人类共同生活的良好适应性。
它们曾被人类当作宠物饲养。
它们出生并成长于动物园。
options: They socialise with zookeepers as well as with each other.
They show good adaptability to living with humans.
They have been kept as pets by humans.
They have been born and raised in zoos.

questions.stem: What is Denver doing with its popular electric bike incentive program?
questions.stemZh: 丹佛正在如何处理其广受欢迎的电动自行车激励计划？

explain.定位: Denver is suspending its popular electric bike incentive program. 丹佛正在暂停其受欢迎的电动自行车激励项目。
explain.信号: 新闻首句直接点题。Denver is suspending its popular electric bike incentive program 位于新闻首句，直接回答了 What is Denver doing 的问题；suspending 与选项 B 的核心 动词完全一致。
explain.替换: is suspending ↔Suspending it 现在进行时动作直接对应
explain.排除: A) 答非所问 选项 A 的 Adjusting 看似与原文 plans design changes 沾边，但 design changes 是 plan（计划），不是当前正在做的动作，且题干问的是 doing（现在进行）。 借用原文：plans design changes to make participation easier C) 未提及选项 C 的 Reevaluating 在录音中没有对应表述，属于凭空捏造。 D) 偷换概念 选项 D 的 Expanding it 容易被 increase access to the program 诱惑，但 increase access 是 plans（未来设计目标），且项目当前是暂停而非扩张。 借用原文：increase access to the program

questions.stem: How did the electric bike incentive program benefit residents?
questions.stemZh: 电动自行车激励计划如何让居民受益？
questions.answerText: They could get $1,200 from government funds if they qualified.

explain.定位: It allowed Denver residents to apply for $400 in government funds before buying an electric bike from a participating shop. Residents who met certain income qualifications could qualify for $1,200. 它允许丹佛居民在从参与商店购买电动自行车之前申请400美元的政府资金。符合特定收入 资格的居民可以获得1,200美元。
explain.信号: 居民获益的具体说明。题干 benefit residents 问居民如何受益，原文 allowed Denver residents to apply for $400 和 Residents who met certain income qualifications could qualify for $1,200 正是对居民所获资助的直接说明。
explain.替换: Residents who met certain income qualifications could qualify for $1,200 ↔ They could get $1,200 from government funds if they qualified 同义替换：资格条件与获得资助的改写
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 选项 A 把 $400 in government funds 和 launched in April 两个原词拼凑成 buy an electric bike for $400 in April，但原文说的是申请 $400 资金，不是花 $400 买车；April 是项目启动时间，不是买车时间。 借用原文：$400 in government funds before buying an electric bike; launched in April B) 原词陷阱 选项 B 盗用原文 buying an electric bike，但原文说的是申请政府补贴，不是直接打折； discount 在录音中并未出现。 借用原文：buying an electric bike from a participating shop C) 未提及选项 C 的 after-sale service 在原文中没有对应内容，属于无中生有。

optionsZh: 他们可以在四月份花400美元购买一辆电动自行车。
他们可以以折扣价购买自己的第一辆电动自行车。
他们可以享受所购电动自行车的免费售后服务。
如果符合条件，他们可以从政府资金中获得1200美元。
options: They could buy an electric bike for $400 in April.
They could buy their first electric bike at a discount.
They could enjoy free after-sale service for their purchase.
They could get $1,200 from government funds if they qualified.

questions.stem: What does the city of Denver expect to do early next year?
questions.stemZh: 丹佛市预计明年年初会做什么？
questions.answerText: Resume its electric bike incentive program.

explain.定位: The city expects to resume the program early next year. 该市预计将于明年初恢复该项目。
explain.信号: 题干关键词直接复现。原文 expects to resume the program early next year 与题干 expect to do early next year 的关键词 expects / early next year 直接对应，resume 就 是答案动作。
explain.替换: expects to resume the program early next year ↔Resume its electric bike incentive program 同义替换：resume the program = Resume its electric bike incentive program
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 选项 A 把 $400 和 put 4,400 electric bikes on the streets 拼凑成 Put 400 more electric bikes on its streets，数字和时态都错了。 借用原文：$400 in government funds; put 4,400 electric bikes on the streets of Denver B) 偷换概念 选项 B 的 8 percent 在原文中没有依据，可能是把 68% of the program funding 误听或 篡改而来。 借用原文：68% of the program funding D) 与原文相反 选项 D 盗用原文 invested $8.6 million into the local economy，但原文用的是 invested （已完成），而题干问的是 expect to do early next year（未来计划），时态不符。 借用原文：invested $8.6 million into the local economy Section B 1 W: Hey, Mike, what do you think of the museum you visited today? W: 嘿，迈克，你觉得今天参观的博物馆怎么样？ 2 M: Hey, Sue. The museum is great, very interesting. They have loads of stuff there on display. The primitive tools early humans used tell a lot about their life, but my favorite is the coin collection. They have some coins that are over 2,000 years old. M: 嘿，苏。这个博物馆很棒，非常有意思。那里展出了很多东西。早期人类使用的原始工具能让我们了 解到很多他们的生活情况，不过我最喜欢的是钱币收藏。他们有些钱币已经有两千多年的历史了。 3 W: That sounds cool. W: 听起来很酷。 4 M: Yeah, what did you do today? M: 是啊，你今天做了什么？ 5 W: Kathy and I just wandered through the old city centre. The streets are narrow but beautiful with plenty of charm. We saw the Trevi Fountain, which is in all the guidebooks. W: 我和凯西只是逛了逛老城区。街道虽然狭窄，却很漂亮，充满了魅力。我们看了特莱维喷泉，所有旅 游指南上都有介绍。 6 M: How do you like it? M: 你觉得怎么样？ Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 7 W: It's very pretty, but it was overcrowded with tourists. W: 非常漂亮，不过游客太多了，挤得水泄不通。 8 M: Yeah, well, it's crowded everywhere. It is August after all, the busiest month of the year. M: 是啊，到处都很拥挤。毕竟现在是八月，一年中最繁忙的月份。 9 W: Yes, it's like the whole world is here on holiday, including us. What will you do tomorrow? W: 是啊，感觉全世界的人都来这里度假了，包括我们。你明天打算做什么？ 10 M: I haven't decided yet. I was thinking of doing what you did today—wandering the old streets and taking pictures. I was also thinking of visiting the square with the Spanish steps. M: 我还没决定。我在考虑做你今天做的事，逛逛老街，拍拍照。我还在考虑去看看有西班牙阶梯的那个 广场。 11 W: What is that? I haven't heard of it. W: 那是什么地方？我没听说过。 12 M: It's a square where on one side, there are some very wide steps with flowers that go up to a church. It's also in all the tourist guidebooks. It's very famous and pretty. I was also thinking of seeing that tomorrow. M: 那是一个广场，广场一侧有一段很宽的台阶，台阶上摆满了鲜花，一直通向一座教堂。旅游指南上也 都有介绍。那里非常有名，也很漂亮。我也在考虑明天去看看。 13 W: It sounds very nice. Do you mind if Kathy and I join you tomorrow? W: 听起来很不错。你介意明天我和凯西跟你一起去吗？ 14 M: Not at all. I spent the whole day today pretty much alone. Doing tourist stuff with others would be a welcome change. M: 当然不介意。我今天基本上独自待了一整天。和别人一起做些游客会做的事，换换方式也挺不错的。 15 W: Let me ask her first, but I'm sure she'll be up for it. W: 我先问问她，不过我相信她会愿意去的。

optionsZh: 在街头投放另外400辆电动自行车。
将该计划的资金增加8%。
恢复其电动自行车激励计划。
向当地经济投入数百万美元。
options: Put 400 more electric bikes on its streets.
Increase the program funding by 8 percent.
Resume its electric bike incentive program.
Invest millions of dollars into the local economy.

questions.stem: What exhibits does the man like best in the museum he visited?
questions.stemZh: 他最喜欢在参观的博物馆里看到哪些展品？

explain.定位: The primitive tools early humans used tell a lot about their life, but my favorite is the coin collection. 早期人类使用的原始工具能告诉我们很多关于他们生活的信息，但我最喜欢的是硬币收藏。
explain.信号: 转折 but + favorite 点出最爱。男士先提 The primitive tools，随即用 but my favorite is 把重点转向 coin collection，favorite 与题干 like best 同义。
explain.替换: my favorite is the coin collection ↔The coin collection. favorite = like best
explain.排除: B) 原词陷阱 The primitive tools. 确实出现在 The primitive tools early humans used...，但它是 but 之前的铺垫，与 like best 无关。 借用原文：The primitive tools early humans used tell a lot about their life C) 未提及录音中只提到 tools 与 coin collection，完全没有 ornaments 这一展品。 D) 偷换概念 The 2,000-year-old clothes. 盗用了 over 2,000 years old 这一数字，但原文说的是 coins，不是 clothes。 借用原文：some coins that are over 2,000 years old

optionsZh: 硬币收藏。
原始工具。
古代饰品。
有两千年历史的服装。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about the old city centre?
questions.stemZh: 关于老城区，女士说了些什么？
questions.answerText: It is charming with narrow but beautiful streets.

explain.定位: The streets are narrow but beautiful with plenty of charm. 街道狭窄但很美，充满了魅力。
explain.信号: 直接描述 + but 强调 beautiful/charm。女士用 narrow but beautiful with plenty of charm 直接描述 old city centre 的街道，but 后的 beautiful 与 charm 是评价重心。
explain.替换: The streets are narrow but beautiful with plenty of charm ↔ It is charming with narrow but beautiful streets. charm→charming，同词保留 narrow but beautiful
explain.排除: B) 张冠李戴 It attracts visitors from every corner of the world. 盗用 it's like the whole world is here on holiday，但这是对整个城市旺季的感受，不是 old city centre 本身。 借用原文：it's like the whole world is here on holiday C) 原词陷阱 It has flowers displayed around the Trevi Fountain. 盗用 with flowers，但 flowers 是 在 Spanish steps 的台阶上，不是 Trevi Fountain 周围。 借用原文：with flowers that go up to a church D) 过度推断 It is more attractive than the pictures in guidebooks. 中的 guidebooks 出现在 in all the guidebooks，但女士只说 Trevi Fountain 上了 guidebooks，并未比较吸引力。 借用原文：in all the guidebooks

optionsZh: 这里虽然街道狭窄，但很迷人美丽。
它吸引着来自世界各地的游客。
特莱维喷泉周围摆放着鲜花。
它比旅游指南中的图片更有吸引力。
options: It is charming with narrow but beautiful streets.
It attracts visitors from every corner of the world.
It has flowers displayed around the Trevi Fountain.
It is more attractive than the pictures in guidebooks.

questions.stem: What does the man say about the square with the Spanish steps?
questions.stemZh: 关于西班牙阶梯所在的广场，男士说了些什么？
questions.answerText: It is very famous and pretty.

explain.定位: It's a square where on one side, there are some very wide steps with flowers that go up to a church. It's also in all the tourist guidebooks. It's very famous and pretty. 这是一个广场，其中一侧有非常宽阔、饰满鲜花的台阶通向一座教堂。它也在所有旅游指南 里。它非常有名而且漂亮。
explain.信号: 连续介绍后 famous/pretty 给出评价。男士先说明 square 的物理特征，再用 It's very famous and pretty. 给出总体评价，这是问题的直接回答。
explain.替换: It's very famous and pretty. ↔It is very famous and pretty. It's → It is 缩写展开，形容词原词保留
explain.排除: A) 未提及录音提到 wide steps with flowers，完全没有 wild grass。 C) 与原文相反 It is located away from an old church. 与 steps with flowers that go up to a church 相 反。 借用原文：steps with flowers that go up to a church D) 原词陷阱 It is surrounded by Spanish-style houses. 盗用 Spanish 一词，但原文只说 square with the Spanish steps，未提 surrounding houses。 借用原文：visiting the square with the Spanish steps

optionsZh: 广场上长满了野草。
它非常著名，也很漂亮。
它远离一座古老的教堂。
它周围环绕着西班牙风格的房屋。
options: It is covered with wild grass.
It is very famous and pretty.
It is located away from an old church.
It is surrounded by Spanish-style houses.

questions.stem: What does the woman say she is going to do first?
questions.stemZh: 她说她打算先做什么？
questions.answerText: Ask Kathy if she'd like to see the square.

explain.定位: Let me ask her first, but I'm sure she'll be up for it. 让我先问问她，但我相信她会愿意的。
explain.信号: first 直接对应题干 first。女士用 Let me ask her first 明确动作的先后顺序，first 与题干 first 同词对应。
explain.替换: Let me ask her first ↔Ask Kathy if she'd like to see the square. ask her → Ask Kathy；语境指约她看 square
explain.排除: A) 答非所问 Ask Kathy what her plan is. 把 ask her 曲解为询问计划，但前文已计划去看 square，实 际问的是愿不愿意加入。 B) 偷换概念 Tell Kathy Mike will join them. 把 ask 偷换成 tell，且 Kathy 是否加入尚未确定，不能提 前告知。 D) 张冠李戴 Tell Kathy Mike would like to have a change. 盗用 Doing tourist stuff with others would be a welcome change，但这是 Mike 的想法，不是女士要 first 做的事。 借用原文：Doing tourist stuff with others would be a welcome change

optionsZh: 问凯茜有什么计划。
告诉凯茜迈克会加入他们。
问凯茜是否愿意去看看那个广场。
告诉凯茜迈克想换换环境。
options: Ask Kathy what her plan is.
Tell Kathy Mike will join them.
Ask Kathy if she'd like to see the square.
Tell Kathy Mike would like to have a change. Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What advice does the man want to get from the woman?
questions.stemZh: 男士想从女士那里得到什么建议？
questions.answerText: How to succeed in a new job.

explain.定位: Can you give me advice about being successful at a new job? I start mine next week. 你能给我一些关于在新工作中取得成功的建议吗？我下周开始新工作。
explain.信号: 开门见山的请求句。对话首句即以 Can you give me advice about… 直接提出求助，后接 I start mine next week 点明新工作背景，是整段对话的总起与问题来源。
explain.替换: being successful at a new job ↔How to succeed in a new job. 同义转写
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 How to fit into the bigger picture. 中的 bigger picture 确实在 P10 出现，但它是女士后 续建议的内容，不是男士最初想获得的建议。 借用原文：fits into the bigger picture B) 原词陷阱 How to get on with colleagues. 中的 colleagues 相关概念在 P3 出现，但那是男士表示 意识到同事重要性，并非他向女士寻求的核心建议。 借用原文：collaborate with my coworkers C) 张冠李戴 How to create a solid first impression. 几乎原样出现在 P2，但那是女士给的第一条建 议，不是男士主动求的建议。 借用原文：create a solid first impression

optionsZh: 如何融入更大的整体。
如何与同事相处。
如何树立良好的第一印象。
如何在新工作中取得成功。
options: How to fit into the bigger picture.
How to get on with colleagues.
How to create a solid first impression.
How to succeed in a new job.

questions.stem: What does the woman say is the most important thing for the man to do at first?
questions.stemZh: 女士说男士最初要做的最重要的事情是什么？
questions.answerText: Understand his role from various perspectives.

explain.定位: The most important thing for you to do at first is to understand your role from multiple perspectives. 你一开始要做的最重要的事，就是从多个角度理解你的角色。
explain.信号: 最高级 + 建议句。The most important thing…is to… 是典型的答案信号，直接给出女士 认为的最优先行动。
explain.替换: understand your role from multiple perspectives ↔ Understand his role from various perspectives. 同义词替换
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 Get familiar with all the details of his job description. 中的 job description 在 P6 原词 出现，但录音说的是 what you do is not just limited to your job description，即「不只 限于岗位描述」，恰恰否定了此项。 借用原文：job description B) 偷换概念 Learn about the relations within the organization. 对应 how your work relates to other people within the organization，但那是解释「为什么要多角度理解角色」的原 因，不是 the most important thing 本身。 借用原文：how your work relates to other people within the organization C) 未提及 录音中没有任何地方提到 limitations and weaknesses 或让男士认识自身弱点。

optionsZh: 熟悉工作说明中的所有细节。
了解组织内部的关系。
认识到自己的局限和弱点。
从不同角度理解自己的角色。
options: Get familiar with all the details of his job description.
Learn about the relations within the organization.
Recognize his own limitations and weaknesses.
Understand his role from various perspectives.

questions.stem: What does the man say he is feeling a bit uneasy about?
questions.stemZh: 男士说自己对什么感到有些不安？

explain.定位: I'm feeling a bit uneasy about meeting my boss as well. 我对去见我的老板也感到有点不安。
explain.信号: 情感表达 + about 对象。feeling a bit uneasy about meeting my boss 直接陈述男士的 情绪及其对象。
explain.替换: meeting my boss ↔Meeting his boss. 原词复现，人称转换
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 Learning history. 中的 history 在 P9 出现，但那是男士举例「了解公司历史」，并非他感 到不安的对象。 借用原文：history of the company C) 原词陷阱 Creating reports for other departments to use. 中的 reports 和 department 在 P7 出 现，但那是男士用来举例说明工作关联性，与不安情绪无关。 借用原文：reports that I create at the end of the month may be used by a team in another department D) 与原文相反 Leaving his coworkers in the present company. 中的 leaving 与录音中 collaborate with my coworkers 的「合作」态度相反，且录音未提及任何离职/离开含义。 借用原文：collaborate with my coworkers

optionsZh: 学习历史。
与老板见面。
为其他部门使用而制作报告。
离开现在公司的同事。
options: Creating reports for other departments to use.
Leaving his coworkers in the present company.

questions.stem: What does the woman suggest the man do to gain insight about the running of the business?
questions.stemZh: 女士建议男士怎样了解企业的运营情况？

explain.定位: However, it's crucial that you get to know the people who have decision-making authority to gain insight regarding how the business is run and decisions are made. 然而，你必须去认识那些有决策权的人，以便了解企业是如何运作、决策是如何做出的。
explain.信号: 建议句 + 目的状语。it's crucial that you get to know…to gain insight regarding… 中， 主句给出建议动作，不定式给出目的，正好对应题干 to gain insight about the running of the business。
explain.替换: get to know the people who have decision-making authority ↔Get to know the decision-makers. 名词化同义替换
explain.排除: B) 偷换概念 Acquire decision-making authority. 盗用 decision-making authority 原词，但原文说的 是「认识拥有决策权的人」，而非男士自己去「获取」决策权。 借用原文：people who have decision-making authority C) 原词陷阱 Promote its products and services. 中的 products and services 在 P10 出现，但那是 「了解公司业务」的内容，不是「了解企业运作与决策」的建议。 借用原文：products and services that the company exists to deliver D) 过度推断 Observe its overall management. 看似与 how the business is run 相关，但原文具体建 议是「认识决策者」，而非泛泛地「观察整体管理」。 借用原文：how the business is run and decisions are made Section C 1 Contrary to popular belief, consumers aren't as smart as they like to believe. Many consumers report comparing multiple competing brands and prices when evaluating a purchase. However, research indicates that this is not actually the case. What consumers really think or feel often contradicts what they say. A big reason is that they are driven by unconscious urges, the biggest of which is emotion. 与普遍看法相反，消费者并没有他们自认为的那么聪明。许多消费者表示，在评估一项购买时，他们会比 较多个相互竞争的品牌及其价格。然而，研究表明，实际情况并非如此。消费者真正的想法或感受往往与 他们所说的相矛盾。一个重要原因是，他们受到无意识冲动的驱使，其中最主要的就是情感。 2 Emotion is what really drives the purchasing behaviors, and also, decision making in general. Good marketers keep in mind this important fact all the time, and examples of emotion-based campaigns are everywhere. Think for a moment, what is actually being sold in most marketing campaigns? Luxury goods target our feelings of self-worth, acceptance, and status in the world. Communication devices Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard. excite us by offering a connection to friends, family and a broader network of people. And many other products, such as rings, target emotions related to love and relationships. 真正驱动购买行为的，是情感；一般而言，决策也是如此。优秀的营销人员始终牢记这一重要事实，而以 情感为基础的营销活动随处可见。请想一想，大多数营销活动实际上销售的是什么？奢侈品瞄准的是我们 关于自我价值、认同感以及社会地位的感受。通信设备通过提供与朋友、家人以及更广泛人际网络的联 系，使我们感到兴奋。许多其他产品，例如戒指，则瞄准与爱情和人际关系相关的情感。 3 As marketers, we should focus on the features of the product, but we must also sell the lifestyle and the feeling. The key is to highlight the emotional response a consumer will have by using the product. To achieve the highest emotional response, we should target our consumer through many different senses. A lot of what drives consumers is subconscious behavior. But this isn't a bad thing. There's nothing manipulative about helping consumers achieve desired states of emotion. 作为营销人员，我们应当关注产品的功能，但也必须销售一种生活方式和一种感受。关键在于突出消费者 使用产品后将产生的情感反应。为了达到最强烈的情感反应，我们应当通过许多不同的感官来触达消费 者。驱动消费者行为的诸多因素都属于潜意识行为。但这并不是一件坏事。帮助消费者获得期望的情感状 态，并没有任何操纵性。

optionsZh: 了解决策者。
获得决策权。
推广其产品和服务。
观察其整体管理情况。

questions.stem: What does research indicate about many consumers when they evaluate a purchase?
questions.stemZh: 关于许多消费者在评估一项购买时的情况，研究表明了什么？
questions.answerText: They do not compare competing brands and prices.

explain.定位: Many consumers report comparing multiple competing brands and prices when evaluating a purchase. However, research indicates that this is not actually the case. 许多消费者声称自己在评估购买时会比较多个竞争品牌和价格。然而，研究表明事实并非 如此。
explain.信号: 转折 however 否定前文自我报告。However, research indicates that this is not actually the case. 中的 however 把前一句消费者自我报告的内容推翻，research indicates 后的否 定才是答案所在。
explain.替换: research indicates that this is not actually the case ↔ They do not compare competing brands and prices. 否定前文的同义改写
explain.排除: A) 偷换概念 原文讨论的是消费者真实想法与所说之间的矛盾，并非'是否告诉营销人员感受'，选项把话 题偷换成 marketers。 C) 原词陷阱 They are not hesitant to contradict themselves. 盗用了原文 What consumers really think or feel often contradicts what they say. 中的 contradict，但原文是'所想/所感与所 说矛盾'，并非'毫不犹豫地自相矛盾'。 借用原文：What consumers really think or feel often contradicts what they say. D) 未提及 原文只说消费者被 unconscious urges / emotion 驱动，并未说他们'不确定自己喜欢买什 么'，属于根据常识编造的选项。

optionsZh: 他们不会告诉营销人员自己对某一产品的感受。
他们不会比较竞争品牌和价格。
他们毫不犹豫地自相矛盾。
他们不确定自己真正喜欢购买什么。
options: They do not tell marketers their feeling about a product.
They do not compare competing brands and prices.
They are not hesitant to contradict themselves.
They are not sure what they really like to buy.

questions.stem: What do good marketers keep in mind all the time?
questions.stemZh: 优秀的营销人员始终牢记什么？
questions.answerText: Consumers are actually driven by emotion.

explain.定位: Emotion is what really drives the purchasing behaviors, and also, decision making in general. Good marketers keep in mind this important fact all the time, and examples of emotion-based campaigns are everywhere. 情感才是真正驱动购买行为、乃至一般决策的东西。优秀的营销人员始终牢记这一重要事 实，基于情感的营销活动例子比比皆是。
explain.信号: 指代 this important fact 回指前句主旨。Good marketers keep in mind this important fact all the time 中的 this important fact 明确回指上一句 Emotion is what really drives the purchasing behaviors, and also, decision making in general.，答案就 在前一句。
explain.替换: Emotion is what really drives the purchasing behaviors, and also, decision making in general. ↔ Consumers are actually driven by emotion. 主动变被动，drive 同根转换
explain.排除: A) 未提及 原文提到 marketing campaigns 和各类产品，但从未说消费者'被新产品吸引'，属于无中 生有。 B) 原词陷阱 Consumers tend to make decisions on the spot. 盗用了原文 decision making in general 中的 decision，但原文讲的是'决策一般被情感驱动'，不是'当场做决定'。 借用原文：decision making in general C) 未提及 原文讲 emotion / unconscious urges 驱动消费者，但并未出现 temptation 或'难以抗拒 诱惑'的表述。

optionsZh: 消费者常常会被新产品吸引。
消费者往往会当场作出决定。
消费者觉得很难抵制诱惑。
消费者实际上是受情感驱动的。
options: Consumers are often attracted by new products.
Consumers tend to make decisions on the spot.
Consumers find it hard to resist temptation.
Consumers are actually driven by emotion.

questions.stem: What should marketers do besides stressing the features of a product?
questions.stemZh: 除了强调产品的特点外，营销人员还应该做什么？
questions.answerText: Highlight the emotional response it will trigger in the consumer.

explain.定位: As marketers, we should focus on the features of the product, but we must also sell the lifestyle and the feeling. The key is to highlight the emotional response a consumer will have by using the product. 作为营销人员，我们应该关注产品特性，但也必须推销生活方式和感觉。关键是突出消费者 使用产品后产生的情感反应。
explain.信号: but / also 补充 + The key is to 强调。but we must also sell the lifestyle and the feeling 先补充应做之事，随后 The key is to highlight the emotional response... 用 The key is to 进一步强调核心动作，答案落在这里。
explain.替换: highlight the emotional response a consumer will have by using the product ↔ Highlight the emotional response it will trigger in the consumer. 同义替换：have by using → trigger in
explain.排除: A) Draw consumers' attention to the luxury goods symbolizing quality life. 盗用原文 Luxury goods target our feelings of self-worth, acceptance, and status in the world. 中的 luxury goods，但该句只是论证情感营销的例子，不是题干问的'除了 features 还应该 做什么'。 借用原文：Luxury goods target our feelings of self-worth, acceptance, and status in the world. B) 原词陷阱 Leave consumers the impression they are doing nothing manipulative. 盗用原文 There's nothing manipulative about helping consumers achieve desired states of emotion. 中的 manipulative，但原文是在为情感营销辩护，不是把它作为营销人员'应该做 的事'。 借用原文：There's nothing manipulative about helping consumers achieve desired states of emotion. D) Remind consumers of the wide connections it can help to build. 盗用原文 Communication devices excite us by offering a connection to friends, family and a broader network of people. 中的 connection / broader network，但这只是 communication devices 的例子，不是营销人员的总体做法。 借用原文：Communication devices excite us by offering a connection to friends, family and a broader network of people. 1 Plastics have for years been used to make nearly everything that surrounds us. But along the way, they escaped the confines of packaging and objects and settled in the environment, the food we eat and the air we breathe. 多年来，塑料一直被用于制造我们周围几乎所有的东西。但在这一过程中，它们逃离了包装和物品的束 缚，进入了环境、我们所吃的食物以及所呼吸的空气中。 2 Americans are consuming and breathing in a lot of plastic. Based on available data, Americans take in an estimated 74,000 to 121,000 microplastic particles every year. However, scientists believe the true number is probably much higher, because for some likely sources of microplastics, there were no strong data available. 美国人正在摄入并吸入大量塑料。根据现有数据估算，美国人每年摄入的微塑料颗粒数量在7.4万至12.1 万之间。然而，科学家认为真实数量可能高得多，因为对于一些很可能的微塑料来源，目前没有可靠的 数据。 3 Microplastics get into food and air in several ways. Many start off as part of larger plastic objects, which over time fragment into smaller and smaller pieces until they become tiny: 5 millimeters or less in Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard. diameter. They are breathed in or consumed by animals, and then become our food. The particles float through the air until people breathe them in. They also settle on the food that people eat. 微塑料通过多种方式进入食物和空气。许多微塑料最初是较大塑料物品的一部分，随着时间的推移逐渐碎 裂成越来越小的碎片，最终变得十分微小，直径仅为5毫米或更小。它们会被动物吸入或摄入，随后成为 我们的食物。这些颗粒漂浮在空气中，直到人们将其吸入。它们也会沉积在供人们食用的食物上。 4 Data shows that for Americans, air, bottled water and seafood were the biggest sources for breathed-in or consumed microplastics. Added sugars accounted for less, and salts, tap water and beer contributed minimal amounts. These estimates are conservative. The included foods only make up about 15% of the average American diet. It's not yet known how much plastic is contained in the remaining 85% of the typical diet. 数据显示，对于美国人来说，空气、瓶装水和海鲜是吸入或摄入微塑料的最大来源。添加糖所占比例较 小，而盐、自来水和啤酒所贡献的数量极少。这些估算是保守的。所纳入的食物仅约占美国人平均饮食的 15%。典型饮食中剩余的85%含有多少塑料，目前尚不清楚。

optionsZh: 将消费者的注意力吸引到象征高品质生活的奢侈品上。
让消费者觉得他们没有在进行任何操纵。
强调产品将引发消费者的情感反应。
提醒消费者产品可以帮助建立广泛的人际联系。
options: Draw consumers' attention to the luxury goods symbolizing quality life.
Leave consumers the impression they are doing nothing manipulative.
Highlight the emotional response it will trigger in the consumer.
Remind consumers of the wide connections it can help to build.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about Americans?
questions.stemZh: 这篇文章说美国人什么情况？
questions.answerText: They are taking in a lot of plastic.

explain.定位: Americans are consuming and breathing in a lot of plastic. 美国人正在摄入并吸入大量塑料。
explain.信号: 段首总领句。Americans are consuming and breathing in a lot of plastic. 是第二段首 句，开门见山给出美国人摄入塑料的结论。
explain.替换: Americans are consuming and breathing in a lot of plastic ↔taking in a lot of plastic 同义概括
explain.排除: B) 原词陷阱 原文 they escaped the confines of packaging and objects and settled in the environment 说的是塑料 escape 到环境中，而不是美国人正在污染环境。 借用原文：they escaped the confines of packaging and objects and settled in the environment C) 未提及 短文只提到 food we eat、the average American diet，没有说美国人 consume much processed food。 D) 原词陷阱 原文 Plastics have for years been used to make nearly everything that surrounds us 的主语是 plastics，而不是 Americans。 借用原文：Plastics have for years been used to make nearly everything that surrounds us

optionsZh: 他们摄入了大量塑料。
他们正在污染环境。
他们食用大量加工食品。
他们用塑料制造一切东西。
options: They are taking in a lot of plastic.

questions.stem: What counted as the biggest sources for Americans breathing in or consuming microplastics?
questions.stemZh: 对于美国人吸入或摄入微塑料而言，哪些被认为是最大的来源？

explain.定位: Data shows that for Americans, air, bottled water and seafood were the biggest sources for breathed-in or consumed microplastics. 数据显示，对美国人而言，空气、瓶装水和海鲜是吸入或摄入微塑料的最大来源。
explain.信号: Data shows＋最高级 biggest。Data shows that for Americans, air, bottled water and seafood were the biggest sources for breathed-in or consumed microplastics. 中 Data shows 引出结论，biggest sources 直接对应题干的 biggest sources。
explain.替换: air, bottled water and seafood were the biggest sources for breathed-in or consumed microplastics ↔Air, bottled water and seafood 原词复现

questions.stem: Those that believed they fell claimed that the capitalists __(26)__ every ounce of surplus they could from the working class.

explain.词性槽: 主语 the capitalists 后缺谓语，宾语从句用过去时 → 过去式及物动词
explain.依据: squeeze...from... 压榨搭配，贴合"生活水平下降"一方的控诉 squeezed 填入得 the capitalists squeezed every ounce of surplus they could from the working class（资本家从工人阶级身上榨取每一盎司剩余）——squeeze...from... 是"从……中榨取"的固定搭配，空后的 from 正是它的信号。更关键的是语境：本句是"认为 生活水平下降"一方的观点，Those that believed they fell claimed that...，控诉资本家压 榨，squeezed 的负面感情色彩与控诉口吻完全一致。
explain.竞争词: C) earned 逻辑指向反：剩余价值是"榨"来的，不是资本家"挣"来的 earned（挣得）填入意为"资本家挣得每一分剩余"，把批判性的"压榨"说成了中性的"赚取"，且 earn 不接 from the working class；本句是批判资本家的观点句，需要带负面色彩的词， earned 色彩不符、搭配不通，双重出局。 I) increased 搭配不成立：increase 不接 from，且方向反 increased（增加）是经济类文章高频词，看见 surplus 容易顺手选它——这是本空最大的坑。 但 increase 从不与 from the working class 搭配；且"资本家增加剩余"是说资本家变富，与本 句"工人被压榨所以生活水平下降"的论证方向相反。它真正的位置在 28 题。 K) occurred 不及物：带不动宾语 surplus occurred（发生）是不及物动词，后面不能接宾语 every ounce of surplus；"资本家发生了剩 余"语法、语义双不通。它真正的位置在 29 题（this improvement occurred）。
explain.易错: 最具迷惑性的错误词是 I) —— increased 是经济文高频词，见 surplus 易顺手选。 increased（增加）词性对、话题贴，"资本家增加每一分剩余"初读也顺——但它不接 from the working class，且本句是"认为生活水平下降"一方的控诉（Those that believed they fell claimed that...），需要负面词。防坑口诀：先定本句褒贬，再查空后介词——from 锁 定 squeeze...from 搭配，squeezed 才是答案，increased 的真正归宿是 28 题。

questions.passage: One of the biggest controversies over the Industrial Revolution is how it affected the working class. The oldest debates were over whether the standards of living rose or fell. Those that believed they fell claimed that the capitalists (26)______  every ounce of surplus they could from the working class. Those that believed the standards of living rose claimed that the environment was consumer-friendly, with more and more goods  (27)______ to the working class every year. Today's historians agree that overall, the standards of living (28)______  . They do not agree, however, on when this improvement (29)______  . In an effort to solve this controversy, historians have attempted to define (30)______  what "standard of living" means. They all seem to agree that it should mean happiness, but happiness is impossible to measure. Instead, historians  (31)______ use "real income" as the measure for the standards of living. Real income is money  (32)______ and then adjusted according to the cost of living. However, it does not take into account unemployment, pollution, health, life expectancy, or free time. After  (33)______ debate and analysis of the average income, historians have agreed to disagree on whether there was rapid or slow economic growth during the Industrial Revolution. Instead, they have decided to  (34)______ how the Industrial Revolution was affected by other events. They have determined that the Industrial Revolution had an overall positive (35)______  , but it quite possibly was neutralized by negative events such as wars, high taxes, and rapid population growth.

questions.stem: with more and more goods __(27)__ to the working class every year

explain.词性槽: with+名词+补足语结构，空后是介词 to → 形容词
explain.依据: available to sb. 固定搭配，且呼应 consumer-friendly available 填入得 more and more goods available to the working class（越来越多商品 对工人阶级"可得"）——available to sb. 是四级核心搭配。句内更有铁证：前面说 the environment was consumer-friendly，"消费环境友好"正是"商品越来越买得到"，语义完 全咬合。
explain.竞争词: B) deteriorating 逻辑指向反：与 consumer-friendly 矛盾 deteriorating（恶化的）若填入，意为"越来越多恶化的商品流向工人"，与本句 consumer- friendly（对消费者友好）的正面语境直接冲突；且 deteriorate 是不及物义， deteriorating to the working class 搭配也不成立。 G) exhausting 搭配不当：exhausting 不接 to，也不修饰 goods exhausting（令人筋疲力尽的）修饰的是过程、工作、行程一类事物，说"令人疲惫的商品"不 通；它也没有 exhausting to sb. 的用法，空后的 to the working class 无法安顿。 L) peculiar 无中生有：全文无"奇怪"语义支撑 peculiar（奇怪的）填入意为"越来越多奇怪的商品"，文章通篇讨论生活水平升降，没有任何语 境支持"奇怪"这一评价；它属于命题人放的纯凑数形容词，靠"词性对"诱选。

questions.stem: Today's historians agree that overall, the standards of living __(28)__.

explain.词性槽: 宾语从句主语 the standards of living 后缺谓语 → 动词
explain.依据: increased 呼应下句 this improvement，定调"总体上升" increased 填入得 overall, the standards of living increased（总体上生活水平上升了）。 铁证在下一句：They do not agree, however, on when this improvement __(29)__.—— this improvement（这一改善）只能回指"上升"，若生活水平没升，improvement 一词无 从谈起。overall 也与首段论战whether the standards of living rose or fell呼应：当代史 学家给出的结论是 rose 一方。
explain.竞争词: C) earned 及物动词无宾语："生活水平挣得"不通 earned（挣得）是及物动词，必须带宾语（earn money），本空后无任何宾语；且"生活水 平"不能发出"挣"的动作。earned 的真正位置在 32 题 money earned。 K) occurred 语义不搭配："发生"的是改善，不是生活水平 occurred（发生）填入意为"生活水平发生了"，occurred 的主语应是事件（improvement、 change），"水平"无所谓发生；且下句 this improvement 表明本句已交代"上升"这一事实， occurred 无法提供这个前提。occurred 的真正位置在 29 题。

questions.stem: They do not agree, however, on when this improvement __(29)__.

explain.词性槽: 从句主语 this improvement 后缺谓语 → 动词（过去式）

questions.stem: historians have attempted to define __(30)__ what "standard of living" means.

explain.词性槽: 动词 define 与宾语从句之间 → 副词修饰 define
explain.依据: define exactly：精确界定，呼应下句"幸福无法测量" exactly 填入得 define exactly what "standard of living" means（精确定义"生活水平"的 含义）。下一句立刻给出理由：They all seem to agree that it should mean happiness, but happiness is impossible to measure.——正因为概念模糊难测，史学家才要努力把它 定义"精确"，exactly 与这段的语义走向严丝合缝。
explain.竞争词: M) probably 语义冲突：定义是确定性动作，不能"大概地定义" probably（大概、可能）表不确定，而 define（下定义）本身就是为了消除不确定——"试图大 概地定义"自相矛盾。本句语气是史学家主动的学术努力，不是猜测。 O) typically 方向不合：此处讲定义的精确度，不讲惯例 typically（通常地）强调"按惯例"，而本句焦点是 define 的程度（定义得多精确），"通常地定 义"答非所问。typically 真正的用武之地在下一空（31），它描述的是"史学家通常采用什么指 标"。两个副词空相邻，正是命题人故意设置的近位干扰。

questions.passage:
A) I was glad I had such terrible jetlag. Wide awake at 3:30 am with our nine-year-old daughter on our lodge balcony, I stared for hours at the most incredible night sky I've ever seen before the dawn slowly started to rub out the stars on the horizon and the multiple shooting stars faded away.
B) We were going to my wife's big family reunion in Auckland, New Zealand, but when we found out that Great Barrier Island, just off the coast, had been recently awarded Dark Sky Sanctuary status—a typically remote area that has an "exceptional or distinguished quality of starry nights"—we thought it would be the perfect place to relax before our busy schedule. It's the first island and only the fourth location in the world to achieve this status.
C) After a 28-hour flight with two travel-sick children, our hearts sank when we saw the tiny twin engine 10-seater that was to take us the 90km across the Hauraki Gulf to Great Barrier Island. But we needn't have worried. Whether it was the gravity force of the plane climbing or the noise of the engine, it put our three-year-old daughter instantly to sleep until we bumped down on the grass at Claris Airport. Our first empty sick bag against all the odds…Things were looking up.
D) Great Barrier Island has no public facilities and the 950 people living there (though only about half permanently) rely on solar and wind energy, and bottled gas for cooking. There are no streetlights. There are no cash machines or banks. The police force comprises a husband and wife, and there's one postman. It's not just the lack of light but the lack of noise that's so delightful on this unique and gorgeous scene. It was first discovered by East Polynesians about 700 years ago and the Maori name for the island is Aotea. Captain Cook gave the island its European name, because it acts as a barrier between the Pacific and the Hauraki Gulf.
E) The climate here is subtropical(亚热带的) like Auckland's. The island boasts a beautiful wilderness with dense forests, glorious, unspoilt sandy beaches and plenty of bays and a few mountainous areas where there are good walking tracks among the wetlands and valleys. You can birdwatch, dive, surf and boat. The best beaches are on the eastern side of the island where the surf is better, too. The sheltered western side is where you'll find the best diving and boating. Lots of people come here for the fantastic fishing spots around the island. Like a lot of spots in New Zealand, there are whale- watching trips and you might just catch sight of sharks.
F) It's rare to find an island that really does feel undiscovered—but this is it. When one of my wife's relations, who comes here regularly, found out that we'd been there, he whispered to us, only half- joking: "Shh—don't tell anyone!" The locals are a relaxed and friendly bunch—a lot of them told us that it's like what Waiheke Island (now in effect a suburb of Auckland) was in the 1970s when it was a commune of artists and people wanting to escape the city.
G) Our guide for some of our stay was the inestimable Hilde Hoven, a Dark Sky ambassador who runs Good Heavens with Deborah Kilgallon and Orla Cumisky. They bring their Dobsonian telescope and beanbags (it's hard work staring up wide-eyed in wonder without neck support) and, our elder daughter was glad to hear, hot chocolate to wherever you are on the island. "It's odd but when the light readings were done," said Hilde, explaining how the island was awarded its special status, "they found there was more light pollution on the northern side coming from Fiji, which is about 3,000km away, than Auckland to the south. It's pretty dark!"
H) Beginning their astronomical PowerPoint demonstration using a green laser pointer, Hilde and Orla showed us the Messier 4 spherical cluster(星团) with white dwarf stars(白矮星), Saturn and its rings, the Southern Cross and the Milky Way, which stretched across the sky. Our daughter was especially taken with Hilde's narrating of the Maori myth of Māui's fish hook to explain the shape of Scorpius. In the fable, Māui hauled the North Island of New Zealand from the bottom of the ocean with his hook.
I) We stayed at Mount St Paul's Estate, a luxurious lodge run by the friendly Chris and Teara, both from Canada. Teara used to be a chef at the Langham in Auckland and so dinner, eaten around a huge circular table (made of one of the most ancient trees in the world), was every bit as mouth- watering as you'd expect. Eating pancakes on the balcony overlooking the unspoilt white sandy beach was a great way to start the day.
J) Another highlight was an hour-long walk to Kaitoke hot pools in the centre of the island, through wetlands and a forest, where we whiled away a good hour sitting in the pools shaded from the heat by layers of delicate umbrella-like plants.
K) We also loved visiting the potter(陶艺家) Sarah Harrison, who showed us round her studio at Shoal Bay harbour, and her many pots and jugs, plates and bowls and colourful mosaics(马赛克). In her work, she also uses a lot of materials found on the beach. Our elder daughter loved the gorgeous hidden pool at Medlands beach where the water is separated from the sea in a private rock pool. Other high points were the ancient pōhutukawa trees and the incredible views of Okiwi Basin and
L) Apparently the island council turned down famous musician Paul McCartney's application to buy a property at Great Barrier Island because of the unwelcome attention he would have brought. You can see why he wanted to come here; equally, the island knows exactly what kind of star watching it prefers.

Whether it was the gravity force of the plane climbing or the noise of the engine, it put our three-year-old daughter instantly to sleep until we bumped down on the grass at Claris Airport. Our first empty sick bag against all the odds…Things were looking up.
D) Great Barrier Island has no public facilities and the 950 people living there (though only about half permanently) rely on solar and wind energy, and bottled gas for cooking. There are no streetlights. There are no cash machines or banks. The police force comprises a husband and wife, and there's one postman. It's not just the lack of light but the lack of noise that's so delightful on this unique and gorgeous scene. It was first discovered by East Polynesians about 700 years ago and the Maori name for the island is Aotea. Captain Cook gave the island its European name, because it acts as a barrier between the Pacific and the Hauraki Gulf.
E) The climate here is subtropical(亚热带的) like Auckland's. The island boasts a beautiful wilderness with dense forests, glorious, unspoilt sandy beaches and plenty of bays and a few mountainous areas where there are good walking tracks among the wetlands and valleys. You can birdwatch, dive, surf and boat. The best beaches are on the eastern side of the island where the surf is better, too. The sheltered western side is where you'll find the best diving and boating. Lots of people come here for the fantastic fishing spots around the island. Like a lot of spots in New Zealand, there are whale- watching trips and you might just catch sight of sharks.
F) It's rare to find an island that really does feel undiscovered—but this is it. When one of my wife's relations, who comes here regularly, found out that we'd been there, he whispered to us, only half- joking: "Shh—don't tell anyone!" The locals are a relaxed and friendly bunch—a lot of them told us that it's like what Waiheke Island (now in effect a suburb of Auckland) was in the 1970s when it was a commune of artists and people wanting to escape the city.
G) Our guide for some of our stay was the inestimable Hilde Hoven, a Dark Sky ambassador who runs Good Heavens with Deborah Kilgallon and Orla Cumisky. They bring their Dobsonian telescope and beanbags (it's hard work staring up wide-eyed in wonder without neck support) and, our elder daughter was glad to hear, hot chocolate to wherever you are on the island. "It's odd but when the light readings were done," said Hilde, explaining how the island was awarded its special status, "they found there was more light pollution on the northern side coming from Fiji, which is about 3,000km away, than Auckland to the south. It's pretty dark!"

Our daughter was especially taken with Hilde's narrating of the Maori myth of Māui's fish hook to explain the shape of Scorpius. In the fable, Māui hauled the North Island of New Zealand from the bottom of the ocean with his hook.

Other high points were the ancient pōhutukawa trees and the incredible views of Okiwi Basin and
L) Apparently the island council turned down famous musician Paul McCartney's application to buy a property at Great Barrier Island because of the unwelcome attention he would have brought. questions.passage:
P1 Is organic food worth the higher price? It's the classic grocery store dilemma. On the one hand, your family dinner table deserves only the best. On the other hand, your wallet can only stretch so far.

P2 Whether or not to buy organic is a personal decision, said Mike von Massow, professor of Food Agriculture.

P3 Science won't give a clear-cut answer to the question of whether organic food is "better". There are often trade-offs( 权衡) and answers become less definitive depending on the product under consideration.

P4 One thing is definitive: Organic and conventionally grown food are equally nutritious. From a nutrition point of view, there is no difference between organic and traditionally grown products.

P5 Organic products don't necessarily have fewer pesticides(杀虫剂)—in fact, they may have more. There is also no big difference between organic and non-organic products from a food-safety perspective. Even organic growers use pesticides. Testing shows little if any pesticide remains on conventionally grown products.

P6 In fact, organic farmers often use larger quantities of pesticide because they can only use the natural variety of insect-killers. Chemical pesticides generally kill a much wider range of pests(害虫) than any single natural pesticide.

P7 The use of animal waste in organic agriculture can also be a factor in the spread of bacteria like E. coli and salmonella. Over the past 10 years, Canada has seen more food-safety recalls for organic products, proportionally, than for conventional products.

P8 On the whole, organic agriculture may have a smaller environmental footprint. That's mostly because the risk of groundwater contamination from organic farming is lower. Organic farmers never use neonics, the controversial pesticides that have been linked to shrinking bee populations worldwide.

P9 Traditional agriculture has been making "dramatic improvements" to reduce its impact on the environment.

P10 It isn't a black-and-white picture, though.

P11 Organic farming is much less efficient when it comes to land use, although yields vary considerably depending on the crop.

P12 On the other hand, advocates of organic farming argue yields and efficiency could be significantly improved if the food industry devoted as much research and money to organic farming as it does conventional agriculture.

questions.passage:
P1 It is still controversial whether we are fundamentally generous or selfish and whether these tendencies are shaped by our genes or environment.

P2 Some evidence points to humans being born cooperative. At later stages in life we routinely work together to reach goals and help out in times of need.

P3 Yet instances of selfish behavior are also plenty. One recent study tested people's willingness to set aside selfish interests to reach a greater good. It found that being selfish was more advantageous than cooperating. The benefit may be short-lived, however. Another study showed that players who cooperated did better in the long run.

P4 It seems that human nature supports both pro-social and selfish traits(特征). Genetic studies have made some progress toward identifying their biological roots. By comparing identical twins, who share nearly 100 percent of their genes, and non-identical twins, who share about half, researchers have found overwhelming evidence for genetic effects on behaviors. In these twin studies, identical and non-identical twins are asked, for example, to split a sum of money with a peer. Such studies often also rely on careful psychological assessments and DNA analysis.

P5 Other work highlights specific genes as key players. My colleagues and I recently identified a gene linked to altruistic(利他的) behavior and found that a particular variant of it was associated with more selfish behavior in preschoolers.

P6 According to evolutionary scientists, cooperative behavior may have evolved first among relatives to promote the continuation of their genetic line. As communities diversified, mutual support could have broadened to include individuals not linked by blood. Another possibility is that humans cooperate to gain some advantage, such as boosting reputation. Finally, evolutionary processes take place at the group level. Groups of highly cooperative individuals have higher chances of survival because they can work together to reach goals that are unattainable to less cooperative groups.

P7 Yet almost no behavior is entirely genetic, even among identical twins. Culture, schooling and parenting are important determinants of cooperation. Thus, the degree to which we act cooperatively or selfishly is unique to each individual and depends on a variety of genetic and environmental influences.

explain.选项: A) 以偏概全 A gene-related selfish behavior in preschool children.只截取了定位句后半句，忽略 了作者首先'identified a gene linked to altruistic behavior'这一核心对象。 B) 过度推断 Key factors that determine one's altruistic behavior.用复数'Key factors'和'determine'，把原文仅识别的一个基因及其关联上升为决定利他行为的多个 关键因素，过度推断。 C) ✓ 正确 identified a gene linked to altruistic(利他的) behavior ↔ A specific gene associated with altruistic behavior. a gene ↔A specific gene A specific gene associated with altruistic behavior.将'identified'转换 为'associated'，'a gene'具体化为'a specific gene'，其余成分一致。 D) 过度推断 Roles played by genes in shaping one's character.用'shaping one's character'替换 了原文'altruistic behavior'，并把范围扩大到'genes in shaping character'，属于上位 的过度泛化。 关于合作行为，进化科学家告诉了我们什么？ A) 它最初可能起源于有血缘关系的个体之间。 B) 它可能导致了群体的多样化。 C) 它有助于在有血缘关系的人之间建立关系。 D) 它保证实现原本无法实现的目标。

questions.passage:
P1 It is still controversial whether we are fundamentally generous or selfish and whether these tendencies are shaped by our genes or environment.

P2 Some evidence points to humans being born cooperative. At later stages in life we routinely work together to reach goals and help out in times of need.

P3 Yet instances of selfish behavior are also plenty. One recent study tested people's willingness to set aside selfish interests to reach a greater good. It found that being selfish was more advantageous than cooperating. The benefit may be short-lived, however. Another study showed that players who cooperated did better in the long run.

P4 It seems that human nature supports both pro-social and selfish traits(特征). Genetic studies have made some progress toward identifying their biological roots. By comparing identical twins, who share nearly 100 percent of their genes, and non-identical twins, who share about half, researchers have found overwhelming evidence for genetic effects on behaviors. In these twin studies, identical and non-identical twins are asked, for example, to split a sum of money with a peer. Such studies often also rely on careful psychological assessments and DNA analysis.

P5 Other work highlights specific genes as key players. My colleagues and I recently identified a gene linked to altruistic(利他的) behavior and found that a particular variant of it was associated with more selfish behavior in preschoolers.

P6 According to evolutionary scientists, cooperative behavior may have evolved first among relatives to promote the continuation of their genetic line. As communities diversified, mutual support could have broadened to include individuals not linked by blood. Another possibility is that humans cooperate to gain some advantage, such as boosting reputation. Finally, evolutionary processes take place at the group level. Groups of highly cooperative individuals have higher chances of survival because they can work together to reach goals that are unattainable to less cooperative groups.

P7 Yet almost no behavior is entirely genetic, even among identical twins. Culture, schooling and parenting are important determinants of cooperation. Thus, the degree to which we act cooperatively or selfishly is unique to each individual and depends on a variety of genetic and environmental influences.

writing.directions: Suppose it is proposed that university students should be required to participate in at least one research project. You are now to write a response by stating what you think of the proposal in terms of its necessity and practicality. You will have 30 minutes to write the response. You should write at least 120 words but not more than 180 words.
writing.model: Requiring university students to take part in at least one research project is a proposal worth supporting, provided it is implemented flexibly and students can choose topics that interest them. From my perspective, such a policy is both necessary and practical for most undergraduates. First, it is necessary because research experience bridges the gap between textbook knowledge and real-world problem solving. Through a well-designed project, students learn to ask meaningful questions, collect reliable data, and think critically. These abilities are essential for their future careers. Second, it is practical because universities already have laboratories, supervisors, and course projects in place. A single semester-long project can fit into the existing curriculum without placing too much burden on students. Therefore, I support the proposal. It helps students develop practical skills that lectures alone cannot provide, and its flexible design makes it achievable for most universities.
writing.modelZh: 【参考译文】要求大学生至少参与一项科研项目是一项值得支持的提案，前提是其能灵活实施，学生也能选择自己感兴趣的课题。在我看来，这项政策对大多数本科生而言既有必要又切实可行。首先，它很有必要，因为科研经历能够弥合课本知识与现实问题解决之间的鸿沟。通过一个设计良好的项目，学生学习提出有意义的问题、收集可靠的数据并进行批判性思考。这些能力对他们未来的职业生涯至关重要。其次，它也很可行，因为高校已经拥有实验室、指导教师和课程项目等资源。一个为期一学期的项目可以嵌入现有课程体系，不会给学生造成过重负担。因此，我支持这一提案。它帮助学生培养课堂讲授无法提供的实践技能，而灵活的设计也让大多数高校能够落实。【第 1 段】同义转述+明确立场。首句用 Requiring university students to take part in... 转述了提案内容，避免机械照抄；第二句用 both necessary and practical 直接点出两个论证维度。【第 2 段】分论点+例子支撑。用 First/Second 分别对应必要性与可行性，每个论点都给出具体理由

outline.text: 同义转述+明确立场。首句用 Requiring university students to take part in... 转述了提案内 容，避免机械照抄；第二句用 both necessary and practical 直接点出两个论证维度。
分论点+例子支撑。用 First/Second 分别对应必要性与可行性，每个论点都给出具体理由 （bridges the gap / universities already have...in place），并加入 well-designed project 等具体 场景。
重申立场并收束。用 Therefore 回扣开头立场，用 practical skills that lectures alone cannot provide 总结双重价值，避免提出新观点。

translation.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2.
translation.source: 中国有句老话："一日为师，终身为父"。在中国人的观念里，老师不仅传授知识，更教给学生做人的道理。在古代，学生初次见老师时要举行隆重的仪式，足见老师地位之高。为弘扬尊师的优良传统，中国从1985年开始将每年的9月10日定为教师节。在这一天，学生以各种方式表达对老师的敬意。尊师是中华民族的传统美德，在当今社会得到了发扬光大。
translation.reference: There is an old Chinese saying: "A teacher for a day is a father for a lifetime." In the eyes of Chinese people, teachers not only impart knowledge, but also teach students how to be a good person. In ancient times, students had to hold a grand ceremony when they met their teacher for the first time, which was enough to show the high status of teachers. To carry forward the fine tradition of respecting teachers, China has observed September 10 of each year as Teachers' Day since 1985. On this day, students express their respect for teachers in various ways. Respecting teachers is a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation, and it has been carried forward in today's society.

sentences.trunk: There is an old Chinese saying 引出谚语（主语策略：There be） 中国有句老话 不是说「中国拥有话」，而是说「（在中国）存在一句老话」——表存在，英文最地 道的骨架是 There be 句型：There is（谓语）an old Chinese saying（真主语）。冒号后的谚语 一日为师，终身为父 作为 saying 的内容直接接在后面。
sentences.downgrade: 引语整体作同位内容，无需拆解 一日为师，终身为父 是 saying 的具体内容，英文惯例是冒号后直接接引号原文，相当于同位语， 不需要另造从句。谚语本身内部「一日／终身」对仗，译成 A teacher for a day is a father for a lifetime，用 for a day / for a lifetime 两个介词短语保住对仗感，而不是逐字硬译 one day be teacher。
sentences.grammar: 时态 回指全篇基调用一般现在时：谚语是超越时间的常理，There is、is 都用现在时；千万不要因为 「老话」听起来古老就用过去时 There was——谚语讲道理永远用现在时。 冠词 saying 是可数名词单数且首次出现、非特指→前面加 an（old 元音开头）：an old Chinese saying；谚语内部 a teacher / a father 均为泛指「任何一个」，用不定冠词 a。 单复数 「一日为师，终身为父」讲的是任何一个个体的情形，a teacher、a father、a lifetime 都用单 数；考生易顺手写成 teachers/fathers 复数，反而破坏对仗。
sentences.target: There is an old Chinese saying: "A teacher for a day is a father for a lifetime." 2. 在中国人的观念里，老师不仅传授知识，更教给学生做人的道理。

sentences.trunk: teachers not only impart…but also teach…（主语策略：原句主语） 中文主语明确：老师不仅传授知识，更教给学生做人的道理 中做动作的是「老师」→主语 teachers（泛指教师这一类人，用复数）；核心动词有两个「传授」「教给」，由「不仅…… 更……」并列为共同谓语：not only impart knowledge, but also teach students…，宾语分别是 knowledge 和 students。
sentences.downgrade: 「在中国人的观念里」降为介词短语，「做人的道理」译为不定式短语 在中国人的观念里 是范围状语，降级为句首介词短语 In the eyes of Chinese people，不要另起 In Chinese people's concept is… 这种残句；做人的道理 是「教给学生」的内容，译成 how to be a good person（疑问词+不定式作宾语），比 the principles of being a person 更口语地道 且不易写错。
sentences.grammar: 时态 回指全篇基调用一般现在时：老师不仅传授知识 说的是教师这一角色的常态职责，impart / teach 用原形。 主谓一致 主语 teachers 为复数泛指，谓语 impart、teach 均用动词原形，不能加 -s；考生常受「老师」中 文无单复数影响，随手写成 the teacher imparts，与后文 students 复数搭配失衡。 单复数 「老师」「学生」都是泛指一类人→teachers、students 复数且不加 the（复数泛指表类别时前面 裸奔）；knowledge 是不可数名词，绝不能写成 knowledges。
sentences.target: In the eyes of Chinese people, teachers not only impart knowledge, but also teach students how to be a good person. 3. 在古代，学生初次见老师时要举行隆重的仪式，足见老师地位之高。

sentences.trunk: students had to hold a grand ceremony（主语策略：原句主语） 主干取自 学生初次见老师时要举行隆重的仪式：做动作的是「学生」→主语 students；核心动词 「举行」→谓语 hold（「要」表必须，译为情态化的 had to hold）；宾语 a grand ceremony。 后半句 足见老师地位之高 不另立主干，留给降级处理。
sentences.downgrade: 「初次见老师时」降为时间状语从句，「足见……」降为which非限定定语从句 「初次见老师时」→ when they met their teacher for the first time，作时间状语挂在主干后； 足见老师地位之高 是对整件事的评论，英文惯用 which 引导的非限定定语从句承接：which was enough to show the high status of teachers（which 指代前面整件事）。「地位之高」这个 「之」字结构不要硬译成 so high status，转写为名词短语 the high status of teachers 或宾语从 句 how high teachers' status was。
sentences.grammar: 时态 本句是全篇基调的第一处正当偏离：在古代 明确指过去，主从句都切一般过去时——had to hold、met、was enough to show。考生最易犯的错就是沿用上句的现在时 hold，时间词出现在 句首时必须警觉。 主谓一致 when 从句主语 they 指代 students，谓语 met 用过去式与主句一致；which 从句的 be 动词跟前 面整件事（单数概念）→用 was。 单复数与冠词 ceremony 可数，「一场隆重的仪式」→a grand ceremony；their teacher 指每个学生拜的那一 位老师，用单数即可；status 此处不可数，the high status 不加 -s。
sentences.target: In ancient times, students had to hold a grand ceremony when they met their teacher for the first time, which was enough to show the high status of teachers. 4. 为弘扬尊师的优良传统，中国从1985年开始将每年的9月10日定为教师节。

sentences.trunk: China has observed September 10 as Teachers' Day（主语策略：原句主语） 主干取自 中国从1985年开始将每年的9月10日定为教师节：动作发出者是「中国」→主语 China； 核心动作「（定为／把……当作节日来过）」→谓语 has observed（observe a day＝过某个纪念 日，可延续，配 since 1985）；宾语 September 10，as Teachers' Day 作宾语补足语。「每年 的」→ of each year 作后置定语。
sentences.downgrade: 「为弘扬……」降为不定式目的状语，「从1985年开始」降为since短语 为弘扬尊师的优良传统 表目的，降级为句首不定式 To carry forward the fine tradition of respecting teachers（「尊师」按全局词表统一用 respecting teachers，「弘扬」用 carry forward，比 promote 更贴「优良传统」）；从1985年开始 降级为句尾介词短语 since 1985， 不要译成 from 1985 began 这种中式结构。
sentences.grammar: 时态 从1985年开始＝从过去持续到现在→用现在完成时 has observed，这是全篇基调的第二处正当偏 离。注意动词必须可持续：observe／celebrate 年年重复成立；若用 designate（一次性指定） 就得改成 In 1985, China designated… 一般过去时，二者只能选一套，不能写成 has designated…since 1985。 主谓一致 主语 China 是单数国家名→助动词用 has，不是 have。 专有名词写法 教师节 按词表统一写 Teachers' Day：复数 teachers＋撇号，Day 大写；September 10 月份首 字母大写。这是阅卷一眼可见的拼写硬伤点。
sentences.target: To carry forward the fine tradition of respecting teachers, China has observed September 10 of each year as Teachers' Day since 1985. 5. 在这一天，学生以各种方式表达对老师的敬意。

sentences.trunk: students express their respect（主语策略：原句主语） 学生以各种方式表达对老师的敬意 主语明确是「学生」→students；核心动词「表达」 →express；宾语「敬意」→their respect（respect 表「敬意」时不可数）。这是典型的主谓宾简 单句骨架。
sentences.downgrade: 「在这一天」「以各种方式」都降为介词短语，「对老师的」用for引出 「在这一天」→ On this day 句首时间状语（自然回指上句的 Teachers' Day，衔接交给第三 步）；「以各种方式」→ in various ways 句尾方式状语；对老师的敬意 中「对……的敬意」英文 固定搭配 respect for teachers，用介词 for 引出对象，不要译成 to teachers' respect。
sentences.grammar: 时态 回指全篇基调用一般现在时：每年的教师节都如此，是反复发生的常态→express 用原形。 单复数 ways 前有 various（多种的）→必须用复数 ways；students、teachers 均为泛指复数；respect 表敬意不可数，不加 -s。 介词搭配 「以……方式」用 in（in various ways），不用 with；「对某人的敬意」用 respect for sb.；「在 这一天」用 On（具体某天用 on，不用 in）。介词是主体考生重灾区，每个介词都按固定搭配核对 一遍。
sentences.target: On this day, students express their respect for teachers in various ways. 6. 尊师是中华民族的传统美德，在当今社会得到了发扬光大。

sentences.trunk: Respecting teachers is a traditional virtue（主语策略：原句主语） 尊师是中华民族的传统美德 中「尊师」是动作短语作主语，英文动词不能直接作主语，要动名词化 →Respecting teachers（动名词短语作主语，视为单数）；谓语 is；表语 a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation（「中华民族」按词表统一译法）。
sentences.downgrade: 「得到了发扬光大」转为and并列分句的被动谓语，「在当今社会」降为介词短语 在当今社会得到了发扬光大 与前半句共享主语「尊师」，用 and it has been carried forward 承 接（it 指代 Respecting teachers，避免重复动名词短语）；「发扬光大」＝被弘扬光大，英文须 用被动 has been carried forward；「在当今社会」→ in today's society 句尾状语。
sentences.grammar: 时态 得到了发扬光大 中「得到了」表至今已实现的结果→用现在完成时 has been carried forward； 前半句「是美德」是永恒判断→is 用一般现在时，与全篇基调一致。一句之内两种时态各有依据， 不是随意切换。 语态 「发扬光大」的承受者是「尊师」→被动语态 has been carried forward；若写成 has carried forward 就变成「尊师弘扬了别人」，意思全反。 主谓一致 动名词短语 Respecting teachers 作主语视为单数→is、has；考生易被 teachers 复数带偏写成 are/have。 冠词 virtue 可数，「一种传统美德」→a traditional virtue；the Chinese nation 特指中华民族→加 the。
sentences.target: Respecting teachers is a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation, and it has been carried forward in today's society. 英语四级 2026年6月·第1套 · 全卷构成 Part I 写作 题目解析 → Part II 听力 题目解析 → Part Ⅲ Section A 完形填空（选词填空） 题目解析 → Part Ⅲ Section B 长篇阅读（信息匹配） 题目解析 → Part Ⅲ Section C (1) 阅读理解（四选一） 题目解析 → Part Ⅲ Section C (2) 阅读理解（四选一） 题目解析 → Part IV 汉译英（段落翻译） 本题

questions.stem: What does the news report say about Nancy Gifford?
questions.stemZh: 新闻报道对南希·吉福德作了什么说明？
questions.answerText: She was born months after the end of World War I.

explain.定位: Nancy Gifford was born months after the end of the First World War, and spent 102 years living in her three-bedroom house in the Somerset Village of Street. 南希·吉福德出生于第一次世界大战结束数月后，并在萨默塞特郡斯特里特村的一栋三居室房 屋里住了102年。
explain.信号: 首段人物定义句。新闻首段在抛出事件（104岁老妇卖房）后，用 Nancy Gifford was born months after the end of the First World War 给出人物关键身份信息，直接回应题 干所问。
explain.替换: Nancy Gifford was born months after the end of the First World War ↔ She was born months after the end of World War I. 同义替换：the First World War = World War I
explain.排除: B) 原词陷阱 原文说 the house she has lived in since she was two years old，并非一生都在此居住； She has been living in her house throughout her life. 把起点从两岁偷换为'一生'。 借用原文：the house she has lived in since she was two years old C) 过度推断 原文仅说 having lived in it through the Second World War，表示她经历了二战，但并 未说她 suffered a great deal；She suffered a great deal during the Second World War. 把'经历'强改为'遭受巨大痛苦'。 借用原文：having lived in it through the Second World War D) 偷换概念 原文说 Nancy Gifford 是 A 104-year-old woman，且 spent 102 years living in her three-bedroom house in the Somerset Village of Street；She is a 102-year-old woman living in Somerset Village. 把居住时长误植为年龄，同时把 Somerset Village of Street 简化为 Somerset Village。 借用原文：A 104-year-old woman

optionsZh: 她出生于第一次世界大战结束几个月后。
她一生都住在自己的房子里。
第二次世界大战期间，她遭受了巨大的痛苦。
她是一名居住在萨默塞特村的102岁女性。
options: She was born months after the end of World War I.
She has been living in her house throughout her life.
She suffered a great deal during the Second World War.
She is a 102-year-old woman living in Somerset Village.

questions.stem: Why is Mrs. Gifford selling the house?
questions.stemZh: 吉福德夫人为什么要出售这所房子？
questions.answerText: She is moving to a nursing home.

explain.定位: Mrs. Gifford is selling the house and moving to a nursing home in nearby Glastonbury because of her health. 吉福德夫人因为健康原因，正在出售房屋并搬到附近格拉斯顿伯里的一家养老院。
explain.信号: because of 因果信号。答案句以 because of her health 结尾，直接回答 Why；卖房与搬 去养老院是并列结果，健康才是原因。
explain.替换: Mrs. Gifford is selling the house and moving to a nursing home in nearby Glastonbury because of her health ↔She is moving to a nursing home. 因果同构：卖房是为搬去养老院
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 原文 According to the estate agent, the house was built in 1882... 只说明中介提供了房 屋信息，并未说 Mrs. Gifford 是被中介说服卖房；She has been persuaded by the estate agent. 把'中介存在'曲解为'被中介说服'。 借用原文：According to the estate agent B) 偷换概念 原文 because of her health 说明健康是原因，但并未说她 needs the money badly；She needs the money badly for her health. 把'因健康搬家'偷换成'因健康急需钱'。 借用原文：because of her health C) 与原文相反 原文说 moving to a nursing home in nearby Glastonbury，即她要搬去格拉斯顿伯里； She is leaving Glastonbury Village. 把'搬入附近格拉斯顿伯里'说成'离开格拉斯顿伯里'， 方向相反。 借用原文：moving to a nursing home in nearby Glastonbury 1 The navy rescued a man who survived 24 days floating in the sea on a boat by eating tomato sauce and vegetable powder. The man, 47, wrote the word "HELP" in English on the boat, which was key to his rescue. 海军救起了一名男子，他靠食用番茄酱和蔬菜粉，在一艘船上漂浮海上生存了24天。这名47岁的男子在 船上用英语写下了“HELP”一词，这对他的获救起到了关键作用。 2 The man told authorities that his experience began in December when currents swept the sailboat out to sea while he was making repairs. To survive, the man collected rainwater with a cloth. He had to constantly remove water from the boat to prevent it from sinking. He also tried to light a fire to send a distress signal without success. Finally, a plane passed by and he signaled with a mirror. He said the navy told him that he was spotted when the plane passed again. The sailboat was abandoned at sea when the man was picked up by a nearby merchant ship. He was found in good health but had lost weight. 这名男子告诉当局，他的遭遇始于12月，当时他正在维修帆船，洋流将帆船冲向了大海。为了生存，他用 一块布收集雨水。他不得不不断将船里的水排出去，以防船只沉没。他还试图生火发出求救信号，但没有 成功。最后，一架飞机经过时，他用镜子发出了信号。他说，海军告诉他，飞机再次经过时发现了他。这 名男子被附近的一艘商船救起时，帆船已被遗弃在海上。他被发现时身体状况良好，但体重有所下降。

optionsZh: 她被房地产经纪人说服了。
她因健康问题急需这笔钱。
她要离开格拉斯顿伯里村。
她要搬到养老院去。
options: She has been persuaded by the estate agent.
She needs the money badly for her health.
She is moving to a nursing home.

questions.stem: What does the news report say was key to the man's rescue? Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
questions.stemZh: 新闻报道说，什么是救出那名男子的关键？
questions.answerText: The word HELP written on the boat.

explain.定位: The man, 47, wrote the word "HELP" in English on the boat, which was key to his rescue. 这名47岁的男子在船身上用英文写下了"HELP"（救命）一词，而这正是他获救的关键。
explain.信号: 非限制性定语从句 'which was key to his rescue' 直接点题。which was key to his rescue 把前文的 'wrote the word "HELP" in English on the boat' 明确标注为获救关键， 是新闻中少见的显性答案标记。
explain.替换: wrote the word "HELP" in English on the boat ↔The word HELP written on the boat 动作名词化 + 核心信息保留
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 The navy's timely arrival 中的 navy 确实出现在录音中，但原文只说 The navy rescued a man，海军是执行救援的一方，而非 'key to his rescue' 所指的原因。 借用原文：The navy rescued a man B) 未提及 His rich sailing experience 中的 sailing experience 在整段录音中没有任何对应信息，属 于无中生有。 D) 原词陷阱 His use of a mirror to send a signal 中的 mirror 确实在 he signaled with a mirror 中出 现，但这是男子在飞机经过时的求救尝试；原文明确说 key 是 HELP，镜子只是另一条求生 手段。 借用原文：he signaled with a mirror

optionsZh: 海军及时赶到。
他丰富的航海经验。
船上写着“救命”二字。
他用镜子发出信号。
options: The word HELP written on the boat.
His use of a mirror to send a signal.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man when he was rescued?
questions.stemZh: 关于那名男子获救时的情况，我们了解到什么？

explain.定位: He was found in good health but had lost weight. 他被发现时身体状况良好，但体重减轻了。
explain.信号: 新闻结尾总结人物状态的收束句。He was found in good health 中的 was found 是被救 后的总结性动词，in good health 直接回应题干 'when he was rescued' 的状态询问。
explain.替换: in good health ↔He was in good condition 近义形容词替换
explain.排除: A) 偷换概念 He lost all consciousness 中的 lost 可能让考生联想到 had lost weight，但 weight 与 consciousness 是完全不同的概念，属于偷换概念。 借用原文：had lost weight C) 未提及 He was too distressed to pick himself up 中的 distressed 与 pick himself up 在录音中 均未出现，且与 'in good health' 的正面评价相反。 D) 原词陷阱 He entirely abandoned himself to despair 中的 abandoned 可能让考生联想到 The sailboat was abandoned at sea，但原文主语是 sailboat（船被遗弃），选项却把它改成 He abandoned himself（自暴自弃），且 despair 在录音中从未出现。 借用原文：The sailboat was abandoned at sea 1 The board of Denver public schools is set to close several elementary and middle schools to make up for a decreased budget caused by declining enrollment. The specific schools will be announced in the coming days, a district spokesperson said. 丹佛公立学校董事会将关闭数所小学和初中，以弥补因入学人数下降而减少的预算。学区发言人表示，具 体关闭的学校将在未来几天内公布。 2 The school board approved criteria to close schools with fewer than 215 students, as well as schools with fewer than 275 students and a projected decline in enrollment. In the next three years, the district expects to enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students, it said. "3,000 students may not seem like that many students, but to a budget where you're receiving per-pupil funding, that's about 36 million dollars," district spokesperson Scott Pribble said. "We know that there are impacts and it's heartbreaking and difficult work. But in order for the district to stay out of debt, it's a step that needs to be taken," he said. The district said the decreased budget means it cannot provide the same mental health supports, social and emotional services or specialized programming to schools with lower enrollment. 学校董事会批准了关闭学校的标准：学生人数少于215人的学校，以及学生人数少于275人且预计入学人 数还会下降的学校。学区表示，未来三年，预计小学和初中的学生人数将减少3,000人。学区发言人斯科 特·普里布尔说：“3,000名学生可能看起来并不算多，但对于一个按照学生人数获得拨款的预算来说，这大 约意味着3,600万美元。”他说：“我们知道这会带来影响，这项工作令人心碎，也十分艰难。但为了让学 区避免陷入债务，这是必须采取的一步。”学区表示，预算减少意味着无法再为入学人数较少的学校提供 同等水平的心理健康支持、社会与情感服务或专业课程。 Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.

optionsZh: 他完全失去了意识。
他的状况良好。
他因过度悲痛而无法站起身来。
他完全陷入了绝望。
options: He was too distressed to pick himself up.
He entirely abandoned himself to despair.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the elementary and middle schools to be closed in Denver?
questions.stemZh: 关于丹佛将要关闭的小学和初中，我们了解到什么？
questions.answerText: Their enrollment has been on a noticeable decline.

explain.定位: The board of Denver public schools is set to close several elementary and middle schools to make up for a decreased budget caused by declining enrollment. 丹佛公立学校董事会准备关闭几所中小学，以弥补因入学人数下降而造成的预算减少。
explain.信号: 因果信号 caused by。答案句中 caused by declining enrollment 直接给出关闭学校的 causal chain：预算减少 ← 入学下降 ← 学校关闭。
explain.替换: declining enrollment ↔Their enrollment has been on a noticeable decline. 同义替换 declining = on a noticeable decline
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 选项 A 说‘提供社会服务的努力被忽视’，但录音末句只说 cannot provide the same mental health supports, social and emotional services，是预算不足导致无法提供，并 非努力被忽视；social services 这个词录音确实念到了，但语义与选项不符。 借用原文：social and emotional services B) 未提及 选项 B 说学校被校董会批评，但录音中校董会是作出关闭决定的主体，并未出现 criticized 的语义，属于无中生有。 C) 选项 C 说学校采取各种措施争取资金，但录音讲的是‘因预算减少而关校’，没有提到学校主 动 steps to get more funding，属于无中生有。

optionsZh: 它们为提供社会服务所作的努力一直被忽视。
它们一直受到丹佛教育委员会的批评。
它们采取了各种措施来获得更多资金。
它们的入学人数一直在明显减少。
options: Their efforts to provide social services have been ignored.
They have been criticized by the Denver school board.
They have taken various steps to get more funding.
Their enrollment has been on a noticeable decline.

questions.stem: What does the Denver district expect to do in the next three years?
questions.stemZh: 丹佛学区预计在未来三年内会做什么？
questions.answerText: Enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students.

explain.定位: In the next three years, the district expects to enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students, it said. 该地区表示，在未来三年内，预计中小学入学人数将减少3000人。
explain.信号: 时间信号 + 数字信号。答案句中 In the next three years 与 expects to enroll 3,000 fewer 形成时间与数字的双重信号，直接对应题干。
explain.替换: enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students ↔ Enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students. 原词复现
explain.排除: A) 选项 A 说‘批准关闭标准’，但录音中 The school board approved criteria 用一般过去时， 表示已经批准，不是 expect to do 的未来动作。 借用原文：The school board approved criteria C) 答非所问 选项 C 说‘决定关闭哪些中小学’，但录音中 The specific schools will be announced in the coming days 指近期宣布，不是 in the next three years 的预期动作；属于答非所 问。 借用原文：The specific schools will be announced in the coming days D) 偷换概念 选项 D 说‘改变 per-pupil funding 政策’，但录音只是用 per-pupil funding 解释预算计算 方式，并未说要 alter policy，属于偷换概念。 借用原文：per-pupil funding

optionsZh: 批准在资金减少的情况下关闭学校的标准。
小学和初中的入学人数减少三千名。
决定关闭哪些小学和初中。
根据合理原则调整其按学生人数拨款的政策。
options: Approve criteria for closing schools with decreased funding.
Enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students.
Decide which elementary and middle schools to close.
Alter its per-pupil funding policy on a rational basis.

questions.stem: Why are some schools in Denver to be closed according to the district spokesperson?
questions.stemZh: 据学区发言人称，丹佛的一些学校为什么将被关闭？
questions.answerText: To keep the district free of debt.

explain.定位: "We know that there are impacts and it's heartbreaking and difficult work. But in order for the district to stay out of debt, it's a step that needs to be taken," he said. ‘我们知道这会带来影响，这是令人心碎且艰难的工作。但为了让学区不负债，这是必须采取 的一步，’他说。
explain.信号: 目的信号 in order for... to stay out of debt。发言人先用 But 转折，再用 in order for the district to stay out of debt 点明关闭学校的根本目的，答案落点在 stay out of debt。
explain.替换: stay out of debt ↔To keep the district free of debt. 同义替换 stay out of = keep... free of
explain.排除: A) 未提及 选项 A 说‘让学区保持竞争力’，但录音全文未出现 competitive / competition 等词，属于 无中生有。 B) 原词陷阱 选项 B 说‘避免对经济造成负面影响’，但录音中 there are impacts 是承认影响存在，并未 说 avoid negative impact on its economy；impact 原词出现，但语义被扭曲。 借用原文：there are impacts D) 原词陷阱 选项 D 说‘为了获得预期资金’，但录音讲的是预算减少、按 per-pupil funding 计算缺口， 关闭学校是为了 stay out of debt（减少支出/避免负债），而不是 obtain funding（获得 资金）；funding 原词出现，但目的被替换。 借用原文：decreased budget Section B 1 M: Good afternoon, Theatre Bookings International. My name's Philip. How may I help you today? M: 下午好，这里是国际剧院订票中心。我叫菲利普。今天有什么可以帮您的吗？ 2 W: Oh, good afternoon. My name's Helen. I've been trying to book tickets for the musical Cats in London on the evening of May the 28th, but I can't get the computer to accept my card payment. I've tried three times, but it just doesn't want to take it. W: 哦，下午好。我叫海伦。我一直想预订5月28日晚上在伦敦观看音乐剧《猫》的票，但电脑就是不接 受我的信用卡付款。我已经试了三次，可它就是不肯接受。 Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 3 M: That's OK, madam. I can book it and take the payment over the phone if that's not a problem for you. M: 没关系，女士。如果您不介意的话，我可以帮您预订，并通过电话收取票款。 4 W: That would be wonderful. I'm not very good with computers. My husband usually does all of these things, but he is in Italy on a business trip until next Thursday, and I know how quickly these things can sell out. W: 那太好了。我不太会用电脑。这些事情通常都是我丈夫处理的，但他要到下周四才结束在意大利的出 差，而我知道这些票很快就会售罄。 5 M: They do indeed, madam. Firstly, can you confirm that it's the performance of Cats on May the 28th at the Lion Theatre in London at 7:30 pm? M: 确实如此，女士。首先，您能确认一下，是5月28日晚上7点30分在伦敦狮子剧院上演的《猫》吗？ 6 W: Yes, that's the one, and I will need two tickets please, not too close to the front. W: 是的，就是那场。我需要两张票，谢谢，位置不要离前排太近。 7 M: Actually, all the tickets at the front are already sold out anyway. But I can offer you two upstairs near the middle. I assume that you don't want to be too high up. M: 实际上，前排的票已经全部售罄了。不过我可以给您安排楼上的两张票，位置靠近中间。我想您应该 不想坐得太高吧。 8 W: Oh, my goodness, no. I'm scared of heights, and you can never see anything if you are too high up anyway. W: 哦，天哪，当然不想。我恐高，而且坐得太高的话，反正什么也看不清。 9 M: No problem, madam. I'll reserve those for you now, and all we need after that is the details of your card number and your full name, and then we are done. M: 没问题，女士。我现在就为您预留那两个座位，之后我们只需要您的卡号和全名，办完这些就可 以了。

optionsZh: 使该学区能够保持竞争力。
避免对其经济造成负面影响。
使该学区不负债。
获得预期的资金。

To avoid a negative impact on its economy.
