questions.stem: Why does the woman call the man?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士为什么给这位男士打电话？
questions.answerText: To book tickets for a musical.

explain.定位: I've been trying to book tickets for the musical Cats in London on the evening of May the 28th, but I can't get the computer to accept my card payment. 我一直在尝试预订5月28日晚上伦敦音乐剧《猫》的门票，但电脑不接受我的银行卡支付。
explain.信号: 被问者直接说明来电目的。女士在第二段直接说 I've been trying to book tickets for the musical Cats，这是对话开头最典型的“说明来意”句型，答案落在此处。
explain.替换: book tickets for the musical Cats ↔To book tickets for a musical. 同义替换：具体剧名概括为 musical
explain.排除: B) 原词陷阱 选项 B 的 cats 盗用了录音原词 Cats，但录音中 Cats 是音乐剧名，不是宠物猫，更不存在 “询问猫的价格”。 借用原文：the musical Cats C) 张冠李戴 选项 C 的 London 和 afternoon 都是录音里出现的词（in London 与问候语 good afternoon），但录音说的是伦敦的演出，不是下午的航班，属于把地点词和时间词张冠李 戴。 借用原文：in London D) 原词陷阱 选项 D 的 computer 盗用了 the computer to accept my card payment，但女士说电脑 只是不接受支付，并没有说要修电脑，核心目的仍是订票。 借用原文：I can't get the computer to accept my card payment

optionsZh: 预订音乐剧的票。
询问猫的价格。
支付她下午飞往伦敦的航班费用。
维修她的个人电脑。
options: To book tickets for a musical.
To enquire about the price of cats.
To pay for her afternoon flight to London.
To have her personal computer repaired.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the woman's husband?
questions.stemZh: 关于这位女士的丈夫，我们了解到什么？
questions.answerText: He is away on a business trip.

explain.定位: My husband usually does all of these things, but he is in Italy on a business trip until next Thursday, and I know how quickly these things can sell out. 我丈夫通常做这些事，但他现在在意大利出差，要到下周四才回来，而且我知道这些票卖得 很快。
explain.信号: 转折 but 后出关键信息。女士说 My husband usually does all of these things, but...， 转折词 but 之后 usually 所暗示的“常规情况”被颠覆，真正要考的丈夫当前状态落在 but 后面。
explain.替换: he is in Italy on a business trip ↔He is away on a business trip. 同义替换：具体地点概括为 away
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 选项 A 的 Lion Theatre 盗用了 the Lion Theatre in London，但那是 Cats 演出的剧院， 与丈夫是否常去无关。 借用原文：the Lion Theatre in London B) 未提及选项 B 的 sell things well 在录音中没有对应表述，属于无中生有。 C) 张冠李戴 选项 C 的 computer 盗用了 the computer 与 I'm not very good with computers，但录 音只说女士自己不擅长电脑，并未说丈夫是电脑专家。 借用原文：I'm not very good with computers

optionsZh: 他经常去狮子剧院。
他知道如何很好地销售东西。
他是计算机科学专家。
他出差了。
options: He knows how to sell things well.
He is a computer science expert.
He is away on a business trip.

questions.stem: What does the man say about the tickets at the front?
questions.stemZh: 这位男士对前排的票说了什么？

explain.定位: Actually, all the tickets at the front are already sold out anyway. 其实，前排的票反正都已经卖完了。
explain.信号: Actually 引出事实修正。男士先用 But I can offer you two upstairs near the middle 给 出替代方案，随后用 actually 进一步说明原因——前排票已售罄，答案句就在 actually 之后。
explain.替换: all the tickets at the front are already sold out ↔They are no longer available. 同义替换：sold out = no longer available
explain.排除: A) 未提及选项 A 的 discount 在录音中没有对应信息，属于无中生有。 B) 与原文相反 选项 B 说“需求低”，但录音说 all the tickets at the front are already sold out，说明需求 很高，选项与原文相反。 借用原文：all the tickets at the front are already sold out anyway D) 未提及 选项 D 的 not too expensive 涉及价格评价，但录音中完全没有讨论票价高低。

optionsZh: 这些票打折出售。
这些票需求量很低。
这些票已经没有了。
这些票并不太贵。
options: They are sold at a discount.

questions.stem: What does the woman say she is scared of?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士说她害怕什么？

explain.定位: I'm scared of heights, and you can never see anything if you are too high up anyway. 我恐高，而且坐得太高的话根本什么都看不见。
explain.信号: 直接陈述 scared of。女士说 I'm scared of heights， scared of 是题目关键词的直接复 现，答案紧随其后。
explain.替换: I'm scared of heights ↔Heights. 原词复现
explain.排除: B) 未提及 选项 B 的 Circus 与音乐剧主题相近，但录音中没有提到马戏团，属于利用话题场制造的无 中生有干扰。 C) 偷换概念 选项 C 的 Wild animals 盗用了音乐剧名 Cats 给人的动物联想，但录音根本没有提到野生 动物。 借用原文：the musical Cats D) 未提及 选项 D 的 Dark nights 在录音中没有对应内容，属于常见恐惧意象的凭空设置。

optionsZh: 高处。
马戏团。
野生动物。
漆黑的夜晚。
options: Dark nights. 1 W: Hi, John, why haven't you answered my text messages lately?

questions.stem: Why hasn't the man answered the woman's text messages lately?
questions.stemZh: 男士最近为什么没有回复女士发来的短信？
questions.answerText: He has switched off his phone.

explain.定位: Oh, I didn't know you had sent any. I turned off my phone almost a week ago and haven't turned it back on since then. 哦，我不知道你发了短信。我大概一周前关掉了手机，之后就没再打开过。
explain.信号: 直接应答 + 关键动作。女人一开口就问为何没回短信，男人用 I turned off my phone almost a week ago and haven't turned it back on since then. 直接给出原因，这是对话 中被问者的核心应答句。
explain.替换: I turned off my phone almost a week ago and haven't turned it back on since then. ↔ He has switched off his phone. 同义词替换（turn off = switch off）
explain.排除: A) 未提及男人从未表达回复短信令他厌烦，属于无中生有。 C) 未提及 录音中男人说的是『我不知道你发了短信』和『关机』，没有提到没时间回短信。 D) 原词陷阱 录音说 I didn't know you had sent any.，是『不知道你发了短信』，选项 He doesn't know how to respond. 把不知对象偷换成『不知如何回应』。 借用原文：I didn't know you had sent any.

optionsZh: 他觉得回复短信很麻烦。
他已经关掉了手机。
他没有时间回复短信。
他不知道该如何回应。
options: He finds it bothersome to reply.
He has switched off his phone.
He hasn't got the time to text back.
He doesn't know how to respond.

questions.stem: What was the man shocked to realize after he downloaded the APP?
questions.stemZh: 男士下载应用程序后震惊地意识到了什么？
questions.answerText: His excessive use of the mobile phone.

explain.定位: Well, I downloaded an APP that recorded how much time I spent on my phone. And I was shocked to realize I was using my phone an average of 8 hours a day, and on my worst day, I used it for 12 hours. 嗯，我下载了一个记录手机使用时长的APP。我震惊地发现我平均每天用手机8小时，最多 的一天用了12小时。
explain.信号: 题干关键词原词复现 + 数据强调。男人的话里出现 shocked to realize，与题干 shocked to realize 原词呼应，后面 8 hours a day、12 hours 用具体数字凸显『使用过度』。
explain.替换: I was using my phone an average of 8 hours a day, and on my worst day, I used it for 12 hours. ↔ His excessive use of the mobile phone. 数字概括为『过度使用』 recorded how much time I spent on my phone ↔His excessive use of the mobile phone. 时间记录映射到使用强度
explain.排除: A) 张冠李戴 女人提到自己的朋友玩手机游戏『all day and into the night』，这说的是朋友，不是男人 的情况。 借用原文：he sometimes played them all day and into the night. B) 原词陷阱 女人问 Were you addicted to mobile phone games?，男人回答 No, my problem was I was spending too much time on social media...，选项 His addiction to mobile phone games. 直接盗用问句原词，却被明确否定。 借用原文：Were you addicted to mobile phone games? D) 未提及 录音只提到 social media / messaging / commenting，没有说 surfing the net，属于用 近义概念捏造。

optionsZh: 自己夜间睡眠不足。
自己沉迷于手机游戏。
自己过度使用手机。
自己上网的频率很高。
options: His lack of sufficient sleep at night.
His addiction to mobile phone games.
His excessive use of the mobile phone.
His high frequency of surfing the net.

questions.stem: What did the man spend much time doing with his phone?
questions.stemZh: 男士花了很多时间用手机做什么？
questions.answerText: Communicating with friends on social media.

explain.定位: No, my problem was I was spending too much time on social media, messaging friends and commenting on other people's posts. 不，我的问题是我花了太多时间在社交媒体上，给朋友发消息、评论别人的帖子。
explain.信号: 否定后的真正落点。女人先猜测是游戏，男人用 No, my problem was I was spending too much time on social media, messaging friends and commenting on other people's posts. 纠正并给出真实答案，否定词 No 后面才是考点。
explain.替换: spending too much time on social media, messaging friends ↔ Communicating with friends on social media. 动名词短语同义替换
explain.排除: A) 张冠李戴 选项 Shopping online and paying for his purchases. 来自女人说的 shopping online and paying for everything with my phone，不是男人的行为。 借用原文：shopping online and paying for everything with my phone. C) 未提及录音没有提到 exploring content / whatever to his liking。 D) 偷换概念 录音说 commenting on other people's posts，选项 Sharing and posting pictures and videos. 添加了 pictures and videos，并把 commenting 换成 sharing，属于偷换概念。 借用原文：commenting on other people's posts.

optionsZh: 网上购物并为所购商品付款。
在社交媒体上与朋友交流。
浏览自己喜欢的各种内容。
分享和发布图片及视频。
options: Shopping online and paying for his purchases.
Communicating with friends on social media.
Exploring whatever content to his liking.
Sharing and posting pictures and videos.

questions.stem: Why does the woman say she has to use her mobile phone?
questions.stemZh: 女士为什么说自己不得不使用手机？
questions.answerText: She needs to talk with her friends and family far away.

explain.定位: That's great for you, but my friends and family don't live in this city, so we can't see each other often, and I don't have any choice but to chat with them online. 这对你很好，但我的朋友和家人不住在这个城市，所以我们不能经常见面，我别无选择，只 能和他们在线聊天。
explain.信号: but 后的不得已理由。女人先肯定男人的做法，随即用 but my friends and family don't live in this city... I don't have any choice but to chat with them online 给出自己的难 处，but 与 have no choice but to 共同标出答案落点。
explain.替换: my friends and family don't live in this city, so we can't see each other often ↔ She needs to talk with her friends and family far away. 『不住同城』替换为『far away』 I don't have any choice but to chat with them online ↔ She needs to talk with her friends and family far away. 『不得不聊』对应『需要聊』
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 录音说 I don't have any choice but to chat with them online，是客观无奈；选项 She prefers chatting with others online to meeting them. 却说她更喜欢线上聊天，改变了 语义极性。 借用原文：I don't have any choice but to chat with them online. B) 张冠李戴 选项 There are few physical stores near where she lives. 借用了男人说的 I go to physical stores and pay in cash.，但说话人与话题都不属于女人。 借用原文：I go to physical stores and pay in cash. C) 答非所问 录音中女人提到的是 shopping online / paying for everything，没有提到 ordering meals online，且这也不是她必须使用手机的核心理由。 Section C 1 If U.S. workers want to switch jobs, they'd better do it now. Last year, job switchers earned far higher wage increases than those staying in their jobs. But the gap is now closing. A three-month moving average of annual wage increases from the Atlanta Federal Reserve Bank's Wage Tracker shows that U.S. job switchers got the highest wage increase last July, when the measure touched 8.5%. Since then, it has gone up and down, and has been going steadily down since November. The gap in wage gains between people who switched jobs and those who stayed in their jobs is now closing. On average, people who changed jobs have almost always gotten better pay raises than those who stayed. But in the past, the difference was usually around one percentage point. In July though, the gap widened to 2.6 percentage points. 如果美国工人想换工作，最好现在就行动。去年，跳槽者的工资涨幅远高于留在原岗位的人。但如今这一 差距正在缩小。亚特兰大联邦储备银行工资追踪器显示，美国跳槽者年度工资涨幅的三个月移动平均值在 去年7月达到最高，当时触及8.5%。此后，该指标有所起伏，并自11月以来持续下降。跳槽者与留在原岗 位者之间的工资涨幅差距如今正在缩小。平均而言，换过工作的人几乎总是比留在原岗位的人获得更高的 加薪幅度。但过去两者之间的差距通常约为一个百分点，而在7月，这一差距扩大到了2.6个百分点。 2 But now wage growth is slowing down for everyone, and job switchers are getting smaller wage bumps in their new jobs. At the moment, those who change jobs get an average 7.3% raise every year, while those who stay get a 5.4% raise. That suggests the demand for workers has reached, or is at least nearing, its peak. The labor market is likely cooling, because even a shortage of workers isn't Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard. overcoming the historic imbalance between employers and employees in the U.S. The volume of income that workers take home as a proportion of what the U.S. economy produces is still falling. 但现在每个人的工资增速都在放缓，跳槽者在新工作中获得的加薪幅度也越来越小。目前，换工作的人平 均每年加薪7.3%，而留在原岗位的人加薪5.4%。这表明，对工人的需求已经达到或至少接近峰值。劳动 力市场可能正在降温，因为即使存在工人短缺，也无法克服美国雇主与雇员之间历史性的失衡。工人带回 家的收入总额占美国经济产出的比例仍在下降。

optionsZh: 比起与他人见面，她更喜欢在网上与他人聊天。
她居住地附近几乎没有实体店。
网上订餐给她带来了极大的便利。
她需要和远方的朋友及家人交谈。
options: She prefers chatting with others online to meeting them.
There are few physical stores near where she lives.
Ordering meals online is a great convenience to her.
She needs to talk with her friends and family far away.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about the gap in wage gains between job switchers and those who stay in their jobs?
questions.stemZh: 这篇文章对换工作者与留在原岗位者工资涨幅之间的差距作何说明？

explain.定位: But the gap is now closing. 但这个差距现在正在缩小。
explain.信号: 转折 but 后直接给出结论。But the gap is now closing. 中 But 承接前一句“跳槽者去年工 资涨幅更高”，转折后才是当前真实趋势；后文又重复 The gap in wage gains between people who switched jobs and those who stayed in their jobs is now closing.，形成 强调。
explain.替换: the gap is now closing ↔It is now narrowing. 同义替换 closing = narrowing
explain.排除: B) 与原文相反录音说差距在 closing，而 It keeps increasing. 说持续扩大，正好相反。 C) 张冠李戴 录音提到过去差距通常约 one percentage point，七月扩大到 2.6 percentage points，但 这些都是铺垫；It has remained huge. 把过去某一时刻的较大差距偷换成“一直很大”，与 now closing 矛盾。 借用原文：In July though, the gap widened to 2.6 percentage points. D) 过度推断 closing 只表示“缩小”，不等于“完全消失”；It will soon disappear. 把趋势推向极端，录音 未提。

optionsZh: 如今正在缩小。
一直在扩大。
一直非常悬殊。
很快就会消失。

questions.stem: What do we learn about wage growth now?
questions.stemZh: 关于目前的工资增长，我们了解到什么？
questions.answerText: It is slowing down for everyone.

explain.定位: But now wage growth is slowing down for everyone, and job switchers are getting smaller wage bumps in their new jobs. 但现在所有人的工资增长都在放缓，跳槽者在新工作中获得的工资涨幅也变小了。
explain.信号: But now 时间转折 + for everyone 绝对化表述。But now wage growth is slowing down for everyone 中 But now 把话题拉回当下，for everyone 给出全称范围，是细节题 中最直接的答案信号。
explain.替换: wage growth is slowing down for everyone ↔It is slowing down for everyone. 原句复现
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 录音提到 7.3% 和 5.4%，而 It is fluctuating between 5-7%. 把这两个数字捏成一个 “5%-7% 之间波动”的说法，但录音说的是两类人各自的平均涨幅，并非整体在 5-7% 之间 波动。 借用原文：those who change jobs get an average 7.3% raise every year, while those who stay get a 5.4% raise. C) 与原文相反 录音说跳槽者 7.3%、留任者 5.4%，即跳槽者更快；It is faster for those who stay in their jobs. 把比较对象的关系说反了。 借用原文：those who change jobs get an average 7.3% raise every year, while those who stay get a 5.4% raise. D) 未提及 录音全文未出现 inflation 一词，It is inadequate for dealing with inflation. 是利用考生 常识（工资增长跑不赢通胀）编造的无中生有选项。

optionsZh: 在5%至7%之间波动。
对所有人来说都在放缓。
留在原岗位的人工资增长更快。
不足以应对通货膨胀。
options: It is slowing down for everyone.
It is faster for those who stay in their jobs.
It is inadequate for dealing with inflation.

questions.stem: What is the labor market likely doing according to the passage?
questions.stemZh: 根据文章，劳动力市场可能正在发生什么？

explain.定位: The labor market is likely cooling, because even a shortage of workers isn't overcoming the historic imbalance between employers and employees in the U.S. 劳动力市场可能在降温，因为即使工人短缺也无法扭转美国雇主与雇员之间长期存在的不 平衡。
explain.信号: 结论句 + because 因果解释。The labor market is likely cooling 位于段落中部，是作者 给出的判断；后接 because 解释原因，进一步确认该句为结论落点。
explain.替换: The labor market is likely cooling ↔Cooling. 原词复现
explain.排除: A) 与原文相反 录音说市场 likely cooling，Booming. 表示繁荣火热，方向完全相反；且录音提到 demand for workers has reached or is nearing its peak，暗示上升空间已尽。 借用原文：The labor market is likely cooling B) 偷换概念 录音说 cooling（降温），Stabilizing. 说稳定，是两个不同的状态；降温意味着从高点回 落，稳定则意味着保持不变。 C) 未提及 录音没有提到 labor market 在 struggling；文中说的是工资增长放缓、市场降温，这是周 期性描述，并非“ struggling（挣扎）”这种带有困难色彩的评价。

optionsZh: 蓬勃发展。
趋于稳定。
举步维艰。
降温。
questions._leakedNextScript: Highly processed foods—the kinds made with lots of sugar, fat and salt—make up as much as 60% of the average American diet. But a new study shows that their low price and convenience come at a cost to health. The study found that when people ate a highly processed diet, they consumed about 500 more calories per day than they did when they ate a less processed diet. They also gained two pounds over two weeks, even though both diets had the same amounts of nutrients, like sugar, fat, fiber and salt.

questions.stem: What does a new study show about highly processed foods?
questions.stemZh: 关于高度加工食品，一项新研究表明了什么？
questions.answerText: Their low price and convenience negatively impact health.

explain.定位: But a new study shows that their low price and convenience come at a cost to health. 但一项新研究表明，它们低廉的价格和便利是以健康为代价的。
explain.信号: 研究结论信号句。录音用 a new study shows that 引出结论，其后 their low price and convenience come at a cost to health 直接对应选项 D 的核心语义。
explain.替换: their low price and convenience come at a cost to health ↔ Their low price and convenience negatively impact health. 同义替换：以健康为代价=对健康有负面影响
explain.排除: A) 与原文相反 录音明确说 both diets had the same amounts of nutrients，即两种饮食营养成分相同； 选项 A 却说 smaller amounts of nutrients，与原文相反。 借用原文：both diets had the same amounts of nutrients B) 未提及 录音只提到 they consumed about 500 more calories per day，给出了具体数字，从未 说 contribution to calorie consumption is hard to determine。 C) 偷换概念 录音说 make up as much as 60% of the average American diet，而 nearly half 约等于 50%，数字被偷换；同时它用了 average American diet 这一原词来增强诱惑力。 借用原文：make up as much as 60% of the average American diet

optionsZh: 与未加工饮食相比，其中的营养成分含量更低。
它们对热量摄入的贡献难以确定。
它们约占美国人平均饮食的一半。
它们价格低廉且方便，这对健康有负面影响。
options: They have smaller amounts of nutrients than unprocessed diets.
Their contribution to calorie consumption is hard to determine.
They account for nearly half of the average American diet.
Their low price and convenience negatively impact health.

questions.stem: What are highly processed foods linked to, according to other research?
questions.stemZh: 根据其他研究，高度加工食品与什么有关？
questions.answerText: A higher risk of cancer and obesity.

explain.定位: It wasn't a shock to find highly processed foods weren't healthy; other research has linked them to a higher risk of cancer and obesity. 发现加工食品不健康并不令人惊讶；其他研究已把它们与更高的癌症和肥胖风险联系起来。
explain.信号: 其他研究关联句。录音中 other research has linked them to 是明显的考点信号，后面的 a higher risk of cancer and obesity 即为问题所问的关联内容。
explain.替换: a higher risk of cancer and obesity ↔A higher risk of cancer and obesity. 关键短语直接复现
explain.排除: A) 张冠李戴 录音先说 other research has linked them to a higher risk of cancer and obesity，随后 才讲新试验发现 'causes people to overeat'；选项 A 把 'overeating' 这个结果张冠李戴到 other research 上。 借用原文：causes people to overeat B) 与原文相反 录音 both diets had the same amounts of nutrients, like sugar, fat, fiber and salt 说明 营养成分含量相同，选项 B 却说 A lack of nutrients like fiber，与原文相反。 借用原文：both diets had the same amounts of nutrients, like sugar, fat, fiber and salt D) 偷换概念 录音 sugar, fat and salt didn't seem to be what caused people to overeat 表明糖、脂 肪、盐并非导致暴食的原因；选项 D 却说 'A greater intake of sugar and salt'，把原文的 否定/排除偷换成了肯定的健康风险关联。 借用原文：sugar, fat and salt didn't seem to be what caused people to overeat

optionsZh: 强烈的过量进食欲望。
缺乏纤维等营养素。
较高的癌症和肥胖风险。
摄入更多的糖和盐。
options: A lack of nutrients like fiber.
A higher risk of cancer and obesity.
A greater intake of sugar and salt.

questions.stem: What do people tend to do when eating highly processed foods?
questions.stemZh: 人们食用高度加工食品时往往会怎么做？

explain.定位: The study also found that, when eating a highly processed diet, people ate faster. 研究还发现，当人们吃高度加工的饮食时，他们吃得更快。
explain.信号: 研究发现的行为结果。录音用 The study also found that 引出另一项发现，其后 people ate faster 直接回答题干所问的行为。
explain.替换: people ate faster ↔Eat more quickly. 同义替换：ate faster = eat more quickly
explain.排除: B) 与原文相反 录音 you're not giving your guts enough time to signal to your brain that you've had enough calories and that you're full 说明大脑更晚收到饱腹信号；选项 B 说 Feel full sooner，与原文相反。 借用原文：you're not giving your guts enough time to signal to your brain that you've had enough calories and that you're full C) 偷换概念 录音 Highly processed food tends to be softer, which makes it easier to chew and swallow 只说更容易咀嚼吞咽，并未说人们会 chew thoroughly；恰恰相反，软食更可能 减少咀嚼。 借用原文：Highly processed food tends to be softer, which makes it easier to chew and swallow D) 偷换概念 录音 easier to chew and swallow 表示吞咽更容易、更快，而选项 D 'Swallow bit by bit' 暗示慢、分小口吞，语义相反。 借用原文：easier to chew and swallow 1 Women continue to spend more time than men taking care of children and doing chores around the house. This is generally attributed to backward thinking and conservative values. But new research shows that such differences could be linked to differences in the preferences of males and females. 女性照顾孩子和做家务的时间仍然多于男性。这通常被归因于落后的思想和保守的价值观。但新的研究表 明，这种差异可能与男性和女性偏好的不同有关。 2 The new study looked at how men and women were dividing work at home and why they divided it that way. In general, both men and women took more responsibility for tasks they liked. For example, men liked yard care and home maintenance more than women. They leaned toward wanting primary responsibility for such tasks. The researchers stated that differences in enjoyment of household and childcare tasks matched how men and women chose to split tasks. The researchers added that there was not a single childcare task that men liked more than women. Keep in mind, however, that, as with any research on group differences, there were large within-group differences. The study's authors concluded that differences in men's and women's time spent on childcare and household tasks do not mean dissatisfaction. The authors noted that previous research revealed gender differences in attitudes towards family and career. These differences appear as early as six years old. Girls that age already show more interest in helping and caring for others than boys do, and they already exhibit a greater orientation toward family versus career. 这项新研究考察了男性和女性如何分配家务，以及他们为何以这种方式分配。总的来说，男性和女性都会 对自己喜欢的任务承担更多责任。例如，男性比女性更喜欢庭院维护和房屋维修。他们更倾向于希望主要 负责此类任务。研究人员指出，男性和女性对家务及照顾孩子等任务的享受程度差异，与他们选择如何分 配任务相吻合。研究人员还补充说，没有一项照顾孩子的任务是男性比女性更喜欢的。不过需要注意的 是，与所有关于群体差异的研究一样，群体内部也存在很大的个体差异。该研究的作者得出结论，男性和 Questions 22 to 25 are based on the passage you have just heard. 女性在照顾孩子及处理家务上所花时间的差异，并不意味着他们对此感到不满。作者指出，先前的研究揭 示了男性和女性在家庭与事业态度方面存在差异。这些差异最早在六岁时就会出现。这个年龄的女孩已经 比男孩表现出更浓厚的帮助和照顾他人的兴趣，并且已经表现出相较于事业更偏向家庭的倾向。

optionsZh: 吃得更快。
更快产生饱腹感。
充分咀嚼。
一小口一小口地吞咽。

questions.stem: How do people generally account for differences between men and women in the amount of time spent on housework?
questions.stemZh: 人们通常如何解释男女在花费于家务上的时间方面存在的差异？
questions.answerText: By attributing them to conservative thinking.

explain.定位: Women continue to spend more time than men taking care of children and doing chores around the house. This is generally attributed to backward thinking and conservative values. But new research shows that such differences could be linked to differences in the preferences of males and females. 女性仍然比男性花更多时间照顾孩子和做家务。这通常被归因于落后思想和保守价值观。但 新研究表明，这种差异可能与男性和女性的偏好差异有关。
explain.信号: 观点对比结构。答案句藏在转折之前：前一句 This is generally attributed to backward thinking and conservative values. 给出'通常看法'，But new research shows that such differences could be linked to differences in the preferences of males and females. 引出转折后的新研究。题干问 generally，所以取 but 前的内容。
explain.替换: backward thinking and conservative values ↔conservative thinking. 同义概括 This is generally attributed to ↔By attributing them to conservative thinking. 结构改写
explain.排除: A) 偷换概念 A 项 By attributing them to current cultural influences. 把录音里的 conservative values 改头换面成'当代文化影响'，原文说的是'保守'而非'当代文化'，方向相反。 C) 未提及 C 项 In terms of new genetic findings. 中的 genetic 在原文完全没有出现，录音只提到 preferences，属于凭空捏造。 D) 原词陷阱 D 项 In terms of personal preferences. 确实是录音原词 preferences of males and females，但它属于 but 之后的新研究发现，不是题干问的'人们通常'的看法。看到原词就 想选是第一大陷阱。 借用原文：preferences of males and females

optionsZh: 将其归因于当今的文化影响。
将其归因于保守思想。
从新的遗传学发现的角度解释。
从个人偏好的角度解释。
options: By attributing them to current cultural influences.
By attributing them to conservative thinking.
In terms of new genetic findings.

questions.stem: What did men lean toward doing according to the new study?
questions.stemZh: 根据这项新研究，男性倾向于做什么？
questions.answerText: Performing household tasks that they enjoy.

explain.定位: In general, both men and women took more responsibility for tasks they liked. For example, men liked yard care and home maintenance more than women. They leaned toward wanting primary responsibility for such tasks. 总体而言，男性和女性都会对自己喜欢的任务承担更多责任。例如，男性比女性更喜欢庭院 护理和房屋维修。他们倾向于想要主要负责这类任务。
explain.信号: 研究结论+例证。答案信号是 In general, both men and women took more responsibility for tasks they liked. 这一研究总括句，随后用 men liked yard care and home maintenance more than women 举例支撑。
explain.替换: tasks they liked ↔Performing household tasks that they enjoy. 同义词替换 took more responsibility for ↔Performing household tasks that they enjoy. 动作概括
explain.排除: A) 未提及 A 项 Sharing with women the chores they see necessary. 中的 see necessary 在原文中 没有对应表述，属于无中生有。 B) 偷换概念 B 项 Dividing housework that is demanding for women. 把录音里'男女共同选择自己喜 欢的任务'改成了'对女性来说繁重的家务'，demanding 在原文没有依据。 D) 未提及 D 项 Doing tasks that are physically challenging. 看似能解释 yard care / home maintenance，但原文从未用 physically challenging 描述这些任务，考生若凭常识推断就 会掉坑。

optionsZh: 与女性分担他们认为必要的家务。
分担对女性来说要求较高的家务。
做他们喜欢的家务。
做体力上具有挑战性的家务。
options: Sharing with women the chores they see necessary.
Dividing housework that is demanding for women.
Performing household tasks that they enjoy.
Doing tasks that are physically challenging.

questions.stem: What should we keep in mind as regards any research on group differences?
questions.stemZh: 关于任何有关群体差异的研究，我们应牢记什么？

explain.定位: Keep in mind, however, that, as with any research on group differences, there were large within-group differences. 然而，请记住，正如任何关于群体差异的研究一样，群体内部也存在很大的差异。
explain.信号: 提醒信号词 keep in mind。答案句以 Keep in mind, however, 开头，直接对应题干 keep in mind，后面跟的就是注意事项。
explain.替换: large within-group differences ↔The large within-group differences. 原词复现 as with any research on group differences ↔The large within-group differences. 题干同义对应
explain.排除: B) 与原文相反 B 项 The great similarities across groups. 说'群体间高度相似'，而原文 large within- group differences 强调的是'群体内差异大'，方向相反。 借用原文：large within-group differences C) 未提及 C 项 The researchers' subjective biases. 中的 subjective biases 在原文没有提到，原文 强调的是群体内部差异，不是研究者偏见。 D) 过度推断 D 项 The noticeable overgeneralizations. 是对群体差异研究可能存在的问题的推断，但 原文只说 within-group differences 大，并未说这是 overgeneralization。

optionsZh: 群体内部存在的巨大差异。
不同群体之间存在的巨大相似性。
研究人员的主观偏见。
明显的过度概括。

questions.stem: What did previous research reveal about gender differences in attitudes toward family and career?
questions.stemZh: 以往的研究揭示了人们对家庭和职业的态度存在怎样的性别差异？
questions.answerText: They appear at an early age.

explain.定位: The authors noted that previous research revealed gender differences in attitudes towards family and career. These differences appear as early as six years old. 作者指出，先前的研究揭示了人们在家庭和职业态度上的性别差异。这些差异早在六岁时就 出现。
explain.信号: 研究结论句。答案信号是 previous research revealed，直接对应题干 previous research reveal；后一句 These differences appear as early as six years old. 给出具体特征。
explain.替换: appear as early as six years old ↔They appear at an early age. 概括改写
explain.排除: A) 过度推断 A 项 They seem to be universal. 把原文的性别差异推断为'普遍存在'，但原文只提到 six years old 就出现，并未说 universal。 B) 未提及 B 项 They impact people's whole life. 中的 whole life 在原文没有对应表述，原文只提到 六岁出现，未说影响一生。 C) 偷换概念 C 项 They shape one's role in society. 把 attitudes towards family and career 偷换成 role in society，扩大了概念范围。 Except for some changes in the toilet and wash area, much of the house remains the same. 第2段，第5句 句首介词短语表例外/范围 + 主系表主干是英语中极为常见的说明性句式，复用性很高。 The man told authorities that his experience began in December when currents swept the sailboat out to sea while he was making repairs. 第2段，第1句 主句带宾语从句且宾语从句中嵌套状语从句的结构，在四六级和考研阅读的叙事/新闻类长难句中 极其常见，具有很高的复用价值。 He said the navy told him that he was spotted when the plane passed again. 第2段，第6句 主句 + 转述宾语从句 + 被动 + 时间状语从句的组合属于高考与四六级阅读理解中极其高频出现的 经典嵌套句型。 The sailboat was abandoned at sea when the man was picked up by a nearby merchant ship. 第2段，第7句 “主句 + when引导的时间状语从句”且结合双被动结构，属于英语阅读与考试中极具代表性的基础 叙事句型。 What does the news report say was key to the man's rescue? 第3题题干 该句型属于非常典型的插入疑问句式（疑问词 + 助动词 + 主语 + 谓语动词 + 从句其余部分），在 四六级与考研真题阅读听力中高频出现，迁移价值极高。 He was too distressed to pick himself up. 第4题，C "too... to..." 是中学及四级考试中极为高频的常考句式，具有很高的迁移与复用价值。 The board of Denver public schools is set to close several elementary and middle schools to make up for a decreased budget caused by declining enrollment. 第1段，第1句 采用 "be set to do sth" 句型结合后置目的状语与分词修饰，属于阅读理解和新闻报道中极为高频 且规范的典型句式。 "We know that there are impacts and it's heartbreaking and difficult work. But in order for the district to stay out of debt, it's a step that needs to be taken," he said. 第2段，第4句 本句涵盖了 "there be" 存在句、主系表结构、目的状语短语、宾语从句及定语从句，成分丰富，非 常适合用于练习识别形式主语、复杂表语及非谓语修饰。 The district said the decreased budget means it cannot provide the same mental health supports, social and emotional services or specialized programming to schools with lower enrollment. 第2段，第5句 主句动词引出多层省略引导词的宾语从句是英语新闻报导和学术阅读中极高频出现的典型句式，方 法迁移价值极高。 They have taken various steps to get more funding. 第5题，C “主谓宾 + 不定式短语作目的状语”是英语写作与阅读中最基础、最频繁出现的典型句型之一，掌握 后迁移复用价值极高。 Why are some schools in Denver to be closed according to the district spokesperson? 第7题题干 特殊疑问句叠加 "be to be done" 计划被动结构是各类英语考试中高频出现的典型句式，掌握其主 干提取方法具有极高的可迁移性。 I've been trying to book tickets for the musical Cats in London on the evening of May the 28th, but I can't get the computer to accept my card payment. 第2段，第3句 句中的 "have been doing" 完成进行时表达以及 "get sth. to do sth." 复合宾语搭配均为四六级及各 类考试的高频常考句式，具备很强的迁移价值。 M: They do indeed, madam. 第5段，第1句 这是日常交际和对白中非常典型的简短强调回应句型。 Firstly, can you confirm that it's the performance of Cats on May the 28th at the Lion Theatre in London at 7:30 pm? 第5段，第2句 该句是日常沟通、信息确认及听力考试场景中极具代表性的高频句式，可复用性强。 M: Actually, all the tickets at the front are already sold out anyway. 第7段，第1句 句中“名词 + 介词短语作后置定语”以及“be + 过去分词”被动表达均属于各类英语考试听力与阅读中 最基础、高频的典型句式，迁移价值高。 I'm scared of heights, and you can never see anything if you are too high up anyway. 第8段，第2句 使用 and 连接并列句并在后句跟 if 条件从句是日常与考试中极常见的经典句式，高度典型且易于 复用。 I'll reserve those for you now, and all we need after that is the details of your card number and your full name, and then we are done. 第9段，第2句 “主句 + and + 主语（带定语从句）+ is + 表语 + and + 结果分句”是日常沟通与考试听说中高频出 现的典型复合表达。 I turned off my phone almost a week ago and haven't turned it back on since then. 第2段，第2句 “一般过去时交代动作 + 现在完成时交代影响/延续”是四六级与日常表达中极其常见的高频经典句 式，极具迁移价值。 W: Why would you do something like that, when our phones make our lives so much more convenient? 第3段，第1句 句子涵盖了疑问倒装、介词短语作后置定语以及使役动词 make 带宾语和宾语补足语等典型语法 点，非常适合句子成分划分练习。 M: Well, I downloaded an APP that recorded how much time I spent on my phone. 第4段，第1句 “主句 + 定语从句 + 宾语从句” 的层层修饰结构在四六级听力和阅读中极为常见，属于掌握后可高 度复用的经典句式。 M: No, my problem was I was spending too much time on social media, messaging friends and commenting on other people's posts. 第6段，第1句 “My problem was + 从句”是英语口语与真题写作、阅读中极其常见的句型，后接分词短语补充说 questions.passage: It may sound surprising, but people who are supersensitive to coffee's bitter taste actually drink more of it, a new study finds. This sensitivity isn't  (26)______ a matter of taste, either, but rather is influenced by a person's genetic makeup, the researchers said in the study. "You'd expect that people who are particularly sensitive to the bitter taste of caffeine would drink less coffee," said study senior researcher Marilyn Cornelis. "The  (27)______ results of our study suggest coffee consumers acquire a taste for or an ability to detect the bitterness of caffeine due to the learned positive (28)______  brought out by caffeine." Put another way, people who have a  (29)______ ability to taste the bitterness of coffee learn to associate "good things with it," Cornelis said. This finding is surprising, given that bitterness often serves as a warning mechanism to (30)______  people to spit out harmful substances, the scientists said. Researchers conducted the study to understand how genetics influences people's (31)______  of tea, coffee and alcohol which tend to taste bitter, said lead researcher Jue Sheng Ong. "While all bitter flavors may seem the same, we (32)______  the bitterness of Brussels sprouts(抱子甘 蓝), quinine(奎宁) and caffeine (33)______  ," Ong told Live Science. "The degree to which we find these flavors bitter is, in part, determined by your genes." People with the genes to taste the bitterness of green vegetables are more likely to prefer tea to coffee. In ,  (34)______ people who were more sensitive to quinine's bitter flavors and those found in green vegetables tended to (35)______  coffee.

questions.stem: The __(27)__ results of our study suggest coffee consumers acquire a taste for or an ability to detect the bitterness of caffeine

explain.词性槽: The 与名词 results 之间需形容词定语
explain.依据: 结果与预期“相反”：预期少喝，实际多喝 前一句刚给出预期 You'd expect that people who are particularly sensitive to the bitter taste of caffeine would drink less coffee（你以为敏感者会少喝），而首段事实是 actually drink more of it（实际多喝）——结果与预期正好相反，opposite results 精准 收口。
explain.竞争词: O) targeted “有针对性的结果”无中生有 targeted results 暗示研究“瞄准了”某个目标对象，上下文没有任何“靶向”信息，纯属看着高级就 选的干扰。
explain.易错: 最具迷惑性的错误词是 O) —— targeted 词性对、词形高级，最易顶替 opposite。The __(27)__ results of our study 填 targeted 读起来也顺，但全段是“预期少喝 would drink less coffee vs 实际多喝 actually drink more of it”的反转结构，答案必须落在 opposite 上。防坑：形容词空先找上下文的逻辑信号词（expect/actually/surprising），别被“高级 感”带走。

questions.stem: due to the learned positive __(28)__ brought out by caffeine

explain.词性槽: 形容词 positive 后需名词作中心词
explain.依据: positive reinforcement“积极强化”，解释“越敏感越爱喝”的心理机制 前半句说喝咖啡的人 acquire a taste for or an ability to detect the bitterness of caffeine（习得对苦味的喜爱），原因是咖啡因带来的习得性“积极强化”——心理学固定术 语 positive reinforcement，正对应下段 learn to associate "good things with it" 的“把 好东西与之挂钩”。
explain.竞争词: H) omission “积极遗漏”语义自相矛盾 positive omission 既不是固定搭配也不合逻辑，咖啡因“带来遗漏”无法解释人们为何学会喜欢 苦味。 K) prospect positive prospect 看似通顺但接不上机制 “积极前景”语法上能站住，但 prospect 指对将来的预期，而这里解释的是“咖啡因让人上瘾般喜 欢”的即时心理奖励机制，且 prospect 不会由咖啡因 brought out（带来）。
explain.易错: 最具迷惑性的错误词是 K) —— positive prospect 搭配感强，最易顶替 positive reinforcement。the learned positive __(28)__ brought out by caffeine 填 prospect 语 法无误，但“前景”是面向未来的预期，无法被咖啡因“带来”，也和下句 learn to associate "good things with it" 的强化机制脱节。防坑：遇到“形容词+空”疑似术语时，先想学科固 定搭配（positive reinforcement），再用下文的解释句验证。

"The  (27)______ results of our study suggest coffee consumers acquire a taste for or an ability to detect the bitterness of caffeine due to the learned positive (28)______  brought out by caffeine." Put another way, people who have a  (29)______ ability to taste the bitterness of coffee learn to associate "good things with it," Cornelis said. This finding is surprising, given that bitterness often serves as a warning mechanism to (30)______  people to spit out harmful substances, the scientists said. Researchers conducted the study to understand how genetics influences people's (31)______  of tea, coffee and alcohol which tend to taste bitter, said lead researcher Jue Sheng Ong. "While all bitter flavors may seem the same, we (32)______  the bitterness of Brussels sprouts(抱子甘 蓝), quinine(奎宁) and caffeine (33)______  ," Ong told Live Science. "The degree to which we find these flavors bitter is, in part, determined by your genes." People with the genes to taste the bitterness of green vegetables are more likely to prefer tea to coffee. questions.passage:
A) If this doesn't encourage you to squeeze in a workout today, nothing will: a new study from Sweden shows that women who were highly fit in mid-life were nearly 90% less likely to get dementia(失智) decades later.
B) After initial exercise tests in middle age, researchers followed the women for 44 years. Both groups lived just as long, but those who could ride an exercise bike at a fast rate for 6 minutes in the initial test had a much lower risk of dementia later on than those who couldn't complete the workout.
C) The study, published Wednesday in the journal Neurology, couldn't prove that exercise prevented dementia, and the findings aren't a surprise—it's long been known there's a correlation between exercise and decreased dementia risk—but the results were particularly dramatic. About 5% of the women with the highest peak workload—those who were able to bike the hardest over those 6 minutes—developed dementia, compared to 25% of those with medium fitness and 45% who weren't fit enough to finish the test, the study found. Overall, women who were highly fit compared to those who were moderately fit decreased their risk of dementia by 88%. The few highly fit women who did develop dementia became symptomatic at age 90 on average, 11 years later than the moderately fit.
D) "I'm very surprised that the finding was so strong," said Ingmar Skoog, the paper's senior author and a psychiatry(精神病学) professor at The University of Gothenburg in Sweden. "It really shows the importance of exercise."
E) Dementia, as defined in medical dictionaries, is a broad term that describes a loss of thinking ability, memory, attention, logical reasoning, and other mental abilities. These changes are severe enough to interfere with social or occupational functioning. Dementia isn't a disease. Instead, it's a group of symptoms caused by other conditions. It happens when the parts of your brain used for learning, memory, decision making, and language are damaged or diseased. About 5%-8% of adults over age 65 have some form of dementia. This percentage doubles every 5 years after 65. As many as half of people in their 80s have some form of dementia.
F) Dementia is not temporary confusion or forgetfulness that might result from an infection that heals without treatment. It can also come from an underlying(潜在的) illness or side effects of medications. Dementia typically gets worse over time. People with dementia have problems with thinking and remembering that affect their ability to manage their daily life.
G) Dementia is typically associated with declines in cognitive function. Yet researchers have found an association between dementia and declines in hearing and other basic sensory functions.
H) Though the study mentioned above was fairly small (only 191 women took the initial fitness test, which means it's hard to maintain statistical significance while breaking the group down into sub- categories of more or less fit), it does give us hope that dementia can be prevented or delayed through exercise in one's middle age.
I) Alzheimer's(阿尔茨海默症) and other dementias are believed to begin 15-20 years before symptoms even appear, so it makes sense that exercising in mid-life would affect the risk, Skoog said. Exercise alone is not likely to prevent Alzheimer's, but the study shows people are not helpless in the face of one of the most feared, costliest and common diseases of old age, he added. And the same activities that help prevent Alzheimer's—including avoiding smoking, getting adequate exercise and sleep and eating a healthy diet—also prevent heart disease, he said, making them even more worthwhile. "You can do something yourself to decrease your odds," Skoog said.
J) Maintaining a healthy lifestyle in mid-life, decades before disease sets in, makes sense, said David Knopman, a fellow of the American Academy of Neurology, who was not involved in the study. "I suspect it's a dose," said Knopman, also associate director of the Alzheimer's Disease Research Center at Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota. "Starting in late life is better than not starting at all, but starting in mid-life seems to offer a larger benefit."
K) Although it is not entirely clear why exercise helps put off or prevent Alzheimer's, Knopman said it's likely that exercise maintains good blood flow to the brain. "When the brain is healthier from a vascular(血管的) point of view, it can absorb more Alzheimer's pathogen(病原体) before people become symptomatic," he said.
L) The message isn't that everyone needs to run marathons in middle age, Knopman said, but a healthy lifestyle pays off.
M) This type of study can't say exactly what kind of exercise is best, or how much is needed—only a study that has a placebo(安慰剂) group and tracks people going forward can do that, said Keith Fargo, director of scientific programs and outreach at the non-profit Alzheimer's Association. "The literature has not yet settled on an amount or type of exercise that is going to be key, although the
N) Several lifestyle studies are getting underway soon, including one backed by the Alzheimer's Association called the US POINTER study, which will offer at-risk adults, ages 60-79, a series of lifestyle interventions(干预) to see if they impact Alzheimer's risk. That and other Alzheimer's-related studies are always looking for volunteers to participate, he said.
O) In the next three to five years, these studies should allow researchers to provide clearer recommendations for exercise and other lifestyle modifications that might reduce Alzheimer's risk, such as sleep, diet and social activities, Fargo said. But it's already quite clear that exercising at any point in life is better for your brain than not exercising at all, Fargo added.
P) "If you don't want to have dementia when you're 80, the time to start getting fit is now," he said. "It may not necessarily give you a longer life, but there's a compelling body of work that it will give you more good years."

P1 People who systematically underestimate themselves and their own performance suffer from the so-called Impostor Phenomenon. They think that any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance. Those people live in constant fear that their "deception" will be exposed.

P2 It is common for people to question their abilities now and again. A healthy amount of reflection and self-doubt can protect a person from acting impulsively. P3 Psychologists from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg examined the topic for the first time under real-life conditions. These results are also completely unrelated to age and gender.

P5 A permanent underestimation of one's own abilities is often accompanied by the fear that this supposed intellectual deception will be exposed sooner or later and that they will pay the price for this. The Impostor Phenomenon was first described in 1978 by US psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes. They observed that there is a particularly high number of successful women who do not think they are very intelligent. The Impostor Phenomenon is not defined as a mental illness. However, people who suffer from it show a higher vulnerability to depression.

questions.passage:
P1 Music is a universal language. In every culture and country, you will find music. It is vitally important across the globe and has the potential to bring people together in peace and harmony. One of my favorite experiences in music is seeing musicians from different cultures come together and perform as a group. When each culture brings its own unique qualities to the group, an entirely new sound is achieved. This can create extraordinary results. People can communicate with each other using music as the common language.

P2 One common musical thread between cultures is known as the pentatonic scale. It is astonishing how many cultures share this tool in approaching music. The pentatonic scale consists of five notes; "penta-" meaning 5, and "tonic" meaning tone or note. This scale can be found in music everywhere including that of Native Americans, Africans, and Asians. It is also found in popular music, blues, jazz, and rock. Using this five-note scale, musicians from around the globe have a medium through which they can relate, communicate, perform, and ultimately understand each other.

P3 Music is tied to specific perceptual(感知的), mental, and emotional faculties, including language (all societies put words to their songs), motor control (people in all societies dance), sound analysis (all musical systems have a distinct pitch and quality), and aesthetics(美感) (their tunes and rhythms are balanced between repetitiveness and chaos).

P4 There is no known society that existed without music. Although each culture has their own specific style and approach to music, you will find that the purposes behind music are very similar across the board. Music essentially serves to express or change emotions. It can cheer you up, sadden you, anger you or excite you. Music is often ceremonial: used in religion, ceremony, and celebration. Music can simply be recreational: entertaining, joyful and fun. Any way you have used music, it is almost certain that every other culture has used music in the very same way. And that is something that bonds all of us. We all share a deep love for music and it has the power to unite us.

questions.passage:
P1 Music is a universal language. In every culture and country, you will find music. It is vitally important across the globe and has the potential to bring people together in peace and harmony. One of my favorite experiences in music is seeing musicians from different cultures come together and perform as a group. When each culture brings its own unique qualities to the group, an entirely new sound is achieved. This can create extraordinary results. People can communicate with each other using music as the common language.

P2 One common musical thread between cultures is known as the pentatonic scale. It is astonishing how many cultures share this tool in approaching music. The pentatonic scale consists of five notes; "penta-" meaning 5, and "tonic" meaning tone or note. This scale can be found in music everywhere including that of Native Americans, Africans, and Asians. It is also found in popular music, blues, jazz, and rock. Using this five-note scale, musicians from around the globe have a medium through which they can relate, communicate, perform, and ultimately understand each other.

P3 Music is tied to specific perceptual(感知的), mental, and emotional faculties, including language (all societies put words to their songs), motor control (people in all societies dance), sound analysis (all musical systems have a distinct pitch and quality), and aesthetics(美感) (their tunes and rhythms are balanced between repetitiveness and chaos).

P4 There is no known society that existed without music. Although each culture has their own specific style and approach to music, you will find that the purposes behind music are very similar across the board. Music essentially serves to express or change emotions. It can cheer you up, sadden you, anger you or excite you. Music is often ceremonial: used in religion, ceremony, and celebration. Music can simply be recreational: entertaining, joyful and fun. Any way you have used music, it is almost certain that every other culture has used music in the very same way. And that is something that bonds all of us. We all share a deep love for music and it has the power to unite us.

writing.directions: Suppose your university newspaper is inviting submissions from the students for its coming edition on future applications of robots on campus. You are now to write an essay for submission. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but not more than 180 words.
writing.model: Robots are no longer figures from science fiction; in the near future, they are likely to become common helpers on university campuses. As the university newspaper invites students to imagine future applications of robots on campus, I believe intelligent machines will mainly reshape our campus life in three areas: library services, laboratory assistance, and daily guidance. First, in the library, robots could locate, fetch, and even deliver requested books to reading rooms, saving students valuable study time. Second, in science labs, robotic assistants might handle repetitive experiments or dangerous chemicals, allowing students to focus on analysis and innovation. Third, robots placed around the campus could provide real-time directions and campus information for visitors and freshmen, reducing confusion during busy periods. Of course, these technologies should serve people rather than replace human interaction. If universities introduce robots wisely, campus life will become more efficient, safe, and welcoming.
writing.modelZh: 【参考译文】机器人不再是科幻小说里的角色；在不久的将来，它们很可能成为大学校园里的常见帮手。校报邀请学生们畅想机器人在校园的未来应用，我认为智能机器主要将从三个方面重塑我们的校园生活：图书馆服务、实验室辅助和日常指引。首先，在图书馆里，机器人可以定位、取书，甚至把所需书籍送到阅览室，从而节省学生宝贵的学习时间。其次，在科学实验室中，机器人助手可以处理重复性实验或危险化学品，让学生专注于分析和创新。第三，放置在校园各处的机器人可以为访客和新生提供实时路线指引和校园信息，减少繁忙时段的混乱。当然，这些技术应该为人类服务，而不是取代人际互动。如果高校明智地引入机器人，校园生活将变得更高效、更安全、更友好。【第 1 段】引入趋势并亮中心。首句用 Robots are no longer figures from science fiction 引入趋势，

outline.text: 引入趋势并亮中心。首句用 Robots are no longer figures from science fiction 引入趋势， 第二句回扣题目中的 future applications of robots on campus，第三句用 I believe ... will mainly reshape ... in three areas 给出中心论点并预告三个分论点，落实了“引入+中心句”方法。

三点论证支撑中心。用 First/Second/Third 衔接图书馆、实验室、校园导览三个场景；每个 场景都说明机器人具体做什么（locate, fetch, deliver / handle repetitive experiments / provide real- time directions），并点出价值（saving time / allowing focus / reducing confusion），对应“主题句 +举例+价值句”的展开法。
限定态度并收束。先用 Of course 做限定，指出机器人应 serve people rather than replace human interaction，再用 If universities introduce robots wisely 给出条件性展望，避免结论空洞，落 实了“让步/限定+总结+展望”方法。

translation.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2.
translation.source: 餐桌礼仪 (dining etiquette) 是中华传统文化的重要组成部分，蕴含着热情有礼的待客之道。为了招待客人，主人会根据客人的口味和喜好准备丰富精致的菜肴。就餐座位的安排非常讲究，主人坐在正对大门的位置，在主人身边就座的是最重要的客人。进餐时，主人会不时地为客人添酒加菜。这种独特的餐桌礼仪已延续了数千年，对促进和谐的人际交往起到了重要的作用。
translation.reference: Dining etiquette is an important part of traditional Chinese culture, embodying the warm and courteous way of treating guests. To entertain guests, the host prepares rich and exquisite dishes according to their tastes and preferences. The seating arrangement is very particular: the host sits in the seat directly facing the gate, while the most important guest sits beside him. During the meal, he refills wine and adds more dishes for the guests from time to time. This unique dining etiquette has lasted for thousands of years and has played an important role in promoting harmonious interpersonal relationships.

sentences.trunk: 主干：Dining etiquette is an important part（主语策略：原句主语） 餐桌礼仪 (dining etiquette) 是中华传统文化的重要组成部分 是典型的「是」字判断句，中文主语 「餐桌礼仪」明确，直接译作 Dining etiquette 作主语，谓语用 is，宾语「重要组成部分」译 an important part of traditional Chinese culture。后半句「蕴含着…待客之道」是第二个动词，先 不抢谓语位置，留到降级处理。
sentences.downgrade: 「蕴含」降级为现在分词 embodying 蕴含着热情有礼的待客之道 是对前半句的补充说明，逻辑主语仍是餐桌礼仪，故译成现在分词短语 embodying the warm and courteous way of treating guests，用逗号挂在主干后作伴随补充； 「热情有礼」译定语 warm and courteous 修饰「待客之道」。这比 and embodies 更紧凑，也 比硬拆成两句更连贯。
sentences.grammar: 时态 回指全篇基调：介绍文化事实的客观判断句，is 用一般现在时，embodying 为分词不随时态变 化；依据见 餐桌礼仪 (dining etiquette) 是中华传统文化的重要组成部分。 冠词 「重要组成部分」是可数单数，译 an important part，important 以元音开头，不定冠词用 an 不用 a；漏冠词是主体考生最高频的扣分点之一。 主谓一致 主语 Dining etiquette 是单数概念，谓语用 is 不用 are；embodying 不受人称影响，无需纠结变 形。
sentences.target: Dining etiquette is an important part of traditional Chinese culture, embodying the warm and courteous way of treating guests. 2. 为了招待客人，主人会根据客人的口味和喜好准备丰富精致的菜肴。

sentences.trunk: 主干：the host prepares dishes（主语策略：原句主语） 主人会根据客人的口味和喜好准备丰富精致的菜肴 的核心动词是「准备」，发出者是「主人」，译 the host（泛指任何请客的主人，用 the 加单数表一类人），谓语 prepares，宾语「菜肴」译 dishes。「为了招待客人」与「根据客人的口味和喜好」都是修饰成分，不入主干。
sentences.downgrade: 目的前置句首，依据后置句尾 为了招待客人 表目的，译不定式 To entertain guests 放句首；根据客人的口味和喜好 表依据，译 介词短语 according to their tastes and preferences 放句尾；「丰富精致的」两个形容词直接前 置修饰 dishes：rich and exquisite dishes。整句形成「目的状语＋主谓宾＋依据状语」的英文 序，而不是照中文语序平铺。
sentences.grammar: 时态 「会」在此表一贯做法而非将来，回指全篇基调用一般现在时 prepares，不译 will prepare；判断 标准：去掉「会」句子仍成立且讲的是惯例→一般现在时。见 主人会根据客人的口味和喜好准备丰 富精致的菜肴。 单复数 「客人」泛指多位，用复数 guests；「口味和喜好」两样并列，tastes and preferences 都用复 数；dishes 用复数表多道菜。 类指表达 「主人」指任何请客的主人这一类人，英文用 the 加单数 the host 表类指；句中 their 指代 guests，别与 the host 混。
sentences.target: To entertain guests, the host prepares rich and exquisite dishes according to their tastes and preferences. 3. 就餐座位的安排非常讲究，主人坐在正对大门的位置，在主人身边就座的是最重要的客人。

sentences.trunk: 主干：The seating arrangement is very particular（主语策略：原句主语） 第一小句 就餐座位的安排非常讲究 自带主语「安排」，译 The seating arrangement，「讲究」 是形容词性谓语，译 is very particular。后两小句是对「讲究」的具体分说；其中 在主人身边就 座的是最重要的客人 是倒装句，须先还原成正装「最重要的客人在主人身边就座」，主语是 the most important guest，谓语 sits。
sentences.downgrade: 一句总起，冒号引出两句分说 三个小句是「总说讲究＋两句分说如何讲究」的关系。总起句 The seating arrangement is very particular 后用冒号引出分说：主人坐在正对大门的位置 译 the host sits in the seat directly facing the gate，「正对大门的」译 directly facing the gate 作 the seat 的后置定语；在主人身 边就座的是最重要的客人 还原后译 the most important guest sits beside the host，两句分说用 while 连接显出主人与客人的对照。
sentences.grammar: 时态 回指基调：描述座位安排的一贯规矩，sits 用一般现在时，见 主人坐在正对大门的位置。 冠词与最高级 「最重要的客人」是最高级，英文必须 the most important guest，the 不可省；「大门」特指宴 请场地的大门，用 the gate（中式宅院大门用 gate 比 door 贴切）。 单复数 「就餐座位的安排」译 the seating arrangement，seating 为动名词不可数；guest 此处指「最 重要的那一位」，用单数，与句2的 guests 不冲突。
sentences.target: The seating arrangement is very particular: the host sits in the seat directly facing the gate, while the most important guest sits beside the host. 4. 进餐时，主人会不时地为客人添酒加菜。

sentences.trunk: 主干：the host refills wine and adds dishes（主语策略：原句主语） 主人会不时地为客人添酒加菜 主语「主人」沿用 the host；「添酒加菜」是四字格，实含两个动 作，拆成并列谓语 refills wine and adds dishes（为客人续酒、添菜）。「进餐时」「不时地」 「为客人」都是状语，不入主干。
sentences.downgrade: 三个状语各归其位 进餐时 译 During the meal 放句首点明场景；「不时地」译固定短语 from time to time 放句 尾；「为客人」译 for the guests 紧跟谓语后。整句为「时间状语＋主谓宾＋对象＋频度状语」的 英文语序，不把三个状语都堆在动词前（那是中文语序）。
sentences.grammar: 时态 「会」表习惯做法，回指基调用一般现在时，与第2句的「会」同样处理；见 主人会不时地为客人 添酒加菜。 主谓一致 主语 the host 是第三人称单数，refills 与 adds 都要加 s；并列谓语两个动词都要随主语变形，漏 掉第二个 s 是高频失误。 短语搭配 「不时地」固定译 from time to time（time 前无冠词，也不用复数 times）；「进餐时」用 During the meal 而非 In the meal，介词 during 表「在…期间」。
sentences.target: During the meal, the host refills wine and adds more dishes for the guests from time to time. 5. 这种独特的餐桌礼仪已延续了数千年，对促进和谐的人际交往起到了重要的作用。

sentences.trunk: 主干：This unique dining etiquette has lasted（主语策略：原句主语） 这种独特的餐桌礼仪已延续了数千年 主语「这种独特的餐桌礼仪」译 This unique dining etiquette（This 承接上文，兼作衔接手段），核心动词「延续」译 has lasted。「对促进和谐的 人际交往起到了重要的作用」是第二个谓语性成分，作并列谓语处理。
sentences.downgrade: 「起到重要作用」作并列谓语 play a role in doing 对促进和谐的人际交往起到了重要的作用 与「延续」共用主语，译成并列谓语 and has played an important role in promoting harmonious interpersonal relationships：「对…起到重要作用」 用固定句型 play an important role in doing sth，「促进」降级为 in 后的动名词 promoting， 「和谐的人际交往」译 harmonious interpersonal relationships 作 promoting 的宾语。两个谓 语共享主语，不硬拆两句。
sentences.grammar: 时态 「已延续了数千年」动作从过去持续至今，用现在完成时 has lasted，配 for thousands of years；这是对全篇一般现在时基调的合理偏离，依据就是原文 已延续了数千年 的「已」与 「了」。 介词搭配 play a role in 的 in 是介词，后接 promoting 不用 promote；thousands of 表概数必须用复数 thousands 加 of（不说 thousand of）。 单复数与冠词 role 是可数单数，play an important role 的 an 不可漏（important 元音开头）；「人际交往」 译 relationships 用复数表泛指各类人际往来。
sentences.target: This unique dining etiquette has lasted for thousands of years and has played an important role in promoting harmonious interpersonal relationships. 英语四级 2026年6月·第2套 · 全卷构成 Part I 写作 题目解析 → Part II 听力 题目解析 → Part Ⅲ Section A 完形填空（选词填空） 题目解析 → Part Ⅲ Section B 长篇阅读（信息匹配） 题目解析 → Part Ⅲ Section C 阅读理解（四选一） 题目解析 → Part Ⅲ Section C (2) 阅读理解（四选一） 题目解析 → Part IV 汉译英（段落翻译） 本题
