questions.passage:
P1 Adults dream during REM (rapid eye movement) sleep and infants have loads of REM. So, it might be fair to assume that babies have tons of dreams.

P2 But scientists believe REM serves a completely different purpose for newborns and infants than dreaming. When babies are in REM, it allows their brain to develop pathways, connections, and eventually, learn languages.

P3 Since your baby doesn't dream at this stage of brain development, it's safe to assume babies do not have nightmares, either. Nightmares stem from exposure to trauma(创伤), an overactive imagination, and the normal stresses of everyday life.

P4 Are you wondering, what do babies dream about? Good question, but the answer is nothing! So, when do babies start dreaming? The general consensus is that they start dreaming around the age of two. Psychologist David Foulkes studies children (from very small kids to teens) to bring the secrets of their dreams to the light of day. In his lab, he lets kids fall asleep and then wakes them 3 times a night and asks them to describe what they recall.

P5 Foulkes' findings are unsurprising. Basically, little kids have little dreams. But exactly what kids see while dreaming depends on their age. As children develop and grow, their dreams do too.

P6 Dreams of very small kids are usually just snapshots(快照), looking much more like a slideshow than a movie, when compared to the dreams of adults. They heavily feature animals and other familiar sights, like images of people eating. According to Foulkes, "Children's dream life…seems to be similar to their waking imagination and narration." Kids ages 5 – 9 begin seeing moving images and characters in action. Dreams now include multiple events strung together, one after the other. They also start developing greater ability to remember dreams. Still, that's not always the case: When roused during REM sleep, 25% of the kids in Foulkes' studies had no recollection of dreaming, a trend that continues through age 9.

P7 So, if your baby seems to be in a stressful state while sleeping or is upset upon waking, there may be other factors at play.

它们反映儿童的清醒生活。

explain.判型: What are Foulkes' findings about kids' dreams? 直接问研究结论是什么，是细节题。
explain.拆句: Q54 结构是 "What are Foulkes' findings about kids' dreams?"，about kids' dreams 限定 findings 的范围，没有从句也没有否定，无陷阱。
explain.定位: Foulkes' findings are unsurprising. Basically, little kids have little dreams. But exactly what kids see while dreaming depends on their age. As children develop and grow, their dreams do too. Foulkes 的发现并不令人意外。本质上，小孩做的也是小梦。但孩子在梦中究竟看到什么， 取决于他们的年龄。随着孩子的发育成长，他们的梦也在发育成长。 54. What are Foulkes' findings about kids' dreams? A) They feature strange animals. B) They are unsurprising to adults. C) They grow and evolve with age. D) They reflect kids' waking life.
explain.选项: A) 以偏概全 They heavily feature animals and other familiar sights 只说幼儿梦多含动物等"熟悉 景象"，They feature strange animals 把动物拔成 "strange animals" 且当成所有孩子 梦的特征。 B) 答非所问 题问 findings 的内容；They are unsurprising to adults. 拿原文 "unsurprising" 的评 价词当做内容，Foulkes' findings are unsurprising 的 unsurprising 是对 "findings 本 身" 的评价，而非 findings 的实质内容。 C) ✓ 正确 As children develop and grow, their dreams do too ↔They grow and evolve with age. 预判 "梦随孩子发育而发育" 与 They grow and evolve with age. 完全对应，选 C。 D) 偷换概念 原文 Children's dream life…seems to be similar to their waking imagination and narration 的相似对象是 "清醒时的想象与叙事"，They reflect kids' waking life. 把 "想 象/叙事" 偷换成 "waking life"（清醒生活本身）。 关于醒来时看起来心烦意乱的婴儿,我们可以假设什么? A) 他们违背自己的意愿被唤醒了。 B) 他们被噩梦打扰了。 C) 他们难以回忆梦境的画面。 D) 他们受到了做梦以外的其他事物的影响。

questions.passage:
P1 Adults dream during REM (rapid eye movement) sleep and infants have loads of REM. So, it might be fair to assume that babies have tons of dreams.

P2 But scientists believe REM serves a completely different purpose for newborns and infants than dreaming. When babies are in REM, it allows their brain to develop pathways, connections, and eventually, learn languages.

P3 Since your baby doesn't dream at this stage of brain development, it's safe to assume babies do not have nightmares, either. Nightmares stem from exposure to trauma(创伤), an overactive imagination, and the normal stresses of everyday life.

P4 Are you wondering, what do babies dream about? Good question, but the answer is nothing! So, when do babies start dreaming? The general consensus is that they start dreaming around the age of two. Psychologist David Foulkes studies children (from very small kids to teens) to bring the secrets of their dreams to the light of day. In his lab, he lets kids fall asleep and then wakes them 3 times a night and asks them to describe what they recall.

P5 Foulkes' findings are unsurprising. Basically, little kids have little dreams. But exactly what kids see while dreaming depends on their age. As children develop and grow, their dreams do too.

P6 Dreams of very small kids are usually just snapshots(快照), looking much more like a slideshow than a movie, when compared to the dreams of adults. They heavily feature animals and other familiar sights, like images of people eating. According to Foulkes, "Children's dream life…seems to be similar to their waking imagination and narration." Kids ages 5 – 9 begin seeing moving images and characters in action. Dreams now include multiple events strung together, one after the other. They also start developing greater ability to remember dreams. Still, that's not always the case: When roused during REM sleep, 25% of the kids in Foulkes' studies had no recollection of dreaming, a trend that continues through age 9.

P7 So, if your baby seems to be in a stressful state while sleeping or is upset upon waking, there may be other factors at play.

questions.stem: What can we assume about babies who appear upset upon waking?
questions.stemZh: 关于醒来时看起来心烦意乱的婴儿,我们可以假设什么?
options: They have been roused against their will.
They have been disturbed by a nightmare.
They have trouble recollecting the images of their dreams.
They have been affected by something other than dreaming.
optionsZh: 他们违背自己的意愿被唤醒了。
他们被噩梦打扰了。
他们难以回忆梦境的画面。

explain.判型: What can we assume about babies who appear upset upon waking? 含 assume，按 推断题处理。
explain.拆句: Q55 结构是 "What can we assume about babies who appear upset upon waking?"， who 引导定语从句修饰 babies，upon waking 是时间状语 "一醒来时"，整句无否定无比 较，理解关键是把 who 从句翻成 "那些一醒来就显得不安的婴儿"。
explain.定位: So, if your baby seems to be in a stressful state while sleeping or is upset upon waking, there may be other factors at play. 因此，如果你的婴儿睡觉时显得紧张、或一醒来就不安，那很可能是别的因素在起作用。 55. What can we assume about babies who appear upset upon waking? A) They have been roused against their will. B) They have been disturbed by a nightmare. C) They have trouble recollecting the images of their dreams. D) They have been affected by something other than dreaming.
explain.选项: A) 无中生有 原文 P7 没有说婴儿被人弄醒；They have been roused against their will. 凭空添加 "被弄醒" + "违背意愿" 两个文本无据的语义。 B) 与原文相反 原文 babies do not have nightmares 明确说婴儿不做噩梦；They have been disturbed by a nightmare. 反着说婴儿被噩梦惊扰。 C) 答非所问 题问 "哭醒原因"，They have trouble recollecting the images of their dreams. 把焦 点换成 "回忆梦境困难"，且 25% of the kids in Foulkes' studies had no recollection of dreaming 说的是 5-9 岁孩子，而非 "babies"。 D) ✓ 正确 there may be other factors at play ↔ They have been affected by something other than dreaming. 预判 "原因不是做梦" 与 They have been affected by something other than dreaming. 完全对应，选 D。

writing.directions: Suppose it is proposed that all university students should be required to learn academic writing. You are now to write a response by stating what you think of the proposal. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
writing.model: It has recently been proposed that all university students should be required to learn academic writing. In my view, this proposal deserves our full support, for such a skill is far more than an optional refinement. For one thing, academic writing trains students to organize ideas logically and cite sources honestly. When I wrote my first term paper, I struggled to structure arguments and nearly copied online material by mistake; a writing course would have taught me both clear reasoning and academic integrity. For another, this ability pays off well beyond campus. Whether a graduate applies for a research position or drafts a report at work, the capacity to express thoughts precisely on paper often determines success. Admittedly, mastering academic writing takes time and effort. Nevertheless, the long-term rewards clearly outweigh the cost. Therefore, I strongly believe universities should make this course compulsory, ideally starting from the first year so that students benefit throughout their studies.
writing.modelZh: 【参考译文】近来有人提议，所有大学生都应必修学术写作。在我看来，这一提议值得我们全力支持，因为这项技能远不只是锦上添花。一方面，学术写作训练学生把思路组织得有条理，并如实引用资料来源。我第一次写学期论文时，就苦于难以搭建论证结构，还险些误抄了网上的材料；一门写作课本可以同时教会我清晰的逻辑与学术诚信。另一方面，这项能力在校园之外同样受用。无论毕业生是申请科研岗位，还是在职场撰写报告，把想法在纸面上精准表达的能力，往往决定着成败。诚然，掌握学术写作需要时间和努力。然而，其长远回报显然远大于付出的成本。因此，我坚信大学应将这门课程设为必修，最好从大一就开设，让学生在整个学业期间都从中受益。【第 1 段】复述加表态。首段落实『复述加表态开篇』：It has recently been proposed that... 用同义改写复述提案、点题；紧接 In my view, this proposal deserves our full support 一句亮明支持立场，兑现 stating what you think of the proposal，开篇即拿任务分。【第 2 段】分点加例证。第二段落实『分点理由配例证』：For one thing... for another... 两条理由并列；中间 When I wrote my first term paper... 用亲身场景把『论文规范与学术诚信』坐实，Whether agraduate... 把价值延伸到就业深造，两条都咬住学术写作本身，不空谈。【第 3 段】让步加重申。第三段落实『让步转折收尾』：Admittedly... 先认成本，Nevertheless... 转折抬高回报，Therefore, I strongly believe... 顺势重申应必修并补『从大一开设』的温和建议，立场首尾一致、毫不摇摆。

translation.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2.
translation.source: 近年来，"城市漫步(city walk)"在中国的年轻人中悄然兴起，已成为一种旅游新潮流。与传统旅游不同，城市漫步不追求在短时间内游览尽可能多的景点。而是随意行走或按照主题路线漫步在城市的大街小巷。漫步者品尝地道小吃，欣赏特色建筑，了解当地生活方式。他们还用相机或手机记录城市的风景和人物。这种旅游方式能让城市漫步者更深入了解城市的历史与文化。
translation.reference: In recent years, city walk has quietly emerged among young people in China and has become a new travel trend. Unlike traditional travel, city walk does not seek to visit as many attractions as possible in a short time. Instead, city walkers wander randomly or stroll along themed routes through the streets and alleys of the city. They taste authentic snacks, admire distinctive buildings, and learn about local ways of life. They also record the city's scenery and people with cameras or mobile phones. This travel style enables city walkers to gain a deeper understanding of the city's history and culture.

sentences.trunk: city walk 作主语，两个并列谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 中文主语就是 "城市漫步(city walk)"，直接拿来作英文主语 city walk。核心动作有两个：悄然兴起 →has quietly emerged，已成为一种旅游新潮流→has become a new travel trend，用 and 连 成两个并列谓语，主谓宾是 city walk has emerged ... and has become a new trend。
sentences.downgrade: 时间状语前置、范围状语降级为介词短语 主干之外两个修饰成分各自降级安放：近年来是时间状语，译 In recent years 放句首；在中国的 年轻人中是范围状语，降级为介词短语 among young people in China 挂在第一个谓语后。这样 写成 In recent years, city walk has quietly emerged among young people in China and become a new travel trend，而不是照中文逐块平铺。
sentences.grammar: 时态 "近年来"+"已成为"暗示动作从过去延续到现在、且已产生结果，用现在完成时 has emerged / has become 比一般现在时更准；这是全篇基调一般现在时的合理偏离，由"已经""近年来"触发。 主谓一致 主语 city walk 是不可数/单数概念，助动词用 has 不用 have。 冠词与单复数 "一种旅游新潮流"是"一种"→用不定冠词 a new travel trend，trend 单数。
sentences.target: In recent years, city walk has quietly emerged among young people in China and has become a new travel trend. 2. 与传统旅游不同，城市漫步不追求在短时间内游览尽可能多的景点。

sentences.trunk: city walk 作主语，谓语 does not aim/seek（主语策略：原句主语） 主语仍是 城市漫步→city walk（承上文，可视情用 it）；核心动作是 不追求→does not aim to / does not seek to。主谓是 city walk does not seek to visit ...，宾语是"尽可能多的景点"。
sentences.downgrade: 对比状语前置、宾语用不定式短语承接 与传统旅游不同是对比状语，降级为介词短语 Unlike traditional travel 放句首；在短时间内游览 尽可能多的景点是"追求"的内容，用不定式短语 to visit as many attractions as possible in a short time 作宾语，其中"在短时间内"再降级为介词短语 in a short time。整句不平铺，而是 Unlike..., city walk does not seek to visit as many attractions as possible in a short time。
sentences.grammar: 时态 陈述城市漫步一贯的特点，回指全篇基调用一般现在时，故助动词用 does（第三人称单数 city walk）。 单复数 "尽可能多的景点"是可数复数→as many attractions as possible，attraction 用复数；many 修 饰可数复数正确。 固定搭配 "尽可能多"用比较结构 as many ... as possible；"在短时间内"用 in a short time，介词 in 不用 within 也可。
sentences.target: Unlike traditional travel, city walk does not seek to visit as many attractions as possible in a short time. 3. 而是随意行走或按照主题路线漫步在城市的大街小巷。

sentences.trunk: 补回主语 city walkers，谓语 wander/stroll（主语策略：补主语） 中文承上句省了主语，但行走的是"漫步者"，需补主语 city walkers（或顺承上句结构 it involves...）。核心动作是 随意行走 与 漫步→wander / stroll，宾语方向是 城市的大街小巷 →the streets and alleys of the city。主谓是 city walkers wander or stroll through the streets and alleys。
sentences.downgrade: 两种方式作状语、地点用介词短语 随意降级为副词 randomly/freely 修饰 wander；按照主题路线降级为介词短语 along themed routes 作方式状语；在城市的大街小巷降级为介词短语 through the streets and alleys of the city 作地点状语。两种行走方式用 or 连接：wander randomly or stroll along themed routes through the streets and alleys。
sentences.grammar: 时态 仍是描述漫步者一贯做法，回指全篇基调用一般现在时；若补主语 city walkers（复数）则动词用 原形 wander/stroll。 单复数 "大街小巷"是泛指多条街巷→streets and alleys 用复数；主语 city walkers 用复数。 介词搭配 "按照主题路线"用 along themed routes 或 following themed routes；"穿行于街巷"用 through，比 in 更有"穿行"的动感。
sentences.target: Instead, city walkers wander randomly or stroll along themed routes through the streets and alleys of the city. 4. 漫步者品尝地道小吃，欣赏特色建筑，了解当地生活方式。

sentences.trunk: city walkers 作主语，三个并列谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 主语就是 漫步者→city walkers；这是一句三动作的排比：品尝地道小吃→taste authentic snacks、欣赏特色建筑→admire distinctive buildings、了解当地生活方式→learn about local ways of life。三个动作地位平等，用并列谓语 taste..., admire..., and learn about... 处理。
sentences.downgrade: 本就是并列结构，无需深度降级 本句三个分句天然平行，只需用并列谓语并排，不必再降级为从句。各分句内部的修饰词处理一下 即可：地道→authentic、特色→distinctive/unique 作前置定语，当地生活方式→local ways of life。整句 City walkers taste authentic snacks, admire distinctive buildings, and learn about local ways of life。
sentences.grammar: 时态 描述漫步者一贯做的事，回指全篇基调用一般现在时；主语 city walkers 复数，动词用原形 taste/admire/learn。 单复数 "小吃""建筑"泛指多种→snacks、buildings 用复数；"生活方式"可用 ways of life 或不可数的 lifestyle。 介词搭配 "了解"用 learn about（about 不可漏），表示"了解关于……的情况"；不要写成 learn local life。
sentences.target: They taste authentic snacks, admire distinctive buildings, and learn about local ways of life. 5. 他们还用相机或手机记录城市的风景和人物。

sentences.trunk: They 作主语，谓语 record（主语策略：原句主语） 主语 他们→They（指漫步者）；核心动作是 记录→record；宾语是 城市的风景和人物→the scenery and people of the city。主谓宾是 They record the scenery and people。
sentences.downgrade: 工具状语用 with 介词短语降级 用相机或手机是"记录"所凭的工具，降级为介词短语 with cameras or mobile phones 作方式状 语，挂在动词后；还→also 作副词置于谓语前。整句 They also record the city's scenery and people with cameras or mobile phones，工具短语后置，不照中文"用……记录"的语序前置 堆砌。
sentences.grammar: 时态 仍描述漫步者一贯做法，回指全篇基调用一般现在时，主语 They 复数→动词原形 record。 单复数 "相机或手机"泛指→cameras or mobile phones 用复数；"人物"指城市中的人们→people。 冠词 特指"这座城市的"风景和人物→用 the city's scenery and people 或 the scenery and people of the city，加 the 表特指。
sentences.target: They also record the city's scenery and people with cameras or mobile phones. 6. 这种旅游方式能让城市漫步者更深入了解城市的历史与文化。

sentences.trunk: This travel style 作主语，谓语 enables/allows（主语策略：原句主语） 主语是 这种旅游方式→This travel style/way of travel；核心结构是 能让……了解…… →enables/allows city walkers to ...，用"enable sb to do"句型。宾语补足语是 更深入了解城市 的历史与文化→to gain a deeper understanding of the city's history and culture。
sentences.downgrade: "更深入了解"名词化为 a deeper understanding 更深入了解可处理为不定式 to gain a deeper understanding of...，把"深入"用形容词比较级 deeper 修饰名词 understanding，比硬译 understand more deeply 更地道；城市的历史与文化 →the city's history and culture 作 of 的宾语。整句 This travel style enables city walkers to gain a deeper understanding of the city's history and culture。
sentences.grammar: 时态 陈述这种方式的一贯功效，回指全篇基调用一般现在时；主语 This travel style 第三人称单数→谓 语用 enables。 主谓一致 主语 This travel style 是单数，动词加 -s 用 enables/allows，别漏掉第三人称单数的 -s。 句型搭配 enable/allow 后接"宾语 + to do"，不定式 to 不可漏；"对……的更深了解"用 understanding of，介词 of 固定。
sentences.target: This travel style enables city walkers to gain a deeper understanding of the city's history and culture. 英语四级 2025年12月·第2套 · 全卷构成 Part I 写作 题目解析 → Part II 听力 题目解析 → Part Ⅲ Section A 完形填空（选词填空） 题目解析 → Part Ⅲ Section B 长篇阅读（信息匹配） 题目解析 → Part Ⅲ Section C 阅读理解（四选一） 题目解析 → Part Ⅲ Section C (2) 阅读理解（四选一） 题目解析 → Part IV 汉译英（段落翻译） 本题

questions.stem: Where was the black cat found?
questions.stemZh: 这只黑猫是在哪里被发现的?
questions.answerText: Under the engine cover of a man's car.

explain.定位: The black cat was found curled up under the engine cover of David King's car when he decided to do an oil check after dropping his grandson off at school in Kent. 这只黑猫是在大卫·金送孙子上学后、决定检查机油时，被发现蜷缩在他汽车的引擎盖下 面的。
explain.信号: found ＋ 地点介词短语。答案句的信号是动词 found 紧跟一个表地点的介词短语 found curled up under the engine cover of David King's car——题干问 Where… found，原 文恰好出现 found ＋『在哪儿』，这就是承载答案的那一句。
explain.替换: under the engine cover of David King's car ↔Under the engine cover of a man's car. 人名换成泛称 a man
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 选项把后文出现的 UK charity Cats Protection 里的 charity 一词搬来，编成『慈善机构门 口』这个地点。可录音里 charity 只用来说明谁救的猫，从没说猫是在慈善机构门口被发现 的，属听到 charity 就想选的原词陷阱。 借用原文：Following a rescue by UK charity Cats Protection B) 张冠李戴 选项把末段的 Mr King's neighbour（邻居）搬来，说猫是在『邻居的车里』被发现。但邻 居在录音里是猫的主人、出现在结局处，发现猫的车是金先生自己的车，把发现地点安到邻 居车上是张冠李戴。 借用原文：reunited with its owner, Mr King's neighbour D) 原词陷阱 选项抓住原文的 school in Kent，把『学校门口』说成发现地点。可录音里 school 是金先 生送孙子去的地方、是事情发生前的背景，猫是他送完孙子、回来做机油检查时才在引擎盖 下被发现的，发现地不是学校门口。 借用原文：after dropping his grandson off at school in Kent

optionsZh: 在一家慈善基金会的办公室外面。
在David King邻居的车内。
在一名男子汽车的引擎盖下面。
在Kent一所小学的大门口。
options: Outside the office of a charity foundation.
Inside the car of David King's neighbour.
Under the engine cover of a man's car.
At the gate of a grade school in Kent.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the cat at the end of the news report?
questions.stemZh: 关于这只猫,新闻报道最后我们了解到什么?
questions.answerText: It got reunited with its owner.

explain.定位: Following a rescue by UK charity Cats Protection, the four-year-old cat was later reunited with its owner, Mr King's neighbour. 在英国慈善机构『猫咪保护』救援之后，这只四岁的猫最终与它的主人——金先生的邻居 ——团聚了。
explain.信号: 末段＋later标结局。本句是录音最末一段、且含时间词 later，正对应题干的 at the end； 新闻的结果通常落在最后一句，later reunited 直接交代了猫的最终下场，是答案句。
explain.替换: reunited with its owner ↔It got reunited with its owner. 近乎原句的同义重述
explain.排除: B) 未提及 选项说猫『在救援中受伤』，但录音从头到尾只字未提受伤，末段只说被救后团聚。它利用 第3段 terrified（受惊）、stuck（卡住）等词让人联想到猫很惨，进而脑补成『受伤』，实 属过度推断、原文未提。 C) 张冠李戴 选项把第1段的 grandson（孙子）搬来，说猫成了金先生孙子的宠物。可孙子只在『送孙 子上学』的背景里出现，录音末段明说猫团聚的对象是主人即邻居，不是被孙子养，属张冠 李戴。 借用原文：after dropping his grandson off at school in Kent D) 原词陷阱 选项说猫『被交由英国一家慈善机构照管』，盗用了末段 UK charity Cats Protection 这个 真出现的机构。但录音里 charity 是负责『救援』的一方，救完之后猫是团聚而非留在机构 照管，把过程中的救援者说成最终归宿，差在结局。 借用原文：Following a rescue by UK charity Cats Protection

optionsZh: 它与主人团聚了。
它在救援过程中受伤了。
它成为了King先生孙子的宠物。
它被交由一家英国慈善机构照料。
options: It got reunited with its owner.
It was injured during the rescue.
It became a pet of Mr King's grandson.
It was placed in the care of a UK charity.
questions._leakedNextScript: In less than a month, the Special Olympics Spring Games will make a return to Fayetteville. The Games are coming back for the first time in five years. The event will take place at Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.

questions.stem: What will Fayetteville witness in less than a month?
questions.stemZh: 不到一个月后，Fayetteville 将见证什么?
questions.answerText: The opening of the Special Olympics Spring Games.

explain.定位: In less than a month, the Special Olympics Spring Games will make a return to Fayetteville. 不到一个月后，特殊奥林匹克运动会春季赛事将重返费耶特维尔。
explain.信号: 题干时间词原样出现。录音开头 In less than a month 与题干 in less than a month 用词 完全一致，这种"题干时间状语在原文原样响起"就是最强的定位信号，听到它，紧跟其后的 主语就是答案所在。
explain.替换: the Special Olympics Spring Games will make a return ↔ The opening of the Special Olympics Spring Games. 重返即开赛
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 录音确实念到了 Methodist University（卫理公会大学），A 就把这个原词捡来编出 The 100th anniversary celebration of Methodist University."百年校庆"，但原文只说赛事在 该校举办，从没提任何校庆或"100th"，是典型听到地名就想选的原词陷阱。 借用原文：The event will take place at Methodist University. B) 原词陷阱 录音说赛事是 coming back for the first time in five years（五年来首次回归），B 把 "five years" 这个原词改头换面成 The first important political event in the next five years.，既把"赛事"偷换成"政治大事"，又把"过去五年"扭成"未来五年"，是盗用数字+偷换 概念的双重陷阱。 借用原文：The Games are coming back for the first time in five years. D) 偷换概念 选项 The reunion of this year's Olympic gold medalists. 借了原文反复出现的 "Olympics" 来误导：原文是 Special Olympics（特殊奥林匹克/残障人士运动会），D 偷 偷掐掉 "Special" 变成普通"Olympic gold medalists 金牌选手聚会"，原文从未提金牌选手 聚会，属偷换概念。 借用原文：the Special Olympics Spring Games will make a return to Fayetteville

optionsZh: Methodist University 的百年校庆庆典。
未来五年中的第一个重要政治活动。
特殊奥林匹克春季运动会的开幕式。
今年奥运会金牌得主的重聚。
options: The 100th anniversary celebration of Methodist University.
The first important political event in the next five years.
The opening of the Special Olympics Spring Games.
The reunion of this year's Olympic gold medalists.

questions.stem: What did Benjamin Kowalczyk say is rewarding to see?
questions.stemZh: Benjamin Kowalczyk 说看到什么令人欣慰?
questions.answerText: Athletes with special needs triumph in the Games.

explain.定位: Kowalczyk said it's rewarding to see athletes with special needs triumph in the Games. Kowalczyk 说，看到有特殊需求的运动员在赛事中取得胜利，是很有意义、很值得的。
explain.信号: 题干rewarding原话再现。录音 Kowalczyk said it's rewarding to see 把题干里的人名和 评价词 "rewarding" 原样念出，这是"人物+评价词"双重信号，听到它就知道接下来 "to see" 后面那件事正是答案承载句。
explain.替换: athletes with special needs triumph in the Games ↔ Athletes with special needs triumph in the Games. 评价词后内容直接对应
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 录音第三段确有 visit the Games' website to sign up，A 把这句原词整段搬来，但那是 给"想当志愿者的人"的报名指引，不是 Kowalczyk "觉得值得一看"的事，盗用原词却答非所 问。 借用原文：Organizers encourage them to visit the Games' website to sign up. C) 张冠李戴 选项 Organizers devote their time and energy to the Games. 看似贴合主题，但原文 Kowalczyk 评"值得"的是运动员取胜，并没说"组织者投入时间精力"这件事值得看；原文只 说想帮忙的人可去志愿，把评价对象悄悄换成了组织者，属张冠李戴+未提及。 借用原文：it's rewarding to see athletes with special needs triumph in the Games D) 原词陷阱 录音第二段确实念了 There will also be a fun tent for children.，D 把 "fun tent/children" 这组原词捡来，但那只是顺带交代赛事设施，Kowalczyk 的 "rewarding" 评价根本没落在孩子玩耍上，是听到原词就想选的原词陷阱。 借用原文：There will also be a fun tent for children. 1 A German supermarket has been ordered to destroy its chocolate rabbits after it lost a court battle with a Swiss chocolate manufacturer. 一家德国超市在与一家瑞士巧克力制造商的法庭诉讼中败诉后,被勒令销毁其巧克力兔子产品。 2 The Swiss firm had argued its gold-wrapped chocolate rabbit deserved copyright protection from a similar product sold by the budget supermarket. 这家瑞士公司辩称,其金色包装的巧克力兔子应当受到版权保护,以防止这家廉价超市销售的类似产品 侵权。 3 Switzerland's highest court agreed and overturned a ruling last year by the country's commercial court that had sided with the supermarket. It ordered that all the imitation rabbits be destroyed, but suggested the chocolate needn't be wasted. It could be melted for use in other products. 瑞士最高法院表示同意,推翻了去年该国商事法院支持超市的裁决。法院下令销毁所有仿冒兔子产品,但建 议巧克力无需浪费,可以融化用于其他产品。 4 It said even though there are some differences between the two products, there was still the possibility of confusion for consumers. The Swiss manufacturer's rabbit has a red bow and bell, while the German supermarket's has a green bow and bell. The colour of the wrapper is similar, as are the illustrations of the features. 法院称,尽管两种产品之间存在一些差异,但仍有可能使消费者产生混淆。瑞士制造商的兔子有红色蝴蝶结 和铃铛,而德国超市的兔子有绿色蝴蝶结和铃铛。包装纸的颜色相似,特征的图案也相似。 Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard. 5 The chocolate company has been to court before to protect its popular chocolate treat. Last year, a German federal court said the shade of the gold wrapping was also protected. 这家巧克力公司此前曾诉诸法庭以保护其畅销巧克力产品。去年,德国联邦法院裁定金色包装纸的色调也受 到保护。

optionsZh: 志愿者访问运动会网站报名参加。
有特殊需要的运动员在运动会上取得胜利。
组织者为运动会投入他们的时间和精力。
孩子们在趣味帐篷里玩耍并尽情享受。
options: Volunteers visit the Games' website to sign up.
Athletes with special needs triumph in the Games.
Organizers devote their time and energy to the Games.
Children play in a fun tent and enjoy themselves fully.

questions.stem: What has the German supermarket been ordered to do?
questions.stemZh: 这家德国超市被要求做什么?

explain.定位: A German supermarket has been ordered to destroy its chocolate rabbits after it lost a court battle with a Swiss chocolate manufacturer. 一家德国超市在与一家瑞士巧克力制造商的官司中败诉后，被勒令销毁其巧克力兔子。
explain.信号: 命令信号 ordered to。答案句的信号是 has been ordered to destroy，ordered to 正是 题干 been ordered to 的呼应，这种表命令、判决的短语就是答案落点，听到立刻锁定其 后的动作。
explain.替换: destroy its chocolate rabbits ↔Destroy its imitation chocolate rabbits. 近乎同表述加补词
explain.排除: B) 原词陷阱 选项 Change the wrapping of its commodities. 借用了原文后文反复提到的 wrapper （包装），但原文从没要求超市改包装，命令是销毁，属听到 wrapping 就想选的原词陷 阱。 借用原文：The colour of the wrapper is similar C) 原词陷阱 选项 Compensate for the Swiss manufacturer's loss. 拼用了原文的 Swiss manufacturer 和 lost（败诉），但原文判的是销毁，从未提赔偿损失，是把熟词重组出的假动作。 借用原文：it lost a court battle with a Swiss chocolate manufacturer D) 原词陷阱 选项 Defend itself in the country's commercial court. 借了原文的 commercial court， 但那是去年商业法院的旧判决场景，本题命令是销毁兔子，并非要超市去出庭辩护。 借用原文：overturned a ruling last year by the country's commercial court

optionsZh: 销毁其仿制的巧克力兔子。
更改其商品的包装。
赔偿瑞士制造商的损失。
在该国商事法院为自己辩护。
options: Change the wrapping of its commodities.
Compensate for the Swiss manufacturer's loss.
Defend itself in the country's commercial court.

questions.stem: What did Switzerland's highest court suggest about the chocolate in question?
questions.stemZh: 瑞士最高法院对有关巧克力提出了什么建议?
questions.answerText: It could be reused in other products.

explain.定位: It ordered that all the imitation rabbits be destroyed, but suggested the chocolate needn't be wasted. It could be melted for use in other products. 法院下令销毁所有仿制兔子，但建议巧克力不必浪费，可以熔化后用于其他产品。
explain.信号: 转折 but 后是真意。答案句信号是转折词 but suggested the chocolate needn't be wasted，but 前讲销毁、but 后才是对巧克力的建议，转折之后才是落点，这正呼应题干 的 suggest。
explain.替换: melted for use in other products ↔It could be reused in other products. 熔化再用即重复使用
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 选项 rewrapped and sold by the budget supermarket 搬来原文的 budget supermarket，但原文建议是熔化再用，从没说重新包装由该超市出售，是熟词拼出的假处 置。 借用原文：a similar product sold by the budget supermarket B) 原词陷阱 选项 reshaped into animals other than rabbits 借了原文 rabbits 一词臆造出改造成别的 动物，原文只说熔化用于其他产品，并未提改塑成动物。 借用原文：all the imitation rabbits be destroyed C) 原词陷阱 选项 resold cheaper to avoid waste 借了原文 needn't be wasted 中的 waste 概念，但 原文是熔化再用以避免浪费，不是降价转售，处置动作被偷换。 借用原文：the chocolate needn't be wasted

optionsZh: 它可以被重新包装并由廉价超市出售。
它可以被重新塑造成兔子以外的动物。
它可以以更低价格转售以避免浪费。
它可以在其他产品中重新使用。
options: It could be rewrapped and sold by the budget supermarket.
It could be reshaped into animals other than rabbits.
It could be resold cheaper to avoid waste.
It could be reused in other products.

questions.stem: Why did Switzerland's highest court overturn the commercial court's ruling?
questions.stemZh: 瑞士最高法院为什么推翻商事法院的裁决?

explain.定位: It said even though there are some differences between the two products, there was still the possibility of confusion for consumers. 法院表示，尽管两种产品之间存在一些差异，但仍有可能让消费者产生混淆。
explain.信号: 让步转折露真因。答案句信号是让步结构 even though there are some differences...there was still the possibility of confusion，even though 让一步、 but/still 后才是真正理由——担心消费者混淆，这就是推翻判决的原因。
explain.替换: the possibility of confusion for consumers ↔To prevent consumers' possible confusion. 存在混淆即为防混淆
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 选项 To be fair to the German supermarkets. 借了原文反复出现的 German supermarket，但原文推翻原判恰恰对超市不利，目的是防混淆而非对超市公平，方向相 反。 借用原文：A German supermarket has been ordered to destroy B) 偷换概念 选项 To protect chocolate retailers' interests. 把原文的 consumers（消费者）偷换成 retailers（零售商），原文明说担心的是消费者混淆，保护对象被换了一方。 借用原文：the possibility of confusion for consumers C) 未提及 选项 To boost the growth of the chocolate industry. 借了反复出现的 chocolate，但原 文从未提推动巧克力行业发展这一目的，是凭熟词臆造的目的。 Section B 1 M: Can you please hand me that book over there? It has instructions for making a winter bean salad. My sister's boyfriend is coming over for dinner. He's vegetarian, so I need to make a lot of vegetable dishes. M: 你能把那边那本书递给我吗？上面有冬季豆子沙拉的做法。我姐姐的男朋友要过来吃晚饭。他是素食 主义者，所以我得做很多蔬菜菜肴。 Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 2 W: He only eats vegetables, no meat? That doesn't sound like a very balanced diet. How can he get enough protein? What does he do to strengthen his muscles and all that? W: 他只吃蔬菜,不吃肉?这听起来可不像是均衡的饮食啊。他怎么获取足够的蛋白质?他怎么增强肌肉什 么的? 3 M: Apparently that's no problem. He's explained this to me when we first met. He eats a variety of different vegetables and nuts, especially those with high amounts of protein. M: 显然这不是问题。我们第一次见面时他跟我解释过。他吃各种不同的蔬菜和坚果,尤其是那些蛋白质含 量高的。 4 W: It sounds a bit difficult, but he's done his research I suppose. What's his reasoning for being vegetarian? Is it his religion, health condition, or lifestyle? W: 听起来有点难,不过我想他是做过研究的。他吃素的理由是什么?是宗教信仰、健康状况,还是生活方式? 5 M: He's an animal activist. He's always been very sensitive and sympathizes with animals. He's even written to his state senator about the torture of dolphins in sea parks. He says that keeping animals in zoos and parks causes them great distress. M: 他是个动物保护主义者。他一直很敏感,同情动物。他甚至给他所在州的参议员写信,抗议海洋公园虐待 海豚。他说把动物关在动物园和公园里会给它们造成巨大的痛苦。 6 W: That's a little gloomy, but I can understand that to a point. Not all zoos and animal parks have the most favorable conditions, but without them it just wouldn't be feasible to learn about animals and their environments. Besides, I don't think I could ever give up a good hot dog at a baseball game. W: 这有点悲观,不过我在某种程度上能理解。不是所有动物园和动物公园的条件都最理想,但没有它们的话, 了解动物及其生存环境根本就不可行。再说,我觉得我永远都放弃不了在棒球赛上吃根美味热狗。 7 M: Honestly, I agree, but just don't let him hear you say that. He's the spokesperson for his local animal rights group. M: 老实说,我同意,不过别让他听到你这么说。他是当地动物权利组织的发言人。

optionsZh: 为了对德国超市公平。
为了保护巧克力零售商的利益。
为了促进巧克力行业的增长。
为了防止消费者可能产生的混淆。
options: To be fair to the German supermarkets.
To boost the growth of the chocolate industry.

questions.stem: What does the man request the woman to do?
questions.stemZh: 男士要求女士做什么?

explain.定位: Can you please hand me that book over there? 你能把那边那本书递给我吗？
explain.信号: 请求句 Can you please...。答案句的信号是请求口吻 Can you please hand me that book over there?，Can you please 一出，后面跟的动作 hand me that book 就是男的 请女的做的事，这正是"做什么"题要锁定的落点。
explain.替换: hand me that book ↔Pass a book to him. hand 与 pass 同义换词
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 A 的 Return the handbook to him. 用 handbook 蹭录音里的 hand me that book 的发 音（hand...book），听着像，但录音说的是 hand（递）+ book（书），不是 handbook （手册），更没有 return（还）的意思。 借用原文：hand me that book B) 答非所问 B 的 Make a vegetable dish. 用了录音 making a winter bean salad 里的做素菜原词，但 做菜是男的自己"I need to make"，不是请女的做，答非所问。 借用原文：I need to make a lot of vegetable dishes D) 原词陷阱 D 的 Meet his sister's boyfriend. 取自录音 My sister's boyfriend is coming over for dinner 的原词，但那只是交代背景（男友要来吃饭），并非男的请女的去见他。 借用原文：My sister's boyfriend is coming over for dinner

optionsZh: 把手册还给他。
做一道蔬菜菜肴。
把一本书递给他。
见见他姐姐的男朋友。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about eating vegetables only?
questions.stemZh: 关于只吃蔬菜,女士是怎么说的?
questions.answerText: It doesn't seem to be a balanced diet.

explain.定位: He only eats vegetables, no meat? That doesn't sound like a very balanced diet. 他只吃菜、不吃肉？那听起来不像是很均衡的饮食啊。
explain.信号: 评价句 That doesn't sound like...。答案信号是女的抛出的总评价 That doesn't sound like a very balanced diet，doesn't sound like 是直接表态，这是她对"只吃素"的核心判 断，后面 protein、muscles 都是她为这个判断补的理由。
explain.替换: That doesn't sound like a very balanced diet ↔It doesn't seem to be a balanced diet. sound like 换 seem to be
explain.排除: B) 原词陷阱 B 的 It would reduce one's protein intake. 蹭了录音 How can he get enough protein? 的 protein 原词，但女的只是反问"怎么获取足够蛋白质"来支撑她的判断，并没下"会减少蛋 白质摄入"的结论。 借用原文：How can he get enough protein? C) 原词陷阱 C 的 It would do harm to one's muscles. 借用录音 strengthen his muscles 的 muscles 原词，但女的是问"他怎么练肌肉"，并没说"会伤肌肉"，属于无中生有地拔高。 借用原文：strengthen his muscles D) 偷换概念 D 的 It doesn't sound practical for her. 套用了录音 sound 的口吻，但女的评价的是"这 饮食不均衡"，从没说"对她本人不实际"，把评判对象悄悄换成了"对她"。 借用原文：That doesn't sound like a very balanced diet

optionsZh: 这似乎不是均衡的饮食。
这会减少一个人的蛋白质摄入。
这会对一个人的肌肉造成伤害。
这对她来说听起来不实际。
options: It doesn't seem to be a balanced diet.
It would reduce one's protein intake.
It would do harm to one's muscles.
It doesn't sound practical for her.

questions.stem: Why does the boyfriend of the man's sister choose to be a vegetarian?
questions.stemZh: 男士的姐姐的男朋友为什么选择成为素食主义者?

explain.定位: He's an animal activist. He's always been very sensitive and sympathizes with animals. 他是个动物保护活动者。他一向很敏感，对动物充满同情。
explain.信号: 亮明身份句 He's an animal activist。答案信号是男的直接亮出男友的身份与立场 He's an animal activist，紧接 sympathizes with animals。原因题里这种"He's a + 身份/立场"的 句子，往往就是动机所在——他吃素是因为他是动物保护者。
explain.替换: He's an animal activist ↔To protect animal rights. 身份具体说法换成概括目的
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 A 的 To improve his health. 蹭了录音 health condition 的 health 原词，但那是女的列举 可能原因时随口提的选项之一，录音随后明确否掉、给出的真实原因是动物保护，不是健 康。 借用原文：Is it his religion, health condition, or lifestyle? C) 原词陷阱 C 的 To follow a trendy lifestyle. 借用录音 lifestyle 原词，但这同样只是女的列举的待选 项之一，男的回答里根本没提"赶潮流"，是答非所问。 借用原文：Is it his religion, health condition, or lifestyle? D) 原词陷阱 D 的 To stick to his religious belief. 用了录音 religion 原词，且"宗教吃素"最符合日常常 识，最易被默认选中；但录音明说原因是动物保护，宗教只是女的列举的可能性之一，并非 答案。 借用原文：Is it his religion, health condition, or lifestyle?

optionsZh: 为了改善他的健康。
为了保护动物权利。
为了追随时尚的生活方式。
为了坚持他的宗教信仰。
options: To stick to his religious belief.

questions.stem: On what point does the man agree with the woman at the end of the conversation?
questions.stemZh: 在对话结束时,男士在哪一点上同意女士的观点?
questions.answerText: The necessity of having zoos and eating meat.

explain.定位: W: Not all zoos and animal parks have the most favorable conditions, but without them it just wouldn't be feasible to learn about animals and their environments. Besides, I don't think I could ever give up a good hot dog at a baseball game. M: Honestly, I agree. 女：并不是所有动物园和动物公园条件都最理想，但要是没有它们，就没法了解动物和它们 的生存环境了。再说，我可舍不得放弃看棒球赛时来一根热狗。男：说实话，我同意。
explain.信号: 赞同信号 Honestly, I agree。答案信号是男的结尾的明确赞同 Honestly, I agree，它指向 的是女的紧挨着说的两点——动物园有存在的必要 without them it just wouldn't be feasible to learn about animals 和不愿放弃吃热狗（肉）I could ever give up a good hot dog。赞同句认同的就是这两点合起来的立场。
explain.替换: without them it just wouldn't be feasible to learn about animals ↔ The necessity of having zoos and eating meat. 没了就不行 = 有必要 I don't think I could ever give up a good hot dog ↔eating meat 舍不得放弃热狗 = 要吃肉
explain.排除: A) 张冠李戴 A 的 The torture and distress dolphins suffer in parks. 几乎照搬录音 the torture of dolphins in sea parks 与 causes them great distress 的原词，但那是男友（动物活动 家）的立场，不是男女二人结尾达成的共识，张冠李戴。 借用原文：the torture of dolphins in sea parks C) 原词陷阱 C 的 The gloomy environments animals are kept in. 蹭录音 That's a little gloomy 的 gloomy 原词，但 gloomy 是女的形容男友说法"有点令人沮丧"，并非两人一致认同"动物 处境阴郁"，答非所问。 借用原文：That's a little gloomy D) 原词陷阱 D 的 The urgency of joining an animal rights group. 借用录音 his local animal rights group 的 animal rights group 原词，但录音只是说男友是该组织发言人，根本没提"加入 组织的紧迫性"，属凭空编造。 借用原文：He's the spokesperson for his local animal rights group 1 W: Did you see that television program on air travel last night? W: 你昨晚看那个关于航空旅行的电视节目了吗？ 2 M: Yes. The part about overcoming jetlag was interesting. I was surprised that the expert recommended not eating for the entire journey and avoiding sleeping on the plane. M: 看了。关于克服时差反应那部分挺有意思的。我很惊讶那个专家建议整个旅程都不吃东西，还要避免 在飞机上睡觉。 3 W: I was too, as I read an article on the subject in the past that suggested the opposite. It claimed that it was important not to miss meals and that taking a nap on the plane was the best way to adjust to a new time zone. W: 我也是，因为我以前读过一篇关于这个话题的文章，建议的是相反的做法。文章说不能错过用餐很重 要，而且在飞机上小睡是适应新时区的最好方法。 4 M: Well, the expert on the show did cite research supporting her recommendations, so I guess I'll give it a try next time I fly a long distance. Jetlag is a big problem for me and has been for the last few years, even though I never suffered from it before. M: 嗯，节目里那位专家确实引用了研究来支持她的建议，所以我想下次长途飞行时试试看。时差反应对 我来说是个大问题，过去几年一直这样，尽管我以前从来没有受过时差困扰。 Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 5 W: Well, she did say that jetlag often becomes more of a problem after 40, so I guess I'm lucky that I can still adjust to different time zones well. My problem is I'm afraid to fly. W: 嗯，她确实说过时差反应在40岁之后往往会变成更大的问题，所以我想我很幸运，还能很好地适应不 同的时区。我的问题是我害怕坐飞机。 6 M: Oh, I didn't know that. Actually, my mother is terrified of airplanes to the point where she can't even fly, so our family vacations were always by car or train. M: 哦，我不知道这个。其实我妈妈特别害怕飞机，严重到根本不能坐飞机，所以我们家的假期总是开车 或坐火车。 7 W: I'm not as bad as that. I just get anxious before I fly and feel nervous the whole time we're in the air, which is why I was hoping the television program would cover that topic more than it did. W: 我没那么严重。我只是在坐飞机前会焦虑，在空中的整个过程都感到紧张，这就是为什么我希望那个 电视节目能更多地讨论这个话题，而不是像实际那样一带而过。 8 M: Yeah. That segment was too brief, especially as so many people have that problem. She said 20% of people are afraid to fly. M: 是啊。那个部分太简短了，特别是有那么多人都有这个问题。她说20%的人害怕坐飞机。 9 W: Actually, it was a quarter of people, so the problem really is widespread and deserves attention. W: 实际上是四分之一的人，所以这个问题确实很普遍，值得关注。

optionsZh: 海豚在公园里遭受的折磨和痛苦。
拥有动物园和吃肉的必要性。
动物被饲养的阴暗环境。
加入动物权利组织的紧迫性。
options: The torture and distress dolphins suffer in parks.
The necessity of having zoos and eating meat.
The gloomy environments animals are kept in.
The urgency of joining an animal rights group.

questions.stem: What part of the TV program does the man say was interesting?
questions.stemZh: 男士说电视节目的哪部分内容很有趣?
questions.answerText: The part about getting over jetlag.

explain.定位: The part about overcoming jetlag was interesting. 关于克服时差的那一部分很有趣。
explain.信号: 被问者男士的直接应答 + 评价词 interesting。本题问的是男士，男士开口的 The part about overcoming jetlag was interesting. 就是被问者的直接应答，句中 interesting 与 题干 interesting 完全对应，是把这句锁成答案句的信号。
explain.替换: overcoming jetlag ↔getting over jetlag 同义短语替换 overcome=get over
explain.排除: B) 未提及 The part about air travel in the past 里 air travel 是整段对话的大话题词，听着耳熟，但 男士说有趣的是克服时差那部分，"过去的航空旅行"录音并未作为有趣的一部分提到，属拿 大话题词凑出的诱选。 C) 原词陷阱 not eating on board the plane 盗用了录音 not eating for the entire journey 这个原词 内容，但那是男士转述"专家推荐"的建议、且他说的是"surprised（吃惊）"，并非回答"哪 部分有趣"。听到 not eating 就选即落陷阱。 借用原文：the expert recommended not eating for the entire journey D) 原词陷阱 avoiding sleeping on the plane 盗用录音 avoiding sleeping on the plane 的原词，但 这与 C 一样属男士转述的专家建议、令他吃惊的内容，并不是他点名"有趣"的那部分（有趣 的是克服时差整块），属原词陷阱。 借用原文：avoiding sleeping on the plane

optionsZh: 关于克服时差反应的部分。
关于过去航空旅行的部分。
关于不在飞机上进食的部分。
关于避免在飞机上睡觉的部分。
options: The part about getting over jetlag.
The part about air travel in the past.
The part about not eating on board the plane.
The part about avoiding sleeping on the plane.

questions.stem: What does the man say he will do next time he flies a long distance?
questions.stemZh: 男士说他下次长途飞行时会做什么?
questions.answerText: Try following the advice given by the expert on the show.

explain.定位: the expert on the show did cite research supporting her recommendations, so I guess I'll give it a try next time I fly a long distance. 节目里的那位专家确实引用了支持她建议的研究，所以我想下次长途飞行时我会试试看。
explain.信号: 表打算的信号 I'll give it a try + 时间短语 next time。I guess I'll give it a try next time I fly a long distance 里的 I'll give it a try 是典型"打算"信号，又带 next time I fly a long distance 与题干时间完全吻合，是锁定答案句的双重信号。
explain.替换: give it a try ↔Try following the advice give it a try=try following，照建议试一试 the expert on the show did cite research supporting her recommendations ↔ the advice given by the expert on the show her recommendations=the advice，同为专家建议
explain.排除: A) 张冠李戴 Take a nap to adjust to a new time zone 盗用了女士那句 taking a nap on the plane was the best way to adjust to a new time zone 的原词，但那是女士转述"过去文章"的主 张，且专家恰恰建议"不要睡"，并非男士下次要做的事，属张冠李戴。 借用原文：taking a nap on the plane was the best way to adjust to a new time zone B) 张冠李戴 Have meals as usual to stay away from hunger 对应女士读到的旧观点 it was important not to miss meals，而男士打算照的是"专家建议"，专家主张是 not eating ——男士要做的恰与 B 相反，属张冠李戴兼与原文相反。 借用原文：it was important not to miss meals C) 偷换概念 Concentrate on reading articles recommended by experts 把录音里的 expert 与 W 提 到的 an article on the subject 拼在一起，造出"读专家推荐的文章"，但男士说的是 give it a try（照建议试做），并非去读文章，属偷换概念。 借用原文：I read an article on the subject in the past

optionsZh: 小睡一会儿以适应新时区。
像平常一样进餐以避免饥饿。
专注阅读专家推荐的文章。
尝试遵循节目中专家给出的建议。
options: Take a nap to adjust to a new time zone.
Have meals as usual to stay away from hunger.
Concentrate on reading articles recommended by experts.
Try following the advice given by the expert on the show.

questions.stem: Why does the woman think she is lucky?
questions.stemZh: 女士为什么认为自己很幸运?
questions.answerText: She does not have to worry about jetlag.

explain.定位: she did say that jetlag often becomes more of a problem after 40, so I guess I'm lucky that I can still adjust to different time zones well. 她确实说过时差在 40 岁以后往往会变成更大的问题，所以我想我算幸运，因为我还能很好 地适应不同的时区。
explain.信号: 标志词 I'm lucky + that 引出理由。I'm lucky that I can still adjust to different time zones well 里 I'm lucky 直接对应题干 lucky，紧跟的 that 从句给出理由——这个"幸运 + that 理由"结构就是答案句信号。
explain.替换: I can still adjust to different time zones well ↔She does not have to worry about jetlag 能适应时区=不必担心时差，肯否定转换
explain.排除: A) 与原文相反 She does not have any problem flying 与原文相反：女士紧接着说 My problem is I'm afraid to fly，明说自己有怕飞的问题，所以"飞行无问题"是反着说的，且她的幸运也不是指 这点。 借用原文：My problem is I'm afraid to fly B) 未提及 She can spend a lot of time vacationing 里 vacation 蹭了后文男士提到的 our family vacations，但那是男士讲自家度假方式，女士的幸运与"能度很多假"毫无关系，属未提及。 借用原文：our family vacations were always by car or train D) 未提及 She has been well treated when traveling"旅行中受优待"在整段录音里没有任何对应内 容，与女士的幸运（能适应时区）也不搭，属凭空捏造。

optionsZh: 她乘飞机没有任何问题。
她可以花大量时间度假。
她不必担心时差反应。
她在旅行时得到了很好的待遇。
options: She does not have any problem flying.
She can spend a lot of time vacationing.
She does not have to worry about jetlag.
She has been well treated when traveling.

questions.stem: Why does the woman think the problem of being afraid to fly deserves attention?
questions.stemZh: 女士为什么认为害怕乘飞机的问题值得关注?
questions.answerText: It affects twenty-five percent of people.

explain.定位: Actually, it was a quarter of people, so the problem really is widespread and deserves attention. 其实是四分之一的人，所以这个问题确实很普遍，值得关注。
explain.信号: 纠正信号 Actually + 数字 a quarter，且与题干 deserves attention 同词。女士用 Actually, it was a quarter of people 纠正男士先前说的数字，so the problem really is widespread and deserves attention 里 deserves attention 与题干同词——Actually 的 纠正语气与同词回扣是双重信号。
explain.替换: a quarter of people ↔twenty-five percent of people a quarter=25%，分数与百分比换算
explain.排除: A) 未提及 It has caused heavy losses to many airlines 蹭了全篇的 air travel/航空话题，但"给航空 公司造成巨额亏损"录音从未提及，女士给的理由是比例之高，不是公司亏损，属未提及。 B) 未提及 It impacts female travelers more seriously 凭空加了"female travelers、more seriously"的范围与程度，录音只说影响四分之一的人、并未区分性别，属无中生有地偷加 范围程度。 C) 与原文相反 It has long been ignored by many experts 借了对话反复出现的 expert 设原词诱惑，但 录音说的是这问题 deserves attention（值得关注），并未说"长期被专家忽视"，方向相 反，属与原文相反兼借词诱选。 借用原文：deserves attention Section C 1 The most common question I'm asked always centers around how to get started in user experience design, to which my response is always that nothing can substitute real-world experience. 我被问到的最常见问题总是围绕如何开始从事用户体验设计，对此我的回答始终是，没有什么能替代真实 世界的经验。 2 Building the skills required of a user experience designer takes time, patience, and commitment. Higher education is a great way to equip yourself with some core skills, but it will not prepare you for actual challenges you'll face with clients' work. In other words, being proficient with a design tool and a few methods doesn't make you a user experience designer. There simply isn't a one-size-fits-all process. 培养用户体验设计师所需的技能需要时间、耐心和投入。高等教育是让你具备一些核心技能的好方法,但它 不会让你为客户工作中将面临的实际挑战做好准备。换句话说,精通一个设计工具和几种方法并不能让你成 为用户体验设计师。根本不存在一个放之四海而皆准的流程。 3 Being effective requires adaptability — something you don't really learn in school, much less in a 6- month training camp. It's gained through experience on the job and learning what's appropriate given the needs of the project. 要做到有效需要适应能力——这是你在学校里真正学不到的,更不用说在6个月的培训营中了。它是通过工 作中的经验获得的,并学会根据项目需求选择合适的方法。 4 I found my way to user experience through graphic design and slowly over many different roles and experiences. That led me to become a user experience designer. It took time and commitment to continue Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard. to pursue roles within teams that I knew could teach and challenge me. That's not to say that I think my path is the only one. But once again, nothing can substitute real-world experience. You can start anywhere as long as you know your end goal and you commit to actively pursuing opportunities to learn and grow along the way. 我通过平面设计找到了进入用户体验的道路,并在许多不同的角色和经历中慢慢成长。这让我成为了一名用 户体验设计师。这需要时间和投入来持续追求那些我知道能教导和挑战我的团队中的角色。这并不是说我 认为我的道路是唯一的。但再次强调,没有什么能替代真实世界的经验。只要你知道自己的最终目标,并致 力于积极寻求学习和成长的机会,你可以从任何地方开始。

optionsZh: 它给许多航空公司造成了重大损失。
它对女性旅客的影响更严重。
它长期以来被许多专家忽视。
它影响百分之二十五的人。
options: It has caused heavy losses to many airlines.
It impacts female travelers more seriously.
It has long been ignored by many experts.
It affects twenty-five percent of people.

questions.stem: What does the speaker think is the best way to get started in user experience design?
questions.stemZh: 演讲者认为入门用户体验设计的最佳方式是什么?

explain.定位: The most common question I'm asked always centers around how to get started in user experience design, to which my response is always that nothing can substitute real- world experience. 别人最常问我的问题总是围绕怎么入门用户体验设计，对此我的回答始终是：没有什么能替 代真实世界的经验。
explain.信号: nothing can substitute抬高某项。答案信号是这句里的 nothing can substitute real- world experience（没有什么能替代真实世界的经验）——nothing can substitute 是把 某一项捧到唯一、最高位置的强调说法，凡听到这种把别的全比下去的句式，那句就是答 案句。
explain.替换: nothing can substitute real-world experience ↔Obtaining real-world experience. 唯一不可替代等于最佳
explain.排除: A) 未提及 Learning from skilled designers. 听起来很合理，但录音通篇没说过要向熟练的设计师 学，它是凭常识脑补的入门方式，原文无对应。 C) 原词陷阱 Joining a 6-month training camp. 盗用了录音第三段的原词 6-month training camp， 但原文是把训练营当成学不到适应力的反面例子来说的，并非入门的最佳方式，属于听到原 词就想选的陷阱。 借用原文：much less in a 6-month training camp D) 原词陷阱 Anticipating actual challenges. 借用了第二段原词 actual challenges，但原文说的是高等 教育无法让你为真实挑战做好准备，并没说入门的最佳方式是去预判挑战，选项把原词搬过 来又改了意思。 借用原文：it will not prepare you for actual challenges you'll face

optionsZh: 向熟练的设计师学习。
获得真实世界的经验。
参加为期6个月的培训营。
预见实际挑战。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say being effective requires?
questions.stemZh: 演讲者说要有效需要什么?

explain.定位: Being effective requires adaptability — something you don't really learn in school, much less in a 6-month training camp. 要做到有效就需要适应力——这是你在学校里学不太到的东西，在六个月的训练营里就更别 提了。
explain.信号: requires直接点出条件。答案信号就是题干原话在录音里几乎复现：Being effective requires adaptability，requires 后面紧跟的 adaptability 就是被点名的条件。这种题干和 原文几乎同形、只差答案词的句子，是最直接的答案句信号。
explain.替换: Being effective requires adaptability ↔Adaptability. 原词同形直接对应
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 Core skills. 盗用了第二段原词 core skills，但原文说的是高等教育能帮你装备一些核心技 能、随后却话锋一转说它不够，core skills 并不是 being effective 所需要的那样东西，属 听到原词就想选的陷阱。 借用原文：Higher education is a great way to equip yourself with some core skills B) 原词陷阱 Higher education. 盗用第二段原词 Higher education，但原文说高等教育不能让你应对 真实挑战、是被往下压的一项，根本不是 being effective 所需，听到这个原词就选会掉 坑。 借用原文：but it will not prepare you for actual challenges D) 未提及 Capability. 和正确项 Adaptability. 一样以 -ability 结尾、长得像，是专为只听个相似尾音 的考生设的形近干扰，但录音从没说 being effective 需要 capability。

optionsZh: 核心技能。
高等教育。
适应能力。
能力。

questions.stem: What can people do as long as they know their end goal and strive for it?
questions.stemZh: 只要人们知道自己的最终目标并为之努力,他们能做什么?

explain.定位: You can start anywhere as long as you know your end goal and you commit to actively pursuing opportunities to learn and grow along the way. 只要你清楚自己的终极目标，并且愿意一路上主动去追寻学习和成长的机会，你可以从任何 地方起步。
explain.信号: as long as条件句的主句。答案信号是这句的结构 You can start anywhere as long as you know your end goal——as long as 是题干照搬的条件信号词，它前面的主句 You can start anywhere 就是回答能做什么的部分，条件句的主句才是答案落点。
explain.替换: You can start anywhere ↔Start anywhere. 主句原话浓缩为动词短语
explain.排除: B) 原词陷阱 Face challenges. 里的 challenges 来自前文（如第二段说的 actual challenges、第四段说 团队能 challenge me），但 as long as 那句答案句里说的是 start anywhere，不是面对 挑战，选项搬了别处的原词来凑。 借用原文：roles within teams that I knew could teach and challenge me C) 张冠李戴 Pursue roles in teams. 盗用第四段原词 pursue roles within teams，但那是作者讲自己当 年的经历（他自己去团队里求角色），不是回答只要知道目标就能做什么，属张冠李戴式的 原词陷阱。 借用原文：to continue to pursue roles within teams that I knew could teach and challenge me D) 与原文相反 Follow their own path. 借用第四段 my path 的说法，但原文是作者说我不认为自己这条 路是唯一的，恰恰是不主张人人照走他的路，选项却说去走自己的路，与原文倾向相反。 借用原文：That's not to say that I think my path is the only one. 1 When planning for this year, our principal asked what needed to change to engage students more in their learning. I responded in a whisper "flexible seating", thinking about our then-current classroom. It had rows of desks with blue chairs and nameplates reminding each student where they should be sitting. 在规划今年的工作时,我们的校长问需要改变什么才能让学生更多地参与到学习中来。我小声回答"灵活座 位",同时想到我们当时的教室。教室里一排排课桌配着蓝色椅子,桌上的姓名牌提醒着每个学生应该坐在 哪里。 2 This began a journey to transform our practice and challenge the ways of learning for a group of Year 6 students used to sitting in desks and rows for years. 这开启了一段转变我们教学实践的旅程,并挑战了一群习惯于多年坐在课桌排列教室里的六年级学生的学习 方式。 3 Flexible seating has been defined as movable furniture to create an engaging learning environment. It is a shift in practice from being teacher-focused to student-focused learning. For us, flexible seating has meant removing most of the traditional chairs and desks and introducing a variety of different seating options to promote student engagement. 灵活座位被定义为可移动的家具,用以创造一个富有吸引力的学习环境。它是从以教师为中心向以学生为中 心学习的实践转变。对我们而言,灵活座位意味着移除大部分传统的椅子和课桌,引入各种不同的座位选择 来促进学生参与。 4 The use of rows and their minimal adaptations to "U" shape were traditionally intended to maximize on-task behavior and reduce distraction from the teacher. Teachers tend to still use this format because Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard. of either the need to control students or the belief that the teacher is the most important person in the room. 使用排列及其向"U"形的最小调整,传统上旨在最大化专注行为并减少对教师的干扰。教师倾向于仍然使用 这种形式,原因要么是需要控制学生,要么是认为教师是教室里最重要的人。 5 Now our students have a range of different seating options, including a floor desk, couches, stools, bean bags, and the traditional desk-and-chair. 现在我们的学生有一系列不同的座位选择,包括地板书桌、沙发、凳子、豆袋椅以及传统的课桌椅。 6 From our experience so far, flexible seating enhances student ownership of space and engagement in learning, while reducing rates of student disengagement and disciplinary actions. It is a win for all concerned. 根据我们迄今为止的经验,灵活座位增强了学生对空间的所有权和学习参与度,同时降低了学生脱离学习和 纪律处分的比率。这对所有相关方来说都是双赢。

optionsZh: 从任何地方开始。
面对挑战。
在团队中追求角色。
遵循自己的道路。

questions.stem: Why did the school principal ask what needed to change?
questions.stemZh: 校长为什么要问需要改变什么？
questions.answerText: To engage students more in their learning.

explain.定位: When planning for this year, our principal asked what needed to change to engage students more in their learning. 在筹划今年的工作时，我们校长问需要改变什么，好让学生更投入到自己的学习中。
explain.信号: 目的状语 to engage… 直接给出动机。句中 to engage students more in their learning 是"为了…"的目的状语，紧跟在校长发问之后，正是他发问的目的所在，是这句成为答案句 的信号。
explain.替换: to engage students more in their learning ↔To engage students more in their learning. 几乎原句搬到选项
explain.排除: A) 未提及 选项说"主动回应学生的请求"，但录音里是校长主动发问、要让学生更投入，没有"回应学生 请求"一说，方向不符。 C) 原词陷阱 选项把焦点说成"让老师与学生更多互动"，盗用了录音反复出现的 teachers、students，但 校长的目的是让"学生"更投入学习，不是促进师生互动，偷换了主体与重点。 借用原文：to engage students more in their learning D) 过度推断 选项说"给学生更多学业自由"，录音目的句只讲 engage（投入），从未提 freedom（自 由），是把投入度过度引申成自由度。

optionsZh: 积极回应学生的要求。
让学生更多地参与到学习中。
使教师能够更多地与学生互动。
让学生在学业上拥有更多自由。
options: To respond actively to students' requests.
To engage students more in their learning.
To enable teachers to interact more with their students.
To allow students more freedom in their academic work.

questions.stem: What has flexible seating meant at the speaker's school?
questions.stemZh: 灵活座位在说话者的学校意味着什么？
questions.answerText: Adopting a variety of different seating options.

explain.定位: For us, flexible seating has meant removing most of the traditional chairs and desks and introducing a variety of different seating options to promote student engagement. 对我们来说，灵活座位意味着撤掉大部分传统桌椅，引入多种不同的座位选择，以促进学生 投入。
explain.信号: 下定义信号 has meant。句中 flexible seating has meant 是"在本校它意味着什么"的下 定义信号，与题干 has meant 完全对应，定义内容紧随其后，是答案句的标志。
explain.替换: introducing a variety of different seating options ↔ Adopting a variety of different seating options. introducing 与 Adopting 同义替换
explain.排除: A) 未提及 选项说"用新家具营造舒适环境"，录音定义句讲的是 promote student engagement（促 进投入），从未提 comfortable（舒适），属凭空添加。 B) 偷换概念 选项说"从传统教学转向任务式学习"，录音只说从 teacher-focused 转向 student- focused，并未出现 task-based learning（任务式学习）这一说法，偷换了概念。 借用原文：a shift in practice from being teacher-focused to student-focused learning D) 原词陷阱 选项"重排大部分传统桌椅"盗用了录音的 traditional chairs and desks，但录音是 removing（撤掉）这些桌椅再引入多样座位，不是 Rearranging（重排），只截了动作的 一半且改了动词。 借用原文：removing most of the traditional chairs and desks

optionsZh: 使用新家具营造舒适的环境。
从传统教学转向基于任务的学习。
采用多种不同的座位选择。
重新摆放大部分传统的椅子和课桌。
options: Using new furniture to create a comfortable environment.
Shifting from traditional teaching to task-based learning.
Adopting a variety of different seating options.
Rearranging most traditional chairs and desks.

questions.stem: What has flexible seating brought about at the speaker's school?
questions.stemZh: 灵活座位在说话者的学校带来了什么？
questions.answerText: A win for all people involved.

explain.定位: From our experience so far, flexible seating enhances student ownership of space and engagement in learning, while reducing rates of student disengagement and disciplinary actions. It is a win for all concerned. 从我们目前的经验看，灵活座位增强了学生对空间的归属感和学习投入，同时降低了学生的 脱离感和纪律处分的发生率。这对所有相关方都是一种共赢。
explain.信号: 结尾总结句 It is a win for all concerned。末段 It is a win for all concerned 是带总结 语气的收束句，把前面列举的好处一句话归纳为"对所有人都是共赢"，是结果题最该锁的 落点。
explain.替换: It is a win for all concerned ↔A win for all people involved. all concerned 与 all people involved 同义
explain.排除: B) 原词陷阱 选项说"纪律效果增强"，盗用录音的 disciplinary，但录音是 reducing…disciplinary actions（减少纪律处分），方向相反；且只取纪律一项，丢了"共赢"的全面性。 借用原文：reducing rates of student disengagement and disciplinary actions C) 原词陷阱 选项说"学生之间关系融洽"，盗用了高频词 students，但录音讲的是学生对空间的归属感与 投入，从未提学生彼此之间的 harmonious relationship（融洽关系）。 借用原文：enhances student ownership of space and engagement in learning D) 未提及 选项说"改变了老师对学生的看法"，录音末段只讲对学生投入、纪律的成效与"共赢"，并未 提到老师对学生看法的任何改变。 1 Dozens of British students arriving for their first day of school on Tuesday were sent home over their shoes. About 30 students were turned away from Taverham High School in Norfolk, England. Headteacher, Dr Roger Harris, confirmed that this was due to a change in the school's uniform policy. Harris, who became headteacher this year, said he notified parents of the updated rules in an email in June. 周二,数十名英国学生因鞋子问题在开学第一天被遣返回家。英格兰诺福克郡Taverham高中约有30名学生 被拒之门外。校长Roger Harris博士证实,这是由于学校校服政策的变化。今年新上任的Harris表示,他在6 月份通过电子邮件通知了家长更新后的规定。 2 The price of school uniforms can spark panic among families struggling with the high cost of living. Nearly all British schools have uniforms. They cost parents an average of £337 per year for each secondary school child. 校服价格可能让那些苦于高昂生活成本的家庭感到恐慌。几乎所有英国学校都有校服。家长平均每年为每 个中学生支付337英镑的校服费用。 3 According to the new rules, students of Taverham are required to wear smart black shoes appropriate for the workplace, Harris held that strengthened rules around school uniforms improved student outcomes and behavior. But for some parents, the school's restrictions are an unnecessary burden. 根据新规定,Taverham的学生必须穿适合职场的得体黑色鞋子。Harris认为,加强校服规定能改善学生的学 业成绩和行为表现。但对一些家长来说,学校的限制是不必要的负担。 4 As annual inflation climbs over 10%, many households are on tight budgets. Private rental prices in Britain rose 3.2% over the 12 months to July 2022, the largest jump since 2016. Soaring energy bills have made things worse. 随着年通胀率攀升至10%以上,许多家庭的预算都很紧张。截至2022年7月的12个月里,英国私人租房价格 上涨了3.2%,这是自2016年以来的最大涨幅。飙升的能源账单使情况更加恶化。 5 Lucinda May, mum of a Taverham student, said that she had to ask her parents for £65 to buy her child the correct pair of shoes. May said that the school's uniform policy showed the lack of regard for Questions 22 to 25 are based on the passage you have just heard. parents dealing with the high cost of living. Taverham学生家长Lucinda May说,她不得不向父母要65英镑给孩子买一双符合规定的鞋子。May表示, 学校的校服政策显示出对正在应对高昂生活成本的家长缺乏关照。

optionsZh: 对所有相关人员都有益。
加强了纪律效果。
学生之间关系和谐。
改变了教师对学生的看法。
options: A win for all people involved.
A strengthened effect of its discipline.
A harmonious relationship among its students.
A change to teachers' opinion of their students.

questions.stem: Why were dozens of British students sent home on Tuesday?
questions.stemZh: 为什么数十名英国学生在周二被送回家？
questions.answerText: They didn't wear the shoes required by the school's new policy.

explain.定位: About 30 students were turned away from Taverham High School in Norfolk, England. Headteacher, Dr Roger Harris, confirmed that this was due to a change in the school's uniform policy. 大约 30 名学生被英格兰诺福克的 Taverham 高中拒之门外。校长 Roger Harris 博士确 认，这是由于学校校服政策的一项变动。
explain.信号: 因果信号 due to。答案句里 this was due to a change in the school's uniform policy 的 "due to" 是明确的因果信号，它后面跟的"校服政策变动"就是被送回家的原因，正是 Why 题要抓的落点。
explain.替换: a change in the school's uniform policy ↔the shoes required by the school's new policy 概括换具体加同义改写
explain.排除: A) 选项说学生"没被告知更新的规定"，但录音里校长明确说 he notified parents of the updated rules in an email in June——是已经通知过的，选项把"通知过"反说成"没被告 知"，方向相反。 借用原文：he notified parents of the updated rules in an email in June B) 录音只说这天是 their first day of school on Tuesday，提到了"开学第一天"，但从未说学 生"迟到"；选项盗用了"first day"的时间背景，把原因编成"迟到"，原文没有依据。 C) 原词陷阱 录音提到校长是用 in an email in June 通知家长的，选项盗用"email"这个原词，编出"以 不礼貌方式回复校长邮件"；原文只说校长发邮件通知，根本没说学生回邮件、更没说态度 不礼貌。 借用原文：he notified parents of the updated rules in an email in June

optionsZh: 他们没有被告知学校更新的规定。
他们在开学第一天迟到了。
他们以不礼貌的方式回复了校长的电子邮件。
他们没有穿学校新政策要求的鞋子。
options: They weren't informed of the school's updated rules.
They arrived late for their first day of school.
They answered their headteacher's email in an impolite way.
They didn't wear the shoes required by the school's new policy.

questions.stem: What can the price of school uniforms spark among families in financial difficulty?
questions.stemZh: 校服的价格会在经济困难的家庭中引发什么？

explain.定位: The price of school uniforms can spark panic among families struggling with the high cost of living. 校服的价格会在那些在高生活成本中苦苦挣扎的家庭里激起恐慌。
explain.信号: 题干原词 spark 几乎原句重现。答案句 The price of school uniforms can spark panic among families 与题干用词高度重合（price/spark/families），spark 紧跟的那个词 panic 就是被引发的反应，是定位信号。
explain.替换: spark panic among families ↔Panic. 原词直接对应
explain.排除: A) Riots（骚乱）程度最重、最抓耳，但录音里从未出现"骚乱"；它是把"恐慌"夸大成"骚乱"的 诱饵，原文无依据。 B) Anger（愤怒）听上去和"家长有意见"很搭，但原文 spark 后面接的是 panic 不是 anger； anger 是个貌似合理却没被念到的情绪词。 C) Disputes（争执/纠纷）也是一种貌似合理的负面反应，但原文激起的是 panic，并未提 到"争执"，属没被念到的干扰项。

optionsZh: 骚乱。
愤怒。
争议。
恐慌。

questions.stem: What did the headteacher think of the school's new uniform rules?
questions.stemZh: 校长如何看待学校的新校服规定？
questions.answerText: They improved student behavior and performance.

explain.定位: Harris held that strengthened rules around school uniforms improved student outcomes and behavior. Harris 认为，更严格的校服规定改善了学生的成绩和行为。
explain.信号: 观点引导词 held that。答案句 Harris held that strengthened rules around school uniforms improved student outcomes and behavior 里的 "held that"（认为）是明确 的观点信号，引出的正是校长本人的看法，是态度题的落点。
explain.替换: improved student outcomes and behavior ↔improved student behavior and performance 同义词替换
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 录音里有 strengthened rules around school uniforms，"strengthened" 这个词真的念 到了；选项 strengthened the school's discipline and order 盗用 strengthened，但把 它的对象换成"纪律和秩序"——原文是"更严格的规定改善了成绩和行为"，strengthened 修饰的是 rules 而非 discipline，张冠李戴。 借用原文：strengthened rules around school uniforms improved student outcomes and behavior C) "提升学校的正面形象"（positive image）听起来是个合理好处，但校长说的是改善"成绩和 行为"，从未提到"形象"，原文无依据。 D) 录音第 4 段出现过 Private rental prices in Britain 等带 district/地区背景的经济描述（原 文用 households/Britain），选项 rendered the school unique in the district 借"地 区"这类背景感造出"让学校在本区独一无二"，但校长的观点里根本没说学校"独特"，属编 造。

optionsZh: 它们加强了学校的纪律和秩序。
它们改善了学生的行为和表现。
它们提升了学校的正面形象。
它们使学校在该地区独树一帜。
options: They strengthened the school's discipline and order.
They improved student behavior and performance.
They enhanced the positive image of the school.
They rendered the school unique in the district.

questions.stem: What did Lucinda May have to do to buy her child the correct pair of shoes?
questions.stemZh: Lucinda May为了给孩子买到正确的鞋子必须做什么？
questions.answerText: Turn to her parents for help.

explain.定位: Lucinda May, mum of a Taverham student, said that she had to ask her parents for £65 to buy her child the correct pair of shoes. Taverham 一名学生的母亲 Lucinda May 说，她不得不向自己的父母要 65 英镑，来给孩子 买那双符合要求的鞋。
explain.信号: 被问者的直接动作 had to ask。答案句 she had to ask her parents for £65 to buy her child the correct pair of shoes 里的 "had to ask" 正是题干问的"不得不做的动作"，her parents 点明动作对象，是定位信号。
explain.替换: ask her parents for £65 ↔Turn to her parents for help 同义短语 + 概括化
explain.排除: B) "缩紧月度预算"和第 4 段 many households are on tight budgets 的 "tight budgets" 背 景相呼应，但那是说大环境下家庭预算紧，并非 May 本人"缩预算"这个动作；她的实际做 法是向父母要钱。 借用原文：many households are on tight budgets C) 偷换概念 金额 £65 是原文真念到的（ask her parents for £65），选项 Borrow £65 from her friend. 保住了对的金额却把对象从"her parents"偷换成"her friend"，动作也 从"ask"变"borrow"，对象错了。 借用原文：she had to ask her parents for £65 D) "推迟支付其他账单"和第 4 段 Soaring energy bills have made things worse. 里的 bills 沾边，但原文只说能源账单让情况更糟，从没说 May"推迟付账单"；这是借 bills 一词编出 的动作。 For anyone who wants to help make this year's Games a massive success, there are still opportunities to volunteer for Fayetteville's Special Olympics. 第3段，第1句 there be 存在句 + 定语从句修饰介词宾语的组合，是四六级和考研阅读中的常见句式。句首长状 语 + 主句的布局也是典型的书面语结构，学习者掌握后可迁移到大量类似句子的分析中。 Organizers encourage them to visit the Games' explain.词性槽: the ___ of the world：定冠词 + 空 + of，典型名词位
explain.依据: the rest of the world：固定搭配，指"世界其余地方" 本句对比的是"美国（the United States）"和"世界其他地方"两部分——Earth Day is celebrated on April 22 in the United States and on either April 22 or the day the spring equinox(春分) occurs throughout the __(26)__ of the world. "the rest of the world"（世界其余地方）正是这种二分对照的固定表达，语义和搭配双双吻合。
explain.竞争词: A) concerns concerns of the world 语义错位 concerns 意为"关切事项"，"the concerns of the world"指"世界的关切问题"，与本句"在世界 其余地方庆祝"的地理范围语义完全不搭。 B) expansion expansion 指"扩张"，与对比语境不合 the expansion of the world 意为"世界的扩张"，原文要表达的是"美国 vs 世界其他地方"的地 域对比，扩张没有对照含义，不通。 D) geography geography 偏"地理学/地形"，不指"其余地区" the geography of the world 通常指"世界的地理（地形地貌）"，强调地理特征，无法承担"美 国以外的其他地方"这层"其余"含义。 E) importance importance 是抽象"重要性"，与地点状语冲突 the importance of the world 意为"世界的重要性"，但本句是 throughout 引导的地点范围状 语，需要的是"地方"概念，importance 完全跑题。 I) partners partners 复数指"合作伙伴们"，与 the…of the world 不搭 the partners of the world 不是一个自然搭配，且 throughout "遍及"后接的是地理范围、不是 人群。 J) potential potential 指"潜力"，不能承载"地方"语义 the potential of the world 意为"世界的潜力"，与 throughout 表达"在……各地"的地点范围意 义不一致。 L) rescues rescues 指"救援"，与本句话题彻底无关 the rescues of the world"世界的救援"在本句完全无依据，地球日叙述中并未涉及救援行动。

questions.passage: Earth Day is an annual celebration that honors the achievements of the environmental movement and raises awareness of the need to protect Earth's natural resources for future generations. Earth Day is celebrated on April 22 in the United States and on either April 22 or the day the spring equinox(春分) occurs throughout the (26)______  of the world. Environmental activism during the 1960s  (27)______ Wisconsin Senator Gaylord Nelson to create a  (28)______ celebration uniting the environmental movement. With the help of Denis Hayes, a graduate student at Harvard University, Nelson organized the first Earth Day on April 22, 1970, educating participants in the (29)______  of environmental protection. Attended by 20 million people across the United States, the event (30)______  support for legislation such as the Clean Air Act and the Endangered Species Act. In 1990, Hayes organized a global Earth Day, with more than 200 million participants in 140 countries. Earth Day now brings  (31)______ citizens and activists from around the world to raise awareness and take action regarding such environmental (32)______  as global warming and renewable energy. Today, the Earth Day Network, which rallies more than 20,000 (33)______  and organizations in 190 countries, supports the Earth Day mission year-round. This mission is founded on the proposition that all people, regardless of race, gender, income, or (34)______  , have a moral right to a healthy, sustainable environment. The Earth Day Network  (35)______ this mission through education, public policy, and activism campaigns.

explain.词性槽: Environmental activism … ___ Wisconsin Senator … to create：主语后缺谓语，需谓 语动词
explain.依据: inspire sb to do sth：激励某人去做某事 Environmental activism during the 1960s __(27)__ Wisconsin Senator Gaylord Nelson to create a national celebration uniting the environmental movement.——"20 世纪 60 年代的环保运动激励参议员去创立一场全国性的环保庆典"，inspire sb to do 是英语里 表"激发某人做某事"的高频固定搭配，过去式 inspired 也与下文 1970 年时间线一致。
explain.竞争词: F) imposed impose 不能直接跟 sb to do 结构 impose 意为"强加（义务/税收/规定）"，典型结构是 impose sth on sb，无法直接构成 imposed sb to do；语义上也偏"强迫"，与"环保运动激励议员"的正面叙述色彩相反。 K) pursues pursues 时态错 + 搭配错 pursues 是一般现在时第三人称单数，本句叙述 1960 年代的过去事件，时态不匹配；且 pursue 后通常接"目标/事业"等宾语，不接"sb to do"。
explain.易错: 最具迷惑性的错误词是 F) —— imposed 时态对但结构错。Environmental activism during the 1960s __(27)__ Wisconsin Senator Gaylord Nelson to create 极易因 imposed 与 inspired 都是过去式而二选一卡壳；防坑要诀：impose 不接 sb to do（典 型是 impose sth on sb），inspire 才有 inspire sb to do sth 的固定结构——记住搭配是 关键。

questions.stem: Hiring managers believe unemployed workers over 45 lack good skills and are less adaptable.
questions.stemZh: 招聘经理认为45岁以上的失业者缺乏良好的技能且适应能力较差。
questions.anchor: 技能差+适应力低

explain.定位: Hiring managers have a strong perception bias against 45+ job candidates — they believe that members of this age group have poor skills and low adaptability 招聘经理对 45 岁以上的求职者抱有强烈的偏见——他们认为这一年龄群体的成员技能差、 适应力低。
explain.改写: lack good skills ↔poor skills 反向短语+名词化的同义替换 less adaptable ↔low adaptability 形容词比较级↔抽象名词
explain.辨邻: F 段 F Managers said they worry that older hires will be reluctant to try new technologies, and will be unable to learn new skills. 只覆盖"学技能"一面，未提及 less adaptable 对应的"低适应力"评价，属典型的"只覆盖局部"。 Managers said they worry that older hires will be reluctant to try new technologies, and will be unable to learn new skills. 转换到新职业是困难的,而在裁员后重新就业则更加艰难。

questions.passage:
A) Ageism and long-term unemployment are most damaging for those in the second half of their careers. Changing careers is hard. Getting back into work after you've been laid off is even harder. Those over 45 make up the bulk of the long-term unemployed, in America and elsewhere. Hiring managers admit they are reluctant to hire those over 40 or 45, arguing they probably won't be a good "fit," their experience won't be relevant to the workplace, and they'll be unable or unwilling to learn new skills.
B) But the one thing that can really make a difference? More education and training. These are the results from a new study by Generation, a nonprofit founded by former McKinsey consultants. They've just published a global survey on midcareer employment, based on surveys of over 5,000 workers and managers in seven countries.
C) "Older midcareer workers … make up the bulk of the long-term unemployed in many countries," Generation's analysts write in their report. Those over 45 comprise over 40% of the long-term unemployed, for example. And if you're out of work past the age of 45, there's nearly a two in three chance you'll be out of work for over a year, they find. "Midcareer individuals are finding it harder to get jobs," they write. "People age 45+ face persistent and rising pressure in the global job market. They are unemployed for much longer than the average, and their age is indeed one of the greatest barriers to their finding a job."
D) A substantial part of this, they report, is "widespread ageism" on the part of hiring managers. Although such managers admit that post-45 hires turn out on average to be just as good as or better than younger workers, they still don't want to hire them. "Hiring managers have a strong perception bias against 45+ job candidates — they believe that members of this age group have poor skills and low adaptability," Generation's analysts report.
E) The survey results are remarkable. Hiring managers are three times as likely to rate job applicants age 35 – 44 as a better "fit" than those over 45. They rate the post-45 job seekers lower on average on all three measures — even experience — than those ages 18 to 34. This is true even though nearly nine managers in 10 also said their post-45 workers were as good as or better than younger employees in the same jobs.
F) Their biggest fears about hiring those over 45? Managers said they worry that older hires will be reluctant to try new technologies, and will be unable to learn new skills. Besides, the majority of hiring managers are under 45 — and seem reluctant to hire people older than themselves.
G) But here's the good news. Older workers who've actively engaged in more education and training relevant to their jobs turn this pretty much on its head. Three-quarters of hiring managers said they'd be more likely to hire an over-45 who had relevant education, training or credentials(文凭). Among those over 45 who'd successfully switched careers, 74% said training helped them get their new job.
H) "Midcareer switchers overwhelmingly say that training enabled them to shift to a new career path," the analysts write. And when they asked over-45 candidates about their attitudes, they found that "those who are excited by training are unemployed for less time, receive more job offers, and are more satisfied by the job offers they receive."
I) Hiring managers said training was three times more likely to get them to hire applicants over age 45 than, say, government subsidies(补贴). What training are we talking about? Obviously it depends on the job. And, yes, managers are most likely to be impressed by industry qualifications you get in school. These things cost money, and time. But these aren't the only things helpful. Those who had successfully changed careers after 45 told Generation that education and training had been a big help — and that included in-person, on-the-job training, "informal learning," and online courses — with or without certification.
J) If they think we're too old to learn new skills after we're 45, just learning some new skills may have an effect on its own. There's a downside to this. The people least interested in retraining are more likely to come from historically disadvantaged communities, more likely to have low incomes, and are more likely to have the least schooling after getting their high-school diploma or earlier. On average, post-45 job switchers with higher incomes participate in 2.5 training programs each. Those with lower incomes: 0.9 programs on average.
K) Many years ago, I wrote about a study which found that employers are much more likely to hire a college graduate who has some work experience in the industry than a college graduate who took the "right" degree. A bank is more likely to hire a literature graduate who spent their summers working in their local bank than a finance or economics graduate who spent their summers surfing or traveling around Italy. They've learned through long experience. The person who worked in the bank is more likely ready, willing and able to be part of the team and do the job from day 1.
L) We can rail against "ageism" all we like. It gets us nowhere. And it's easy to forget that employers, like everyone else, are under time pressure and are just trying to solve problems. Any and all "training," including inexpensive and informal training, is going to help resolve their worries about hiring someone over 45. And it has never been easier or cheaper to gain instruction in new skills,
M) Bottom line? Yes, it really can be difficult getting a new job after age 45, let alone changing careers. One of the best things we can do to help ourselves is to go online and learn new, relevant skills. Sadly, the people who most need the help are least likely to take it — which raises a challenge for society as a whole. Not only do we not want to see lives go to waste, but we all benefit if more people are working and fewer are unemployed.

A) Ageism and long-term unemployment are most damaging for those in the second half of their careers. Changing careers is hard. Getting back into work after you've been laid off is even harder. Those over 45 make up the bulk of the long-term unemployed, in America and elsewhere. Hiring managers admit they are reluctant to hire those over 40 or 45, arguing they probably won't be a good "fit," their experience won't be relevant to the workplace, and they'll be unable or unwilling to learn new skills.
B) But the one thing that can really make a difference? More education and training. These are the results from a new study by Generation, a nonprofit founded by former McKinsey consultants. They've just published a global survey on midcareer employment, based on surveys of over 5,000 workers and managers in seven countries.
C) "Older midcareer workers … make up the bulk of the long-term unemployed in many countries," Generation's analysts write in their report. Those over 45 comprise over 40% of the long-term unemployed, for example. And if you're out of work past the age of 45, there's nearly a two in three chance you'll be out of work for over a year, they find. "Midcareer individuals are finding it harder to get jobs," they write. "People age 45+ face persistent and rising pressure in the global job market. They are unemployed for much longer than the average, and their age is indeed one of the greatest barriers to their finding a job."
D) A substantial part of this, they report, is "widespread ageism" on the part of hiring managers. Although such managers admit that post-45 hires turn out on average to be just as good as or better than younger workers, they still don't want to hire them. "Hiring managers have a strong perception bias against 45+ job candidates — they believe that members of this age group have poor skills and low adaptability," Generation's analysts report.
E) The survey results are remarkable. Hiring managers are three times as likely to rate job applicants age 35 – 44 as a better "fit" than those over 45. They rate the post-45 job seekers lower on average on all three measures — even experience — than those ages 18 to 34. This is true even though nearly nine managers in 10 also said their post-45 workers were as good as or better than younger employees in the same jobs.
F) Their biggest fears about hiring those over 45? Managers said they worry that older hires will be reluctant to try new technologies, and will be unable to learn new skills. Besides, the majority of hiring managers are under 45 — and seem reluctant to hire people older than themselves.
G) But here's the good news. Older workers who've actively engaged in more education and training relevant to their jobs turn this pretty much on its head. Three-quarters of hiring managers said they'd be more likely to hire an over-45 who had relevant education, training or credentials(文凭). Among those over 45 who'd successfully switched careers, 74% said training helped them get their new job.
H) "Midcareer switchers overwhelmingly say that training enabled them to shift to a new career path," the analysts write. And when they asked over-45 candidates about their attitudes, they found that "those who are excited by training are unemployed for less time, receive more job offers, and are more satisfied by the job offers they receive."
I) Hiring managers said training was three times more likely to get them to hire applicants over age 45 than, say, government subsidies(补贴). What training are we talking about? Obviously it depends on the job. And, yes, managers are most likely to be impressed by industry qualifications you get in school. These things cost money, and time. But these aren't the only things helpful. Those who had successfully changed careers after 45 told Generation that education and training had been a big help — and that included in-person, on-the-job training, "informal learning," and online courses — with or without certification.
J) If they think we're too old to learn new skills after we're 45, just learning some new skills may have an effect on its own. There's a downside to this. The people least interested in retraining are more likely to come from historically disadvantaged communities, more likely to have low incomes, and are more likely to have the least schooling after getting their high-school diploma or earlier. On average, post-45 job switchers with higher incomes participate in 2.5 training programs each. Those with lower incomes: 0.9 programs on average.
K) Many years ago, I wrote about a study which found that employers are much more likely to hire a college graduate who has some work experience in the industry than a college graduate who took the "right" degree. A bank is more likely to hire a literature graduate who spent their summers working in their local bank than a finance or economics graduate who spent their summers surfing or traveling around Italy. They've learned through long experience. The person who worked in the bank is more likely ready, willing and able to be part of the team and do the job from day 1.
L) We can rail against "ageism" all we like. It gets us nowhere. And it's easy to forget that employers, like everyone else, are under time pressure and are just trying to solve problems. Any and all "training," including inexpensive and informal training, is going to help resolve their worries about hiring someone over 45. And it has never been easier or cheaper to gain instruction in new skills,
M) Bottom line? Yes, it really can be difficult getting a new job after age 45, let alone changing careers. One of the best things we can do to help ourselves is to go online and learn new, relevant skills. Sadly, the people who most need the help are least likely to take it — which raises a challenge for society as a whole. Not only do we not want to see lives go to waste, but we all benefit if more people are working and fewer are unemployed.

questions.passage:
P1 New York's Eleven Madison Park has become the first vegan( 素食主义的) restaurant to be awarded three Michelin stars.

P2 The fine dining establishment received its first three-star Michelin rating in 2011 when the menu was famed for its fancy animal-based dishes.

P3 However, last year, the restaurant's co-owner and famous chef, Daniel Humm, made the bold decision to remove meat from the menu, citing our unsustainable food system. While cow milk is still served for tea and coffee, the menu is almost 100 percent vegan.

P4 At the time, Humm acknowledged the move was risky, admitting that "it wasn't clear if guests would come", but called the gamble "a risk worth taking."

P5 "In view of the climate crisis, I didn't want to open the same restaurant," Humm told the Financial Times in an interview. "If we can show the possibilities of eating plant-based food in this setting, it can open a lot of doors" for others to follow.

P6 Now, this impressive new accomplishment validates Eleven Madison Park's decision to take meat off the menu and embrace plant-based foods, with Michelin's 2022 New York guide branding it 'a bold vision of luxury dining'.

P7 "We took the jump to transform Eleven Madison Park into a plant-based fine dining restaurant knowing in our hearts this is what we believed in," stated Humm on Instagram. "Last night, we were honored to be awarded three Michelin stars for the 11th year in a row. I am so grateful to the team members who contributed through its nearly 25-year history. We are also grateful to our guests and partners who believed in our vision and encouraged us to push harder."

P8 Three Michelin stars is the highest award, given to chefs who are at the peak of their profession. "Their cooking is elevated to an art form and some of their dishes are destined to become classics," reads Michelin's website, in a clear nod to plant-based foods' growing significance in the culinary(烹饪的) world.

P9 "I think luxury companies have a real role to play and a responsibility," says Humm. "The more creative we are, the more beautiful and delicious our future will be."
