questions.passage:
P1 With genetic testing becoming increasingly popular, many people are left wondering exactly how accurate it is. Whether you are taking a DNA test to build your extended DNA family tree, or want precise information on inborn( 先天的) health conditions, it is important to understand how accurate genetic tests are, and what information we can rely upon.

P2 How accurate DNA tests are relies greatly upon the kind of test being taken, on the specific question you ask, and on how complex the genetics behind a trait(特征) is. For example, tests for traits that depend on a single gene provide much more reliable results, because you can see whether a disease- causing trait is present.

P3 Ancestry tests claim to reveal our genetic identities. But saying you are 30 percent East Asian or American hardly reflects your real ancestry.

P4 What about using DNA tests to discover distant family members? There are tools to compare one's DNA with others' to find distant relatives based on their genetic identification. These kinds of applications are generally accurate. It's relatively easy to tell whether two DNA samples belong to close relatives. With distant relatives, results become hazier.

P5 Genetic health tests claim to be able to detect certain hereditary( 遗传的) diseases, or other health conditions. While certain rare diseases can be easily identified, most potential health conditions cannot be identified by genetic testing alone. The large majority of our traits and diseases also depend upon non-genetic factors, such as lifestyle, the environment, and many others.

P6 Genetic tests for multi-factorial traits are often very tricky to interpret. Height, for example, depends on hundreds of genes, each contributing a little to the outcome, together with a bunch of environmental factors. A test can look at many genes at once, but it's difficult to predict how they will play together. Then you should also account for non-genetic factors that are not written in the DNA.

P7 Tests that offer to find your perfect romantic match and those claiming to predict personality or talents based on your DNA are pure nonsense. At the moment, the scientific bases for these applications are non-existent or incredibly weak.

questions.stem: What kind of genetic tests tend to be comparatively reliable?
questions.stemZh: 什么样的基因检测往往相对可靠？
options: Those complex enough to reveal the genetics behind a trait.
Those looking for traits responsible for certain diseases.
Those focusing on the specific questions being asked.
Those looking for traits determined by a single gene.
optionsZh: 那些足够复杂以揭示某一特征背后遗传机制的检测。
那些寻找导致某些疾病的特征的检测。
那些专注于所提出的特定问题的检测。
那些寻找由单一基因决定的特征的检测。

explain.判型: What kind of genetic tests tend to be comparatively reliable 是查询事实性比较，找到 原文那句 "X 更可靠" 即可对答案。
explain.拆句: What kind of genetic tests tend to be comparatively reliable 中 "tend to be" 是"倾向 于、往往是"的弱化系动词结构，相当于 are usually；comparatively 修饰 reliable，是"相 对来说"，并非"绝对可靠"。 52. What kind of genetic tests tend to be comparatively reliable? A) Those complex enough to reveal the genetics behind a trait. B) Those looking for traits responsible for certain diseases. C) Those focusing on the specific questions being asked. D) Those looking for traits determined by a single gene.
explain.定位: For example, tests for traits that depend on a single gene provide much more reliable results, because you can see whether a disease-causing trait is present. 举个例子，对于那些只依赖单个基因的性状，相关检测能给出准确得多的结果，因为你可以 直接看到致病性状到底存不存在。
explain.选项: A) 与原文相反 Those complex enough to reveal the genetics behind a trait 说"复杂到能揭示性状 背后基因"，原文却是"取决于单基因的简单情况更可靠"，方向相反。 B) 偷换概念 Those looking for traits responsible for certain diseases 抓住的是 a disease- causing trait——但原文里 "致病性状" 只是"为什么单基因检测可靠"的解释，不是"哪 一类检测可靠"。 C) 偷换概念 Those focusing on the specific questions being asked 把 the specific question you ask 直接搬来，但原文那一句讲的是"准确度取决于问题"，不是"针对特定问题的检 测更可靠"。 D) ✓ 正确 tests for traits that depend on a single gene ↔ Those looking for traits determined by a single gene 全篇只有 single gene 这一处出现"单基因"，且就配着 more reliable，预判和 D 完全 对齐，锁定 D。 从文章中我们了解到关于基因健康检测的什么信息？ A) 它们本身无法识别某些遗传性疾病。 B) 它们通常无法区分遗传因素和非遗传因素。 C) 它们无法独立识别大多数潜在疾病。 D) 它们无法区分生活方式的影响和环境的影响。

questions.stem: What do we learn about genetic health tests from the passage?

options: They are unable to identify certain hereditary diseases by themselves.

writing.directions: Suppose your university is organizing a forum on how students can make the best use of on- campus resources for academic development. You are now to write an essay to express your view. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
writing.model: On-campus resources are a treasure that too many students overlook. In my view, actively making use of these facilities is one of the smartest ways to boost our academic development. There are several practical steps we can take. First, we should visit the library and its online databases regularly, since they offer academic papers and books that turn a rough idea into a well-supported argument. Moreover, we ought to consult professors during their office hours, because a ten-minute talk often clears up confusion that hours of self-study cannot. In addition, attending academic lectures and joining study groups exposes us to fresh perspectives and keeps our motivation high. In short, the campus is full of tools waiting to be used. Only by taking the initiative to utilize them can we truly grow as learners and get the most out of our university years.
writing.modelZh: 【参考译文】校内资源是一座被太多学生忽视的宝藏。在我看来，主动利用这些设施，是提升我们学业发展最聪明的方式之一。我们可以采取几项切实可行的做法。首先，我们应当经常光顾图书馆及其在线数据库，因为它们提供的学术论文和书籍能把一个粗糙的想法变成有充分支撑的论证。此外，我们应当在教授的答疑时间当面请教，因为一次十分钟的交流，往往能解开数小时自学都绕不过去的困惑。再者，参加学术讲座、加入学习小组能让我们接触到新视角，并保持高昂的学习动力。总之，校园里满是等待被利用的工具。只有主动去利用它们，我们才能真正作为学习者成长，把大学时光用到极致。【第 1 段】首段两句立观点。本段用『点题引入＋亮明观点』句架：一句 On-campus resources are atreasure that too many students overlook 把话题立起来，一句 In my view 抛出总观点，落实了outline 第一段『点价值亮总观点』的功能。【第 2 段】主体段并列三做法。本段以 There are several practical steps 领起，用 First / Moreover /In addition 串起图书馆数据库、请教教授、听讲座三条做法，每条都跟一句 since/because 理由，落实『分点给具体做法』。【第 3 段】结尾重申并升华。本段用 In short 收束、Only by ... can we ... 强调句升华，重申主动利用资源方能成长，落实『重申升华呼应主题』。

outline.text: 首段两句立观点。本段用『点题引入＋亮明观点』句架：一句 On-campus resources are a treasure that too many students overlook 把话题立起来，一句 In my view 抛出总观点，落实了 outline 第一段『点价值亮总观点』的功能。
主体段并列三做法。本段以 There are several practical steps 领起，用 First / Moreover / In addition 串起图书馆数据库、请教教授、听讲座三条做法，每条都跟一句 since/because 理由，落实 『分点给具体做法』。
结尾重申并升华。本段用 In short 收束、Only by ... can we ... 强调句升华，重申主动利用资 源方能成长，落实『重申升华呼应主题』。

translation.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2.
translation.source: 中国政府十分重视绿色经济的发展。通过加强森林资源保护、加大污染治理力度等一系列措施，许多地区的生态环境得到了显著改善。绿水青山 (lucid waters and lush mountains) 促进了当地的旅游、健康等产业的发展，创造了可观的经济效益。如今，生态环境与人类社会和谐共存的观念在中国已深入人心。绿色经济的推进不仅能为中国可持续发展做出贡献，也为全球环境保护提供了宝贵经验。
translation.reference: The Chinese government attaches great importance to the development of the green economy. Through a series of measures such as strengthening forest resource protection and intensifying pollution control, the ecological environment in many regions has improved remarkably. Lucid waters and lush mountains have promoted the development of local industries such as tourism and health care, generating considerable economic benefits. Today, the idea that ecology and human society can coexist in harmony has taken deep root in China. The promotion of the green economy not only contributes to China's sustainable development but also provides valuable experience for global environmental protection.

sentences.trunk: 主谓宾＝政府＋重视＋发展（主语策略：原句主语） 中文已有现成主语 中国政府，核心动词是 重视，宾语是 绿色经济的发展。骨架直接立成 The Chinese government attaches great importance to the development of the green economy，主谓宾一一对应，不必绕弯。
sentences.downgrade: 本就是简单句，无需降级 全句只有「重视」一个核心动词，结构就是「谁＋重视＋什么」，是天然的简单句，不存在多余分 句要降级，直接照主干写出即可。
sentences.grammar: 时态 回指全篇基调用一般现在时：政府「重视」是当前一贯的态度，谓语用 attaches（第三人称单 数）。 主谓一致 主语 The Chinese government 是单数，谓语动词须加 s → attaches，别漏掉这个 s。 短语搭配 「重视」最稳的地道说法是 attach importance to（importance 前可加 great 表「十分」），to 后接名词；也可用 value highly。不要写成 very value 这类中式表达。 冠词 the green economy、the development 都用 the：特指中国正在发展的这一个绿色经济、这一 项发展，是确定所指，加定冠词。
sentences.target: The Chinese government attaches great importance to the development of the green economy. 2. 通过加强森林资源保护、加大污染治理力度等一系列措施，许多地区的生态环境得到了显著 改善。

sentences.trunk: 主谓＝生态环境＋已改善（主语策略：原句主语） 句子真正的主干是后半截 许多地区的生态环境得到了显著改善，主语 the ecological environment（in many regions），谓语「得到改善」其实是「环境被改善了」，写成 has improved 或 has been improved。前半截 通过……等一系列措施 只是方式状语，不是主干。
sentences.downgrade: 措施块降级为 through 引导的状语 通过加强森林资源保护、加大污染治理力度等一系列措施 整块降级成介词短语作状语：Through a series of measures such as strengthening forest resource protection and intensifying pollution control。注意「加强」「加大」是两个动词，并列后都改成动名词 strengthening / intensifying 挂在 such as 后，不另起谓语。
sentences.grammar: 时态 「得到了显著改善」强调动作已完成并对现在有影响，偏离全篇基调、用现在完成时 has improved / has been improved，这是基调允许的例外。 语态 「环境得到改善」是环境被改善，可用被动 has been improved；也可把 environment 作主语用 主动 has improved（improve 可作不及物动词表「好转」）。两种都对，不要写成中式的 has been got improved。 单复数 「许多地区」是复数 many regions；「一系列措施」用 a series of measures（measures 复 数，series 不变）。 动词形式 such as 之后的「加强、加大」必须用动名词 strengthening、intensifying（介词后跟 -ing）， 不能用动词原形 strengthen。
sentences.target: Through a series of measures such as strengthening forest resource protection and intensifying pollution control, the ecological environment in many regions has improved remarkably. 3. 绿水青山 (lucid waters and lush mountains) 促进了当地的旅游、健康等产业的发展，创造了可 观的经济效益。

sentences.trunk: 主语＝绿水青山，双谓语促进＋创造（主语策略：原句主语） 主语是原文给定译名的 绿水青山 (lucid waters and lush mountains)，它有两个并列动作：促进 了……产业的发展 和 创造了可观的经济效益。骨架是 Lucid waters and lush mountains have promoted… and created…，一个主语带两个并列谓语。
sentences.downgrade: 两动作并列，时态保持一致 两个谓语 have promoted 与 (have) created 并列，第二个谓语可省略助动词 have，只要时态平 行即可。「当地的旅游、健康等产业」译成 the development of local industries such as tourism and health care，用 such as 列举、用 the development of 承接「……产业的发展」。
sentences.grammar: 时态 「促进了、创造了」表已产生并延续至今的成效，用现在完成时 have promoted、(have) created；主语是复数概念 lucid waters and lush mountains，助动词用 have。 单复数 并列主语 waters and mountains 视为复数，谓语用 have 不用 has；「产业」复数 industries。 用词 「可观的经济效益」译 considerable economic benefits（benefits 复数）；「促进」用 promote／boost／facilitate 均可，不要用生硬的 push。 短语搭配 「健康产业」指大健康产业，译 health care（industry）或 health industry 更准；「旅游业」 tourism 本身即名词，不必再加 industry。
sentences.target: Lucid waters and lush mountains have promoted the development of local industries such as tourism and health care, generating considerable economic benefits. 4. 如今，生态环境与人类社会和谐共存的观念在中国已深入人心。

sentences.trunk: 主语＝观念，谓语＝深入人心（主语策略：原句主语） 主干主语是 观念（the idea / concept），谓语是 已深入人心（has taken root / become deeply rooted）。「生态环境与人类社会和谐共存的」整块是修饰「观念」的定语，「如今」 「在中国」是时间／地点状语。
sentences.downgrade: 长定语降级为同位语从句／介词短语 生态环境与人类社会和谐共存的 这串定语降级安放到「观念」之后：the idea that ecology and human society coexist in harmony（that 引导同位语从句解释 idea），或 the idea of harmonious coexistence between the eco-environment and human society（介词短语）。 绝不照中文语序把定语全堆在 idea 前面。
sentences.grammar: 时态 「已深入人心」表已完成且影响持续，用现在完成时 has taken root / has become deeply rooted；句首「如今」对应 Today / Nowadays，与完成时并不冲突。 短语搭配 「深入人心」地道译法是 take root in people's minds / become deeply rooted / win popular support，不要逐字硬译成 deep into people's heart。 主谓一致 主语是单数 the idea / concept，谓语用 has（单数第三人称）。 用词 「和谐共存」译 coexist in harmony / harmonious coexistence；coexist 是不及物动词， 「与……共存」用 coexist with 或 between A and B。
sentences.target: Today, the idea that ecology and human society can coexist in harmony has taken deep root in China. 5. 绿色经济的推进不仅能为中国可持续发展做出贡献，也为全球环境保护提供了宝贵经验。

sentences.trunk: 主语＝推进，谓语＝贡献＋提供经验（主语策略：原句主语） 主语是 绿色经济的推进（the promotion of the green economy），由「不仅……也……」连起两 个并列谓语：为中国可持续发展做出贡献 和 为全球环境保护提供了宝贵经验。骨架＝The promotion… not only contributes to… but also provides…。
sentences.downgrade: 不仅……也……→not only… but also… 「不仅……也……」是固定的递进关联，对应 not only… but (also)…，把两个谓语 contributes to 与 provides 分别嵌进去：not only contributes to China's sustainable development but also provides valuable experience for global environmental protection。两个谓语保持平行。
sentences.grammar: 时态 整句陈述绿色经济推进的普遍意义，回指全篇基调用一般现在时 contributes、provides；主语 the promotion 单数，谓语加 s。 主谓一致 主语是单数 the promotion，not only / but also 连接的两个谓语都用第三人称单数 contributes、provides。 短语搭配 「为……做出贡献」固定搭配 contribute to（to 后接名词）；「为……提供」provide… for…； 「环境保护」environmental protection。 用词 「宝贵经验」译 valuable experience，experience 表「经验」时不可数，不加 s，前面也不加 a。
sentences.target: The promotion of the green economy not only contributes to China's sustainable development but also provides valuable experience for global environmental protection. 英语四级 2025年12月·第3套 · 全卷构成 Part I 写作 题目解析 → Part II 听力 与2025年12月第1套共用 · 题目解析 → Part III Section A 完形填空（选词填空） 题目解析 → Part III Section B 长篇阅读（信息匹配） 题目解析 → Part III Section C 阅读理解（四选一） 题目解析 → Part III Section C (2) 阅读理解（四选一） 题目解析 → Part IV 汉译英（段落翻译） 本题

questions.stem: How did Tariq make corn taste better?
questions.stemZh: Tariq 是如何让玉米味道更好的?
questions.answerText: By slapping some butter on it.

explain.定位: Everything changed for 7-year-old Tariq when he slapped some butter on an ear of corn. He knew it tasted good, but butter made it better. 对 7 岁的塔里克来说，当他往一根玉米上抹了点黄油时，一切都变了。他本就知道玉米好 吃，但黄油让它更好吃了。
explain.信号: but 后点出"黄油让它更好吃"。答案句的信号是转折词 but：but butter made it better 直 接把 butter 和 made it better 挂钩，正好回答"怎么让玉米更好吃"，转折之后的这半句才 是落点。
explain.替换: he slapped some butter on an ear of corn ↔By slapping some butter on it. an ear of corn 被代词 it 概括
explain.排除: B) 原词陷阱 录音第2段确实提到玉米能 provides nourishment across the globe，B 项 By enhancing its nourishment. 盗用了 nourishment 这个原词，但那是讲玉米向全球提供营养，跟"塔里 克怎么让玉米更好吃"无关，听到 nourishment 就选就中陷阱。 借用原文：The corn provides nourishment across the globe. C) 原词陷阱 C 项 By growing it in South Dakota. 盗用了录音里的 South Dakota 这个高频地名， South Dakota is one of the top corn producers in America 说的是它是产玉米大州， 与"让玉米更好吃"是两码事，属听到地名就想选的原词陷阱。 借用原文：South Dakota is one of the top corn producers in America. D) 未提及 D 项 By cooking it in vegetable oil. 听起来也是个合理做法，且和正确项 A 的"加黄油"形 成对立诱惑，但录音从头到尾只提了抹黄油，没说用植物油烹饪，属凭常识硬造、原文未提 及。

optionsZh: 在玉米上涂一些黄油。
通过增强其营养价值。
通过在 South Dakota 种植它。
通过用植物油烹饪它。
options: By slapping some butter on it.
By growing it in South Dakota.
By cooking it in vegetable oil.

questions.stem: Why were Tariq and his family invited to South Dakota?
questions.stemZh: 为什么 Tariq 和他的家人被邀请到 South Dakota?

explain.定位: Tariq and his family were invited to South Dakota to attend the honorary ceremony at the state's Corn Palace. 塔里克和他的家人受邀前往南达科他，去参加该州玉米宫举行的荣誉典礼。
explain.信号: invited to… to attend… 把人和目的连起来。答案信号是 invited 后接的目的不定式： were invited to South Dakota to attend the honorary ceremony，to attend 直接说明 受邀目的就是参加荣誉典礼，这句一字对上题干所问。
explain.替换: to attend the honorary ceremony ↔To attend an honorary ceremony. the→an，去掉地点状语，核心动作不变
explain.排除: A) 张冠李戴 录音确实提到官方想突出 tourism and agriculture，A 项 To introduce their corn to tourists. 盗用了 tourism 引申出的 tourists，但那是官方的产业意图，不是塔里克一家"被 邀请"的目的，二者主体不同，听到游客相关词就选会被带偏。 借用原文：Officials wanted to highlight South Dakota's two largest industries: tourism and agriculture. C) 未提及 C 项 To share experience with other corn growers. 借 corn 这个全篇高频词造出"和其他 玉米种植者交流经验"的合理场景，但录音通篇没说塔里克要去交流经验，属凭话题臆造、 未提及。 D) 原词陷阱 D 项 To exhibit their corn at the state's Corn Palace. 盗用了答案句里真实出现的地名 at the state's Corn Palace，极具迷惑性；但录音说的是去玉米宫"参加典礼"，不是去那里"展 出他们的玉米"，偷换了在玉米宫做的事，听到 Corn Palace 就选会中招。 借用原文：to attend the honorary ceremony at the state's Corn Palace

optionsZh: 向游客介绍他们的玉米。
参加一个荣誉典礼。
与其他玉米种植者分享经验。
在该州的玉米宫展示他们的玉米。
options: To introduce their corn to tourists.
To share experience with other corn growers.
To exhibit their corn at the state's Corn Palace.
questions._leakedNextScript: Two arrests were announced Thursday. The arrests were in connection with a string of mail thefts from U.S. Postal Service's collection boxes in Marion County and for the possession of a stolen postal Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.

questions.stem: What did Jordan Jax and Tarod Goodman do according to a news release?
questions.stemZh: 根据一则新闻稿，Jordan Jax 和 Tarod Goodman 做了什么?

explain.定位: Jordan Jax and Tarod Goodman, both 23, were arrested after evidence gathered in an investigation showed the pair stole mail on multiple occasions using a postal key, according to a news release. 据一份新闻稿，乔丹·贾克斯和塔罗德·古德曼，两人均为 23 岁，在一项调查所收集的证据显 示二人多次盗窃邮件、并使用了一把邮政钥匙后，被逮捕。
explain.信号: 题干来源词回扣定位。题干里的 according to a news release 与录音 according to a news release 逐字对应，这处来源短语就是定位信号：它出现的那一句正是承载答案的句 子，紧接的 stole mail on multiple occasions 即两人所做之事。
explain.替换: stole mail on multiple occasions ↔Stole mail several times. 多次的同义改写
explain.排除: B) 原词陷阱 录音说两人 using a postal key，是使用一把邮政钥匙作案，并非 Forged postal keys illegally. 所说的非法伪造钥匙；选项盗用了 postal key 这一原词，却把使用偷换成伪造， 答非所问。 借用原文：using a postal key C) 张冠李戴 录音里的 on multiple occasions 修饰的是盗窃邮件，Attacked postmen on multiple occasions. 却把这个多次短语套到攻击邮递员上；录音通篇没有任何袭击邮差的内容，属盗 用频次短语的张冠李戴。 借用原文：stole mail on multiple occasions D) 原词陷阱 录音多处提到 collection boxes，如 collection boxes，但说的是两人用钥匙打开邮筒取 信，从无砸坏之意；Broke a number of postal collection boxes. 盗用 collection boxes 原词，硬加上 Broke 这一录音没有的动作。 借用原文：collection boxes

optionsZh: 多次盗窃邮件。
非法伪造邮政钥匙。
多次袭击邮递员。
破坏了多个邮政收集箱。
options: Broke a number of postal collection boxes.

questions.stem: What do Jordan Jax and Tarod Goodman face?
questions.stemZh: Jordan Jax 和 Tarod Goodman 面临什么?
questions.answerText: Up to fifteen years in prison.

explain.定位: Jax and Goodman each face up to five years in federal prison in the mail thefts and up to ten years for possession of the postal key. 贾克斯和古德曼二人因盗窃邮件各面临最高五年的联邦监禁，并因持有邮政钥匙各面临最高 十年监禁。
explain.信号: 题干动词 face 原句重现。题干的 face 在录音 each face up to five years 里原样念出，这 处动词回扣即定位信号；该句把两项刑期 up to five years 与 up to ten years 一并给出， 正是答案所在。
explain.替换: up to five years in federal prison ↔Up to fifteen years in prison. 两项刑期相加得十五年 up to ten years for possession of the postal key ↔Up to fifteen years in prison. 另一项刑期并入总数
explain.排除: A) 未提及 录音只说面临有期的 five years 与 ten years，从未提无期；A sentence for life. 是夸大到 终身监禁的后果，录音并无对应内容。 B) 未提及 录音谈的全是坐牢的年限，未提任何财产损失；Loss of all their possessions. 所说丧失全 部财产在录音里毫无依据。 C) 原词陷阱 录音里的 23 出自两人年龄 both 23，并非刑期；Twenty-three years' hard labor. 盗用 23 这个数字，硬安成二十三年苦役，且 hard labor 录音也从未提及，把年龄数偷换成刑期。 借用原文：both 23 1 Can fast-fashion be sustainable? Researchers think yes. Identifying why the fast-fashion business model creates waste and determining whether regulators can establish incentives for consumers and manufacturers are steps to reduce waste. 快时尚能否实现可持续发展？研究人员认为可以。确定快时尚商业模式为何会造成浪费，以及判断监管机 构能否建立激励机制来引导消费者和制造商，是减少浪费的关键步骤。 2 Recently, the clothing industry has come under attack for creating a waste problem with serious environmental consequences. In the absence of environmentally and economically feasible recycling options, fast-fashion manufacturers pump out low-quality clothes produced in high volumes that are worn only a few times and then discarded. 近年来，服装行业因制造严重的环境后果的废物问题而受到抨击。在缺乏环境和经济上可行的回收选择的 情况下，快时尚制造商大量生产低质量的服装，这些服装只穿几次就被丢弃。 3 The researchers put forth policy contributions, ranging from sustainable disposal of leftover stock to production tax to incentivize both manufacturers and consumers to be more waste conscious. 研究人员提出了一系列政策建议，从可持续处置剩余库存到征收生产税，以激励制造商和消费者更加注重 减少浪费。 4 In order to devise effective policies to curb the environmental impact of the clothing industry, it is important to identify the source of the problem in the supply chain. Manufacturers, consumers, and regulatory bodies can then take an informed approach to recognize the environmental impact of fast- fashion and to design an ecosystem to reduce waste, incentivize innovation, and create new business models to manage waste. 为了制定有效的政策来遏制服装行业对环境的影响，确定供应链中问题的根源至关重要。然后，制造商、 消费者和监管机构可以采取知情的方法来认识快时尚的环境影响，并设计一个生态系统来减少浪费、激励 创新以及创建新的商业模式来管理废物。 Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.

optionsZh: 终身监禁。
失去所有财产。
二十三年苦役。
最高十五年监禁。
options: Up to fifteen years in prison.

questions.stem: Why has the clothing industry come under attack?
questions.stemZh: 为什么服装行业受到抨击?
questions.answerText: It creates waste and severely impacts the environment.

explain.定位: Recently, the clothing industry has come under attack for creating a waste problem with serious environmental consequences. 最近，服装业因制造废物问题、带来严重环境后果而受到抨击。
explain.信号: 题干原词 come under attack 复现处。录音中 has come under attack for 与题干 come under attack 几乎一字不差，听到这个短语就锁定这句；紧跟 for 后面的内容正是被抨击的 原因，即答案所在。
explain.替换: creating a waste problem ↔It creates waste 动名词转一般现在时 serious environmental consequences ↔severely impacts the environment 名词短语改写成动词短语
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 A 说 misleads consumers（误导消费者），其中 consumers 是录音后文反复出现的原 词，听到就想选；但录音说行业被抨击的原因是制造废物、害环境，从没说它误导消费者， A 借原词制造错觉。 借用原文：incentivize both manufacturers and consumers B) 偷换概念 B 说 ignores economically feasible recycling options（忽视经济可行的回收方案），其 中 recycling、economically feasible 直接来自录音 environmentally and economically feasible recycling options；但录音说的是这类回收方案本就缺失（in the absence of）， 不是行业故意忽视，B 把客观缺失偷换成主观无视。 借用原文：In the absence of environmentally and economically feasible recycling options D) 与原文相反 D 说 produces clothes affordable only to a tiny minority（生产只有极少数人买得起的 衣服），clothes、produces 是录音原词，但录音明说快时尚是 low-quality clothes produced in high volumes（低质、量产），价格便宜、人人能买，与 D 说的只有极少数 人买得起恰好相反，录音也没提价格门槛。 借用原文：low-quality clothes produced in high volumes

optionsZh: 它逃避监管并误导消费者。
它忽视经济上可行的回收选择。
它制造废物并严重影响环境。
它生产的服装只有极少数人能够负担得起。
options: It escapes regulation and misleads consumers.
It ignores economically feasible recycling options.
It creates waste and severely impacts the environment.
It produces clothes affordable only to a tiny minority.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers put forth such policies as production tax?
questions.stemZh: 为什么研究人员提出诸如生产税之类的政策?
questions.answerText: To urge manufacturers and consumers to reduce waste.

explain.定位: The researchers put forth policy contributions, ranging from sustainable disposal of leftover stock to production tax to incentivize both manufacturers and consumers to be more waste conscious. 研究者提出了一系列政策建议，从对剩余库存的可持续处理到征收生产税，目的是激励生产 商和消费者都更有减废意识。
explain.信号: 目的状语 to incentivize。录音里 to incentivize both manufacturers and consumers to be more waste conscious 是 production tax 后面的目的状语，to incentivize 就是表目 的的信号，它后面的内容正是这些政策要达成的目标。
explain.替换: incentivize both manufacturers and consumers ↔urge manufacturers and consumers 同义动词替换 to be more waste conscious ↔to reduce waste 概括式改写
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 A 说 cut consumers' expenses in buying quality clothes（替消费者省下买好衣服的 钱），consumers 是录音原词，但录音讲政策目的是减废，从没说为消费者省钱，A 把减 废目的偷换成省钱目的。 借用原文：incentivize both manufacturers and consumers B) 过度推断 B 说 To enable the whole fast-fashion industry to be sustainable（让整个快时尚业可 持续），sustainable 是录音开头出现的原词，但生产税这类政策的直接目的录音说得很具 体——是激励双方减废，而非让整个行业可持续，B 把目的范围夸大了。 借用原文：Can fast-fashion be sustainable? C) 偷换概念 C 说 incentivize manufacturers to be more consumer-friendly（激励生产商更体贴消费 者），incentivize、manufacturers 是录音原词，但录音说的是激励双方更有减废意识，不 是让生产商对消费者更友好，C 把减废目的偷换成讨好消费者。 借用原文：incentivize both manufacturers and consumers to be more waste conscious

optionsZh: 为了削减消费者购买优质服装的开支。
为了使整个快时尚行业能够可持续发展。
为了激励制造商更加关注消费者利益。
为了敦促制造商和消费者减少废物。
options: To cut consumers' expenses in buying quality clothes.
To enable the whole fast-fashion industry to be sustainable.
To incentivize manufacturers to be more consumer-friendly.
To urge manufacturers and consumers to reduce waste.

questions.stem: What should be done first to eliminate the harm caused by the clothing industry?
questions.stemZh: 要消除服装行业造成的危害,首先应该做什么?
questions.answerText: Identifying the source of the problem.

explain.定位: In order to devise effective policies to curb the environmental impact of the clothing industry, it is important to identify the source of the problem in the supply chain. 为了制定有效政策来遏制服装业对环境的影响，关键是先找出供应链中问题的根源。
explain.信号: 强调句 it is important to。录音 it is important to identify the source of the problem 用 it is important to 强调首要之事，这就是表先后、表首要的信号词；它后面的动作 identify the source 即题目问的第一步。
explain.替换: identify the source of the problem ↔Identifying the source of the problem 动词原形转动名词，近乎原句
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 A 说 Recognizing the impact on consumers，其中 recognize、impact 来自录音 recognize the environmental impact of fast-fashion，听到就想选；但录音把这一步放 在找出根源之后，而且说的是认识环境影响、不是对消费者的影响，既不是第一步、对象也 被改了。 借用原文：recognize the environmental impact of fast-fashion C) 过度推断 C 说 Abandoning the current business model（放弃现有商业模式），business model 取自录音 create new business models，但录音说的是创造新商业模式，从没说要放弃现 有模式，C 把创造夸张成放弃。 借用原文：create new business models to manage waste D) 原词陷阱 D 说 Establishing powerful regulatory bodies（建立强有力的监管机构），regulatory bodies 出现在录音 Manufacturers, consumers, and regulatory bodies 中，但录音只是 提到监管机构是参与方之一，从没说要先建立强有力的监管机构，D 是凭原词编出来的。 借用原文：Manufacturers, consumers, and regulatory bodies can then take an informed approach

optionsZh: 认识到对消费者的影响。
找出问题的根源。
放弃当前的商业模式。
建立强有力的监管机构。
options: Identifying the source of the problem.
Establishing powerful regulatory bodies. Section B

questions.stem: Why is the woman complaining?
questions.stemZh: 女士为什么在抱怨?
questions.answerText: The city's rush-hour traffic is intolerable.

explain.定位: Rush hour in this city is killing me. 这座城市的高峰期真要把我折腾死了。
explain.信号: 她开口的第一句直接吐槽。男方问"你怎么这么烦/出什么事了"之后，女方应答的第一句 Rush hour in this city is killing me. 就是直接吐槽，is killing me 这种强烈情绪用语正是 抱怨的落点信号——被问者的第一反应往往就是答案句。
explain.替换: Rush hour in this city is killing me. ↔The city's rush-hour traffic is intolerable. is killing me 改写成 intolerable
explain.排除: B) 原词陷阱 B 盗用了录音里反复出现的 Rush hour 来勾人，但她抱怨的是高峰期"让人受不了"，从没 说"她躲不开高峰"。She cannot avoid rush-hour traffic. 是凭空加上的内容，属听到原词 就想选的陷阱。 借用原文：Rush hour is terrible C) 原词陷阱 录音后面女方确实提到 the local government could help improve things，C 盗用"政 府"这个原词，却编成"政府效率低"。她说的是"政府本可以帮忙改善"，并没说政府无能，C 答非所问。 借用原文：the local government could help improve things D) 原词陷阱 男方说过 a city this big，D 盗用"城市大"这个原词，编成"城市太大不好出行"。但那是男 方的话，且女方抱怨的对象是高峰期本身，不是城市大小，D 既张冠李戴又答非所问。 借用原文：a city this big

optionsZh: 这座城市的高峰时段交通令人无法忍受。
她无法避开高峰时段的交通。
当地政府效率低下。
这座城市太大了,出行不便。
options: The city's rush-hour traffic is intolerable.
The city is too big to move around easily.

questions.stem: What does the woman suggest doing?
questions.stemZh: 女士建议做什么?

explain.定位: Well, for example, the subway system could have air conditioning. I know many cities in the world have air conditioning in their subway, so why can't we? 比如说，地铁系统可以装空调嘛。我知道世界上很多城市的地铁都有空调，咱们为什么不能 有呢？
explain.信号: 建议信号 could 与 why can't we。the subway system could have air conditioning 里 的 could（可以…）就是建议信号，紧接着 why can't we（咱为什么不能）用反问加重了这 条提议——could + 反问，正是"我建议这么做"的落点。
explain.替换: the subway system could have air conditioning ↔Air conditioning the city's subway. 句子改写成动名词短语
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 A 盗用录音里的 subway carriages（地铁车厢）来勾人。"车厢"确实念到了，但女方的建 议是"装空调"，不是"升级车厢"。况且后面 The trains here are too old 是男方说的，不是 女方的建议，A 答非所问。 借用原文：strangers packed close together in the subway carriages B) 未提及 增开公交线路这件事女方从没提过。录音只在男方那段提到 Bus No. 36，与"增加线路"无 关，B 属凭空捏造的措施。 D) 原词陷阱 D 盗用了 many cities in the world 里的"别的城市"来勾人，但女方提"很多城市有空调"是 为论证"应给地铁装空调"，并非建议"向别的大城市学习"。D 把具体建议偷换成空泛口号， 答非所问。 借用原文：I know many cities in the world have air conditioning in their subway

optionsZh: 升级地铁车厢。
增加公交线路数量。
为城市地铁安装空调。
向其他大城市学习。
options: Increasing the number of bus routes.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?
questions.stemZh: 从对话中我们了解到男士的什么情况?
questions.answerText: He takes a half-hour bus ride to work.

explain.定位: Yeah, it's more convenient. Bus No. 36 goes straight from my house to the office. It's a 30- minute ride and I don't have to make any changes. 对，公交更方便。36 路车从我家直达办公室，车程 30 分钟，中途不用换乘。
explain.信号: 男方自述上班方式 + 数字 30-minute。Bus No. 36 goes straight from my house to the office 是男方在讲自己怎么上班，紧跟的 It's a 30-minute ride 给出具体时长——"自述 + 数字"是细节题最硬的落点信号，听到数字就要立刻记下。
explain.替换: It's a 30-minute ride ↔He takes a half-hour bus ride to work. 30-minute 换说成 half-hour Bus No. 36 goes straight from my house to the office ↔bus ride to work 坐公交去办公室=坐公交上班
explain.排除: A) 张冠李戴 A 盗用录音里 rush-hour crowds 这个"高峰拥挤"原词来勾人，但受高峰挤之苦的是女方 （坐地铁），男方说自己坐公交、还自称 fortunate。把女方的处境安到男方身上，是张冠 李戴。 借用原文：the rush-hour crowds with strangers packed close together B) 原词陷阱 B 盗用男方说的 I'm fortunate（我算幸运）来勾人。他幸运是因为"坐公交方便、不用挤地 铁"，而不是"住得离公司很近"——通勤还要 30 分钟，谈不上很近。B 把"幸运的原因"偷换 了。 借用原文：I guess I'm fortunate I take the bus instead D) 张冠李戴 D 盗用了 move closer to the office 这个原词，但说"也许我该搬得离公司近点"的是女 方，不是男方。把女方的打算记到男方头上，张冠李戴。 借用原文：Maybe I should move closer to the office

optionsZh: 他也深受高峰时段拥挤之苦。
他很幸运住得离工作地点非常近。
他乘坐半小时公交车上班。
他打算搬到离办公室更近的地方。
options: He suffers from rush-hour crowding too.
He is fortunate to live very near to work.
He takes a half-hour bus ride to work.
He is going to move closer to his office.

questions.stem: What does the woman ask the man to do at the end of the conversation?
questions.stemZh: 对话结束时女士要求男士做什么?
questions.answerText: Send her his housing agent's telephone number.

explain.定位: Hmm, could you send me his number, please? 嗯，你能把他的电话号码发给我吗？
explain.信号: 请求句 could you…please。could you send me his number, please? 用 could you… please 提出请求，正是"请对方做某事"的标准信号，且出现在对话末尾，与题干"at the end"对得上——这就是答案句。
explain.替换: could you send me his number, please? ↔Send her his housing agent's telephone number. his number 补全为中介的电话号码
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 A 盗用了对话里 move closer to the office、flat 这一带"房子"话题来勾人，但她请的是"发 中介电话"，不是"请他直接推荐一套好房子"。把"给电话"偷换成"荐房"，答非所问。 借用原文：I found the flat I'm living in now through him C) 张冠李戴 C 盗用了男方那句 tell him exactly what you are looking for，但那是男方让"她去告诉中 介"要什么，不是她请男方做的事，也不是"由男方告诉她该找什么样的房"。既张冠李戴又把 方向弄反。 借用原文：Just tell him exactly what you are looking for D) 原词陷阱 D 盗用男方那句 he will find something good 来勾人，但那是男方对中介能办好的预期， 不是女方请男方"确保中介给她找到好的"。把一句预期偷换成她的请求，答非所问。 借用原文：I'm sure he will find something good 1 M: Did you hear about Johnny? M: 你听说Johnny的事了吗？ 2 W: No. Why? Is he okay? W: 没有。怎么了？他还好吗？ 3 M: He had some plastic surgery done. M: 他做了整形手术。 4 W: What? Why? W: 什么？为什么？ 5 M: Do you remember he had a scar on his face? M: 你还记得他脸上有道疤吗？ 6 W: Yes, of course. He always had that. I've known him since primary school, and I always remember him having that on his cheek. W: 记得，当然记得。他一直都有那道疤。我从小学就认识他了，一直记得他脸颊上有那道疤。 7 M: Well, he had it fixed. M: 嗯，他把它修复了。 8 W: Fixed? What do you mean? You can't fix a scar. W: 修复？什么意思？疤痕是修复不了的。 9 M: You know what I mean? He had an operation done on it, plastic surgery, in order to cover it and make it less noticeable. M: 你懂我的意思吧？他做了个手术，整形手术，用来遮盖疤痕，让它不那么明显。 Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 10 W: Oh, well, that's ridiculous, isn't it? It was noticeable, sure. But it wasn't an ugly scar. It never occurred to me that he should have it taken care of like that. W: 哦，这太荒唐了，不是吗？那道疤确实挺明显的。但它并不丑。我从来没想过他应该那样处理它。 11 M: I agree. I can understand some scars and physical defects can be ugly and distracting, but not Johnny's. In fact, I thought it added character… like it gave him a certain uniqueness. M: 我同意。我能理解有些疤痕和身体缺陷可能很丑、很扎眼，但Johnny的不是。事实上，我觉得那道疤 为他增添了个性……让他有了某种独特性。 12 W: He must have felt differently though. He must have felt self-conscious and insecure, perhaps. W: 但他肯定想法不一样。他可能觉得难为情、不自信吧。 13 M: No, no, that's not the reason. He was totally fine with his scar. As you said, he had had it for most of his life. M: 不，不，不是那个原因。他对自己的疤完全没问题。就像你说的，他大半辈子都带着那道疤。 14 W: Then why did he have the operation? W: 那他为什么要做手术？ 15 M: Because his girlfriend wanted him to. M: 因为他女朋友想让他做。 16 W: What? That's so superficial and selfish of her. If Johnny's girlfriend doesn't like him for who he is, then she does not deserve to be his girlfriend. W: 什么？她也太肤浅、太自私了。如果Johnny的女朋友不喜欢真实的他，那她就不配做他女朋友。 17 M: You are right. So he is insane to give in to her like that. But when I told him, he said he loves her and would just do what she wants him to. M: 你说得对。所以他那样向她妥协简直疯了。但当我跟他说的时候，他说他爱她，愿意做她想让他做 的事。 18 W: What a fool he is. W: 他真是个傻瓜。

optionsZh: 向她推荐他办公室附近的好房子。
把他的房产中介的电话号码发给她。
准确告诉她应该寻找什么类型的房产。
确保中介为她找到好房子。
options: Recommend to her a good house near his office.
Send her his housing agent's telephone number.
Tell her exactly what kind of property to look for.
Make sure the agent finds something good for her.

questions.stem: What does the man say about Johnny?
questions.stemZh: 男士对Johnny说了什么?
questions.answerText: He had some plastic surgery done.

explain.定位: He had some plastic surgery done. 他做了整形手术。
explain.信号: 对方一开口的核心信息。男生在被问『他还好吗』之后，第一句给出的实质消息就是 He had some plastic surgery done.，这是整段对话的引子和核心事件，承载本题答案。
explain.替换: He had some plastic surgery done. ↔He had some plastic surgery done. 几乎原句照搬
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 选项 He was remembered for the scar on his cheek. 借了录音里真出现过的 scar 和 cheek（女生说 I always remember him having that on his cheek），但那是女生说『记 得他脸上有疤』，并非男生关于 Johnny 所说的核心事件；题问 the man 说了什么，答非 所问。 借用原文：I always remember him having that on his cheek B) 偷换概念 选项 He received a heart operation a few days ago. 蹭了录音里的 operation 一词（He had an operation done on it, plastic surgery），却擅自改成 heart operation（心脏手 术）；录音说的是脸上的整形手术，不是心脏，属偷换。 借用原文：He had an operation done on it, plastic surgery C) 未提及 选项 He used to wear a sad face in school. 里的 sad face（哭丧脸）录音根本没说，只 是借了 school 一词（女生提到 I've known him since primary school）凑出来的；属无 中生有。 借用原文：I've known him since primary school

optionsZh: 他因脸颊上的疤痕而被人记住。
他几天前接受了心脏手术。
他在学校时常常一副悲伤的表情。
他做了一些整形手术。
options: He was remembered for the scar on his cheek.
He received a heart operation a few days ago.
He used to wear a sad face in school.
He had some plastic surgery done.

questions.stem: What does the woman find puzzling?
questions.stemZh: 女士觉得什么令人困惑?
questions.answerText: The man's use of the expression 'fixed'.

explain.定位: Fixed? What do you mean? You can't fix a scar. 修好？你什么意思？疤是没法『修好』的。
explain.信号: 对某个用词的反问。女生紧接男生说的 he had it fixed，立刻反问 Fixed? What do you mean? You can't fix a scar.——她重复并质疑了 fixed 这个词，反问语气正是『困惑』的 信号，答案句就在此。
explain.替换: Fixed? What do you mean? You can't fix a scar. ↔The man's use of the expression 'fixed'. 把疑问句概括为『对用词不解』
explain.排除: A) 未提及 选项 The man's deep sympathy for Johnny. 说男生对 Johnny 深表同情，录音里男生从 头到尾没有表达同情，更不是女生困惑的点；属未提及。 C) 原词陷阱 选项 The man's covering up of what happened. 蹭了录音里 in order to cover it and make it less noticeable 的 cover，但原文 cover 是『遮盖那道疤』，选项偷换成『掩盖发 生的事（隐瞒）』，且女生并不为此困惑。 借用原文：in order to cover it and make it less noticeable D) 张冠李戴 选项 The man's good memory of his childhood. 里『好记性』其实是女生自己说的（I always remember him having that on his cheek），却被安到 the man 头上，且与『困 惑』无关；属张冠李戴。 借用原文：I always remember him having that on his cheek

optionsZh: 男士对Johnny的深切同情。
男士使用"fixed"这个表达。
男士对所发生事情的掩饰。
男士对童年时光的良好记忆。
options: The man's deep sympathy for Johnny.
The man's use of the expression 'fixed'.
The man's covering up of what happened.
The man's good memory of his childhood.

questions.stem: What did the man think of Johnny's scar?
questions.stemZh: 男士对Johnny的疤痕有何看法?
questions.answerText: It seemed to give him a certain uniqueness.

explain.定位: In fact, I thought it added character… like it gave him a certain uniqueness. 其实我觉得那道疤还添了几分个性……好像让他有种独特感。
explain.信号: I thought 引出的主观评价。男生用 In fact, I thought it added character… like it gave him a certain uniqueness，I thought 直接亮出他对疤的看法，且 In fact 加重了肯定语 气，是承载态度的答案句。
explain.替换: it gave him a certain uniqueness ↔It seemed to give him a certain uniqueness. 近乎同句，只换了语气词
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 选项 It gave him a noticeable smartness. 蹭了录音里多次出现的 noticeable（make it less noticeable），但 smartness（精明/帅气）男生从没说过；属用熟词拼凑的原词陷 阱。 借用原文：make it less noticeable B) 未提及 选项 It made him appear even more manly. 说疤让他更有男子气概，录音里男生评价用 的是 character、uniqueness，从未说 manly；属未提及。 D) 与原文相反 选项 It seemed to make up for his physical defects. 蹭了录音 physical defects 一词， 但男生说的是『有些缺陷确实丑、可 Johnny 的疤不是』，并不认为疤在弥补缺陷；这是反 着用了原文，张冠李戴加曲解。 借用原文：I can understand some scars and physical defects can be ugly and distracting, but not Johnny's

optionsZh: 它赋予了他明显的精明。
它使他显得更加阳刚。
它似乎赋予了他某种独特性。
它似乎弥补了他的身体缺陷。
options: It gave him a noticeable smartness.
It made him appear even more manly.
It seemed to give him a certain uniqueness.
It seemed to make up for his physical defects.

questions.stem: How could we describe the speakers' attitude towards Johnny's girlfriend?
questions.stemZh: 我们可以如何描述说话者对Johnny女友的态度?

explain.定位: What? That's so superficial and selfish of her. If Johnny's girlfriend doesn't like him for who he is, then she does not deserve to be his girlfriend. 什么？她这么做也太肤浅、太自私了。如果 Johnny 的女友不能接受真实的他，那她就不配 做他女友。
explain.信号: 连串贬义评价词。女生对女友连用 so superficial and selfish（肤浅、自私）和 does not deserve（不配），都是强烈负面用词；加上男生附和 You are right，两人态度一致偏负 面，这几句是态度答案句。
explain.替换: That's so superficial and selfish of her ↔Critical. 贬义评价归为『批评』
explain.排除: A) 与原文相反 选项 Liberal.（开明、宽容）方向与录音相反——两人对女友是 superficial and selfish 的 指责，毫无宽容之意；属与原文相反。 借用原文：That's so superficial and selfish of her B) 过度推断 选项 Hostile.（充满敌意）程度太重，录音是批评女友的做法（肤浅、自私），并未到仇 视、敌对的地步；属程度过度推断。 C) 与原文相反 选项 Indifferent.（漠不关心）与录音情绪冲突——女生说到激动处骂女友、还评 What a fool he is，明显在意、不是无所谓；属与原文相反。 借用原文：What a fool he is Section C 1 Talking is unique to humans. An animal might make 10 different sounds, but an adult human knows more than 20,000 words. Additionally, we're the only animal that expresses thoughts in full sentences. Researchers don't think language was invented; instead, they think it evolved. How did talking evolve? There are two main theories. 说话是人类独有的能力。动物可能会发出10种不同的声音,但成年人掌握的词汇超过20,000个。此外,我们 是唯一能用完整句子表达思想的动物。研究人员认为语言不是被发明出来的,而是进化而来的。说话是如何 进化的?有两种主要理论。 2 The first theory is that language started with people making different sounds, mostly imitating the things around them, like animal calls, nature sounds, and the sounds of tools. Perhaps they made the sound of wind to comment on the weather or imitated the sound of a bird to tell a friend that there was a bird nearby. Then over hundreds of thousands of years, those sounds turned into words that people began to learn as part of their language. At some point, people started stringing the words together to form sentences. 第一种理论认为,语言起源于人们发出不同的声音,主要是模仿周围的事物,比如动物叫声、自然界的声音以 及工具的声音。也许他们发出风的声音来评论天气,或者模仿鸟叫声来告诉朋友附近有一只鸟。然后在数十 万年的时间里,这些声音演变成了词汇,人们开始将其作为语言的一部分来学习。在某个时刻,人们开始将词 汇串联起来形成句子。 3 The other main theory, which is more recent, is that people started off by gesturing—pointing at things with their hands and imitating actions using their bodies. Eventually these gestures turned into a Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard. full sign language. This theory guesses that after developing sign languages, people eventually started making sounds along with their gestures. At some point, they switched to mostly making sounds that became words instead of just using their bodies. The reason they switched to making sounds, the theory goes, is that talking out loud lets you communicate with someone even when you can't see them. 另一种主要理论更为近期,认为人们最初是通过手势——用手指向事物并用身体模仿动作来交流的。最终 这些手势演变成了完整的手语。这个理论推测,在发展出手语之后,人们最终开始在做手势的同时发出声 音。在某个时刻,他们转变为主要发出声音形成词汇,而不仅仅是使用身体。该理论认为,他们转向发出声音 的原因是,出声说话可以让你即使在看不见对方的情况下也能进行交流。

optionsZh: 宽容的。
敌对的。
漠不关心的。
批评的。

questions.stem: How did language come into being according to researchers?
questions.stemZh: 根据研究人员的说法,语言是如何产生的?

explain.定位: Researchers don't think language was invented; instead, they think it evolved. 研究者不认为语言是被发明出来的；相反，他们认为它是进化（演变）而来的。
explain.信号: 否定+instead 的对比落点。这句靠 don't think 先否掉一个说法、再用 instead 引出真正 的答案——『否定 + instead/but』之后才是真意。前半 language was invented（被发 明）是要被排除的，后半 they think it evolved（进化而来）才是研究者的真实立场。
explain.替换: they think it evolved ↔Through evolution. 动词 evolved 名词化为 evolution
explain.排除: C) 原词陷阱 Through invention. 直接套用了录音里的 invented 一词，听到 invent 就想选正中陷阱 ——但原文是 don't think language was invented，明确否定了『发明』这个说法，所以 它恰恰是错的。 借用原文：Researchers don't think language was invented A) 未提及 Through deliberation.（通过深思熟虑/商议）在录音里根本没出现，研究者只在 invented 和 evolved 之间表态，从未说语言是『商量出来的』。 D) 未提及 Through collaboration.（通过协作）听上去合理，但录音只谈『进化还是发明』，从没说 语言是靠人们协作产生的，属于自己脑补、原文未给的内容。

optionsZh: 通过深思熟虑。
通过进化。
通过发明。
通过协作。

questions.stem: How did language start according to the first theory?
questions.stemZh: 根据第一种理论,语言是如何起源的?
questions.answerText: With people imitating sounds around them.

explain.定位: The first theory is that language started with people making different sounds, mostly imitating the things around them, like animal calls, nature sounds, and the sounds of tools. 第一个理论是：语言始于人们发出各种不同的声音，主要是模仿周围的事物，比如动物的叫 声、自然的声响和工具发出的声音。
explain.信号: started with 直接点出起点。这句用 language started with（语言始于……）这种明确的 『起点』标志词，正面回答题干问的『怎么开始』；其后的 imitating the things around them（模仿周围事物）就是起步的具体动作。
explain.替换: making different sounds, mostly imitating the things around them ↔ With people imitating sounds around them. imitating things around→imitating sounds around
explain.排除: B) 原词陷阱 With people interacting with animals close by. 抓住了录音里的 animal calls（动物叫 声）做诱饵，但原文说的是『模仿动物的叫声』，不是『和身边的动物互动』——听到 animal 就选就掉进陷阱，模仿声音 ≠ 与动物互动。 借用原文：like animal calls, nature sounds, and the sounds of tools D) 答非所问 With people trying to string sounds together. 套用了原文 stringing the words together，但那是录音明说『At some point』（在某个时间点）才出现的后期步骤，不是 『怎么开始』；它答的是后来的事，与题干问的『起点』错位。 借用原文：people started stringing the words together to form sentences C) 张冠李戴 With people showing each other things nearby. 的『互相展示身边的东西』其实更接近 第三段第二个理论里的『比划、用手指东西』，而本题限定 the first theory，张冠李戴把 另一个理论的内容搬了过来。 借用原文：pointing at things with their hands and imitating actions using their bodies

optionsZh: 人们模仿周围的声音。
人们与附近的动物互动。
人们相互展示附近的事物。
人们试图将声音串联起来。
options: With people imitating sounds around them.
With people interacting with animals close by.
With people showing each other things nearby.
With people trying to string sounds together.

questions.stem: Why did people switch from gesturing to making sounds according to the more recent theory?
questions.stemZh: 根据较新的理论,人们为什么从做手势转向发出声音?
questions.answerText: Making sounds helps one communicate with people they can't see.

explain.定位: The reason they switched to making sounds, the theory goes, is that talking out loud lets you communicate with someone even when you can't see them. 按这个理论的说法，人们之所以改用发声，原因是大声说话能让你即使在看不见对方的时候 也能与之交流。
explain.信号: The reason…is that 直给原因。这句以 The reason they switched to making sounds 开头、用 is that 直接引出理由，是最明确的因果信号；is that 后面的 even when you can't see them 就是『为什么改成出声』的答案。
explain.替换: communicate with someone even when you can't see them ↔ Making sounds helps one communicate with people they can't see. 几乎逐词对应的同义改写
explain.排除: A) 过度推断 Making sounds can free one's hands for doing other things.『腾出双手做别的事』听 上去很合理，但录音从手语切到发声时只给了『看不见也能交流』这一个理由，从没提过 『腾出手』，这是凭常识自己补出来的，原文未给。 B) 原词陷阱 Making sounds proves markedly easier than sign languages. 借用了录音里的 sign language，但原文只说手语后来发展出发声，从没比较『出声比手语更容易』，这个 easier 的比较是凭空加上去的。 借用原文：after developing sign languages, people eventually started making sounds C) 未提及 Making sounds enables one to express their ideas more explicitly.『能更清楚地表达想 法』是个看似合理的好处，但录音给出的唯一理由是『看不见对方也能交流』，从没说出声 能表达得『更明确』，属于无中生有。

optionsZh: 发出声音可以解放双手去做其他事情。
发出声音明显比手语更容易。
发出声音使人能够更明确地表达自己的想法。
发出声音有助于人们与看不见的人交流。
options: Making sounds can free one's hands for doing other things.
Making sounds proves markedly easier than sign languages.
Making sounds enables one to express their ideas more explicitly.
Making sounds helps one communicate with people they can't see. Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: How would people describe someone who shows off their social status according to new research?
questions.stemZh: 根据新研究,人们会如何描述炫耀自己社会地位的人?

explain.定位: But new research found that people believe someone who shows off their social status cares more about benefiting themselves than helping others. 但新研究发现，人们认为炫耀自己社会地位的人更在意让自己得益，而非帮助他人。
explain.信号: 转折 But + new research。答案句以 But new research found 起头，转折词 But 加上题 干点名的『new research』双重信号——前一句讲『显得有钱被认为更聪明自律』是铺 垫，But 之后才是新研究的真正结论，这正是答案落点。
explain.替换: cares more about benefiting themselves than helping others ↔Somewhat selfish. 整句释义→一词概括
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 Well disciplined. 盗用了答案句前那句铺垫里的 disciplined，但那句说的是『显得有钱的 人被认为更自律』，是 But 之前的对比信息，不是新研究对炫耀者的评价，听到 disciplined 就选正中陷阱。 借用原文：people who appear to be wealthy tend to be considered more intelligent, disciplined, and competent B) 未提及 Quite confident.『相当自信』录音通篇没有提到，是凭『炫耀的人大概很自信』的常识硬 推出来的，没有原文依据。 D) 原词陷阱 Highly intelligent. 盗用了铺垫句里的 intelligent，同样出自 But 之前『显得有钱者被认为 更聪明』的对比信息，不是新研究对炫耀者的真正评价，与 A 是同一类陷阱。 借用原文：people who appear to be wealthy tend to be considered more intelligent

optionsZh: 纪律严明的
相当自信的
有些自私的
高度聪明的

questions.stem: When were participants more likely to choose someone who signaled their wealth or status?
questions.stemZh: 参与者在什么情况下更可能选择那些展示自己财富或地位的人?
questions.answerText: When they wanted to have a competitive team member.

explain.定位: But participants were more likely to choose that person when they're looking for a competitive team member. 但当参与者在寻找一名有竞争力的团队成员时，他们更倾向于选这个人。
explain.信号: 转折 But + more likely。本段先说『seeking cooperative members 时不太会选』，But participants were more likely to choose 用 But 转折并出现题干同款的 more likely to choose，这句把『更愿意选』明确配给了后面那种情形，正是答案句。
explain.替换: looking for a competitive team member ↔ When they wanted to have a competitive team member. 近义动词替换
explain.排除: B) 与原文相反 When they were looking for a cooperative workmate. 盗用了 looking for 的句式和 『合作』概念，但录音说『找 cooperative members 时反而 less likely 选』，正好与题干 问的 more likely 相反，是把『不选』的情形错当成『选』的情形。 借用原文：participants were less likely to choose someone who signals their wealth or status to join a group seeking cooperative members C) 原词陷阱 When they found collaboration essential to them. 搬来第一段的 cooperation is essential 那层意思（collaboration、essential），听着很耳熟，但那是讲『需要合作时该 谦逊』，与本题『更愿意选炫耀者』的情形无关，是典型听到熟词就想选的陷阱。 借用原文：Modesty may be key when cooperation is essential D) 未提及 When they were seeking someone to help them.『想找人帮忙时』录音从未把『更愿意 选炫耀者』绑到这种情形上，是凭常识臆造的条件，无原文依据。

optionsZh: 当他们想要一个有竞争力的团队成员时
当他们在寻找一个合作的工作伙伴时
当他们发现合作对自己至关重要时
当他们在寻找能帮助自己的人时
options: When they wanted to have a competitive team member.
When they were looking for a cooperative workmate.
When they found collaboration essential to them.
When they were seeking someone to help them.

questions.stem: What should people do when sharing their wealth and status online?
questions.stemZh: 人们在网上分享自己的财富和地位时应该做什么?

explain.定位: People can easily share their wealth and status to large audiences, but they need to consider the consequences. 人们可以轻松地向广大受众展示自己的财富和地位，但他们需要考虑后果。
explain.信号: 建议信号 need to + 转折 but。末段先说『社媒能轻易把财富地位分享给大众』，but they need to consider the consequences 用 but 转折并带 need to（需要做某事）这一 建议信号，把『该怎么做』直接点出，是答案句。
explain.替换: need to consider the consequences ↔Consider the consequences. 建议句去主语即选项
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 Avoid frightening competitors. 搬来末段的 frighten competitors，但录音说炫耀『可以 帮你吓退竞争者』，那是分享地位的好处之一，并非『应该做什么』的建议；而且选项加了 Avoid（避免）把意思反成『避免吓退』，与原文方向不符。 借用原文：Posting about luxury purchases and expensive vacations online may help you to persuade others and frighten competitors B) 张冠李戴 Make clear their social goal. 借了第二段的 depending on their social goal，但那句讲 的是『按社交目标调整自我展示』，不是末段『网上分享该怎么做』的建议，是把别段内容 安到本题头上。 借用原文：people should change how they present themselves depending on their social goal C) 原词陷阱 Adopt persuasive strategies. 盗用末段 persuade others 的词根（persuasive），但录音 说炫耀『可以帮你说服别人』也是好处之一，不是建议人去『采取说服策略』，属听到 persuade 就想选的陷阱。 借用原文：may help you to persuade others 1 Human fascination with animals goes back as far as humans do. Of the oldest cave paintings discovered, some are up to 40,000 years old, and there are more images of animals than humans. At some point, humans began to capture and hold animals. 人类对动物的迷恋可以追溯到人类诞生之初。在已发现的最古老洞穴壁画中,有些距今已有4万年之久,其中 动物图像多于人类图像。在某个时期,人类开始捕获和饲养动物。 2 The first-known collections were held by royalty and were not open to the public. In Egypt, researchers have found buildings from around 3500 B.C., containing the remains of animals, including elephants, which were not native to Egypt. But life wasn't easy for these animals. They probably had short lives, and their remains show evidence of severe injuries. 已知最早的动物收藏由王室持有,不对公众开放。在埃及,研究人员发现了约公元前3500年的建筑,其中存有 动物遗骸,包括并非埃及本土物种的大象。但这些动物的生活并不轻松。它们的寿命可能很短,其遗骸显示 出严重受伤的痕迹。 3 The first public exhibit of animals may have been created by Egypt's Queen Hatshepsut around 1480 B.C. Researchers think the zoo was started with animals brought home from a far-off land known as Punt. It's unclear why the Queen built the zoo, but it might have been to show off her wealth and power. 首个向公众展出的动物园可能由埃及女王Hatshepsut于公元前1480年左右建造。研究人员认为该动物园 始于从一个名为Punt的遥远之地带回的动物。女王建造动物园的原因尚不清楚,但可能是为了炫耀她的财 富和权力。 Questions 22 to 25 are based on the passage you have just heard. 4 Early zoos are found all over the world. In China, Emperor Wenwang is said to have built a "Garden of Intelligence" around 1060 B.C. It included deer, birds, and many fish. In England, King Henry I set up a collection of animals in about 1110 as part of the royal estate. His collection included tigers and lions. This collection eventually moved to the Tower of London in 1235. The collection stayed at that location for 600 years. 早期动物园遍布世界各地。在中国,据说周文王于公元前1060年左右建造了一座"灵囿",其中包括鹿、鸟类 和许多鱼类。在英国,亨利一世国王于1110年左右在皇家庄园内设立了动物收藏。他的收藏包括老虎和狮 子。这个收藏最终于1235年迁至伦敦塔。该收藏在那里保留了600年。

明确自己的社交目标

questions.stem: What can we see in the oldest cave paintings?
questions.stemZh: 我们能在最古老的洞穴壁画中看到什么?
questions.answerText: More images of animals than humans.

explain.定位: Of the oldest cave paintings discovered, some are up to 40,000 years old, and there are more images of animals than humans. 在已发现的最古老的洞穴壁画中，有些距今多达四万年，而且其中动物的图像比人类的图像 更多。
explain.信号: 题干原词 oldest cave paintings 复现处。原文 Of the oldest cave paintings discovered 与题干 the oldest cave paintings 是同一处，紧跟其后的 there are more images of animals than humans 就是承载答案的关键句，靠题干主题词在原文复现来 定位。
explain.替换: more images of animals than humans ↔More images of animals than humans. 几乎原句照搬
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 Much evidence of humans capturing animals. 盗用了下一句 humans began to capture and hold animals 的 capture 一词，但那讲的是后来人类开始圈养动物，不是壁 画内容；题问壁画里能看到什么，答非所问。 借用原文：humans began to capture and hold animals C) 未提及 Fewer images of buildings than animals. 里的 buildings 在第一段壁画的描述中根本没 提（buildings 出现在第二段讲埃及建筑处），壁画只比较了 animals 与 humans，没说 buildings 的图像，属凭空捏造。 D) 与原文相反 Little proof of human fascination with animals. 用了开头句 Human fascination with animals 的原词，却说成 Little proof（很少证据）；而原文开头明说人类对动物的迷恋自 古就有、壁画里动物图像还更多，恰恰是证据充分，极性完全相反。 借用原文：Human fascination with animals goes back as far as humans do

optionsZh: 人类捕捉动物的大量证据。
动物的图像多于人类的图像。
建筑物的图像少于动物的图像。
人类对动物着迷的证据很少。
options: Much evidence of humans capturing animals.
More images of animals than humans.
Fewer images of buildings than animals.
Little proof of human fascination with animals.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the first-known collections of animals?
questions.stemZh: 关于最早已知的动物收藏,我们了解到什么?

explain.定位: The first-known collections were held by royalty and were not open to the public. 已知最早的（动物）收藏由王室持有，并且不对公众开放。
explain.信号: 题干主语 first-known collections 在原文复现处。原文 The first-known collections were held by royalty 与题干 the first-known collections of animals 是同一主语，紧跟 其后对「归谁所有、是否开放」的正面陈述就是答案句，靠题干主语在原文复现来定位。
explain.替换: were held by royalty ↔They were kept by royalty. held 同义替换为 kept
explain.排除: A) 与原文相反 They were open to the public. 借用了原文 not open to the public 里的 open to the public 短语，却把否定的 not 去掉，说成对公众开放；原文恰恰说这些最早的收藏不对公 众开放，极性相反。 借用原文：were not open to the public B) 与原文相反 They were primarily native. 盗用了原文 native 一词，却把意思整个说反：原文是 not native to Egypt（大象不是埃及本土的），选项却说 primarily native（主要是本土的）， 方向相反。 借用原文：which were not native to Egypt D) 与原文相反 They were hardly injured. 借用了原文 injuries 一词，却说几乎没受伤；原文明说 their remains show evidence of severe injuries（遗骸显示有严重伤害），是伤得很重，与选 项正好相反。 借用原文：their remains show evidence of severe injuries

optionsZh: 它们向公众开放。
它们主要是本地的。
它们由皇室饲养。
它们几乎没有受伤。
options: They were open to the public.

questions.stem: What might be the reason the Egyptian Queen created the zoo?
questions.stemZh: 埃及女王创建动物园的原因可能是什么?
questions.answerText: To show off her riches and power.

explain.定位: It's unclear why the Queen built the zoo, but it might have been to show off her wealth and power. 女王为何建这座动物园尚不清楚，但可能是为了炫耀她的财富与权力。
explain.信号: 转折 but 之后的目的句。答案句的信号是转折加目的：It's unclear why 先说原因不明，转 折词 but 之后 it might have been to show off her wealth and power 才给出真正的可能 原因，but 后 + to do 处即答案。
explain.替换: to show off her wealth and power ↔To show off her riches and power. wealth 同义替换为 riches
explain.排除: A) 原词陷阱 To enable the public to watch animals close by. 把第三段开头 The first public exhibit of animals 里的 public 拿来当动机，但 public exhibit 只是给这座动物园定性，原文说的 建园原因是炫耀财富权力，不是为让公众近距离看动物。 借用原文：The first public exhibit of animals B) 张冠李戴 To introduce to Egyptians animals from Punt. 盗用了原文 a far-off land known as Punt 的地名 Punt，但原文说 Punt 只是动物的来源地（从那带回动物），不是建园是为了 向埃及人介绍这些动物，张冠李戴。 借用原文：animals brought home from a far-off land known as Punt C) 未提及 To protect the endangered animals. 说为保护濒危动物，但全文从未提到 protect 或 endangered，建园原因原文只给了炫耀财富权力一种，属凭空添加。

optionsZh: 使公众能够近距离观看动物。
向埃及人介绍来自Punt的动物。
保护濒危动物。
炫耀她的财富和权力。
options: To enable the public to watch animals close by.
To introduce to Egyptians animals from Punt.
To show off her riches and power.

questions.stem: What do we learn about King Henry I's collection of animals in England?
questions.stemZh: 关于英格兰国王亨利一世的动物收藏,我们了解到什么?
questions.answerText: It was part of the royal estate.

explain.定位: In England, King Henry I set up a collection of animals in about 1110 as part of the royal estate. 在英格兰，亨利一世国王约在 1110 年建立了一处动物收藏，作为王室领地的一部分。
explain.信号: 人名 King Henry I 后紧跟的定性。定位靠人名复现：题干问 King Henry I，原文 In England, King Henry I set up a collection of animals 一出现这个名字，紧跟的 as part of the royal estate 就是对这处收藏的定性，即答案句。
explain.替换: as part of the royal estate ↔It was part of the royal estate. 近乎原句对应
explain.排除: B) 未提及 It was a shelter for wild animals. 借用了全篇反复出现的 animals，但原文从没把亨利一 世这处收藏说成野生动物的庇护所（shelter），这是凭空添加的定性。 C) 过度推断 It was the kingdom's best-equipped zoo. 用 best-equipped（装备最好的）拔高，但原 文只说它是 part of the royal estate 并养有老虎狮子，从未评价它是王国里设施最好的动 物园，属过度拔高。 借用原文：His collection included tigers and lions D) 张冠李戴 It was the first public exhibit of animals. 盗用了第三段 The first public exhibit of animals 的原话，但那说的是埃及女王 Hatshepsut 的动物园，不是英格兰亨利一世这处， 把别处的定性安到了这处头上。 借用原文：The first public exhibit of animals may have been created by Egypt's Queen Hatshepsut Identifying why the fast-fashion business model creates waste and determining whether regulators can establish incentives for consumers and manufacturers are steps to reduce waste. 第1段，第3句 涵盖并列主语（动名词短语）、宾语从句（why 和 whether 引导）、系表结构、后置定语（介词短 语 for consumers and manufacturers）等多种成分，且并列主语各自嵌套从句是常见易错点。适合 训练学生识别复杂主语、区分动名词与谓语、以及定位从句边界的能力。 In the absence of environmentally and economically feasible recycling options, fast-fashion manufacturers pump out low-quality clothes produced in high volumes that are worn only a few times and then discarded. 第2段，第2句 定语从句修饰宾语、过去分词作后置定语、介词短语作状语、并列谓语结构，这些都是四六级和考 研阅读中的高频句式。句子整体结构代表了学术写作和新闻报道的常见模式，学习后可广泛迁移。 I mean, getting rid of rush hour may be impossible, but it could be made more tolerable, don't you think? 第4段，第2句 本句覆盖了动名词短语作主语（getting rid of rush hour）、系表结构（may be impossible）、被 动语态中的宾语补足语（more tolerable），以及否定疑问句的主谓识别。这些成分组合在基础训 练中较有代表性，尤其动名词主语和被动结构是常见易错点，训练价值中等偏上。 W: Well, for example, the subway system could have air conditioning. 第6段，第1句 情态动词 + 动词原形 + 宾语的结构在四六级和考研真题中较为常见，属于常规句式。但本句过于 简单，没有展现从句嵌套、复杂修饰或其他高频难点结构，代表性中等。掌握本句结构对理解类似 简单陈述句有帮助，但迁移价值不如包含从句或复杂修饰成分的句子。 I know many cities in the world have air conditioning in their subway, so why can't we? 第6段，第2句 包含宾语从句（省略 that）和并列主句（so 连接因果关系），这两种结构在四六级和考研真题中 高频出现，具有较强的代表性和迁移价值。 And add to that the rush-hour crowds with strangers packed close together in the subway carriages, the whole thing is just horrible. 第6段，第5句 本句覆盖了祈使句谓语、及物动词宾语（含较长的后置修饰）、介词短语状语、主系表结构、程度 状语等多种成分，且第一个主句的宾语部分较长，包含独立主格结构作后置定语，适合练习如何在 复杂修饰中识别宾语边界。第二个主句虽简单但典型。整体成分种类较丰富，有一定训练价值，但 难度不高，不算"坑点密集"的高难练习句。 I guess I'm fortunate I take the bus instead. 第7段，第4句 I guess 引导宾语从句、形容词后接从句(fortunate 后省略 that)都是四六级和考研阅读中的高频句 式,双层宾语从句嵌套也较为典型。掌握本句结构后,可迁移至大量类似表达(I think/believe/feel + 从句、glad/sure/afraid + 从句等),实用性强。 The city is too big to move around easily. 第8题，D "too ... to ..." 句型在四六级和考研阅读中频繁出现，是表达程度与结果关系的典型结构，学生掌握 后可直接迁移到大量类似句子。 What does the woman suggest doing? 第9题题干 "特殊疑问词 + 助动词 + 主语 + 动词原形"是非常常见的基础问句框架，考试和日常阅读里都高频 出现。掌握这种识别路径后，可直接迁移到大量同类句子。 What do we learn about the man from the conversation? 第10题题干 本句为典型的特殊疑问句结构（疑问词 + 助动词 + 主语 + 动词原形 + 状语），是四六级听力和阅 读中常见的提问方式，掌握后可迁移至大量类似疑问句的理解和构造，代表性较强。 M: He had some plastic surgery done. 第3段，第1句 have something done 使役结构在四六级和考研阅读中高频出现,掌握后可迁移至大量类似句式,如 get something done、have something repaired 等,具有很强的代表性。 M: Well, he had it fixed. 第7段，第1句 have something done 使役结构在口语和考试中频繁出现，属于高频实用句式，掌握后可迁移至大 量类似表达（如 get something done, have something repaired 等）。 He had an operation done on it, plastic surgery, in order to cover it and make it less noticeable. 第9段，第2句 使役结构 "have something done" 和目的状语 "in order to" 都是四六级和考研常考句式，同位语补 充说明也是典型用法，整体结构在真题中出现频率高，学习迁移价值大 It never occurred to me that he should have it taken care of like that. 第10段，第4句 本句覆盖了形式主语与真正主语的区分、主语从句、使役动词后接宾语和宾语补足语、方式状语等 多种成分，且涉及易错点（如 It 的性质判断、taken care of 是补语而非谓语）。作为划分成分的练 习句，训练价值较高。 In fact, I thought it added character… like it gave him a certain uniqueness. 第11段，第3句 主句 + 宾语从句(省略 that)+ 状语从句的三层嵌套是四六级和考研阅读中高频出现的句式;双宾语结 构和 "like" 引导方式状语从句也是常考点;整体结构具有较强代表性,掌握后可应用于大量类似长难 句的理解。 W: He must have felt differently though. 第12段，第1句 "情态动词 + have + 过去分词" 表示对过去的推测，是四六级和考研阅读、听力中的常见句式，尤 其在对话和议论文中频繁出现。主系表结构本身也非常典型。句末 "though" 作副词表转折的用法 同样常见。掌握本句结构后可以迁移到大量类似句子的理解和生成中。 He must have felt self-conscious and insecure, perhaps. 第12段，第2句 情态动词加完成式表推测是四六级和考研阅读中的常见句式,尤其在描述对过去事件的推断或假设 时频繁出现。主系表结构配合情态动词的组合也是典型的考点结构。掌握本句的分析方法后,可迁 移至大量类似句型,具有较强的代表性和实用性。 As you said, he had had it for most of his life. 第13段，第3句 "As you said" 引导方式状语从句置于句首的结构在四六级和考研阅读中频繁出现，主句使用过去完 成时表示"在过去某时间点之前持续的状态"也是高频考点；"had had" 的双 "had" 结构属于典型易 混淆句式，掌握后可迁移至大量类似句子的识别。 If Johnny's girlfriend doesn't like him for who he is, then she does not deserve to be his girlfriend. 第16段，第3句 条件状语从句搭配主句是四六级和考研高频句式,宾语从句嵌套在状语从句中也是真题常见结 构。"for+宾语从句"作状语、"who"在从句中作表语等都是典型考点。掌握后可在阅读和写作中大 量迁移,代表性较强。 So he is insane to give in to her like that. 第17段，第2句 本句涵盖主语、谓语（系动词）、表语、状语四种基本成分，适合练习主系表结构和不定式状语的 识别；但成分种类相对单一，无宾语、无定语从句、无复杂修饰，缺少易错的成分辨析点（如宾补 与表语的区分、多层定语的归属等），训练价值中等偏下。 He used to wear a sad face in school. 第12题，C "used to" 结构是英语考试中常见的考点，表示过去习惯的用法在四六级和考研阅读中经常出现， 学生需要掌握。主谓宾加地点状语的基本句型也具有一定代表性。但作为简单句，它不涉及从句、 复杂修饰或长难句的典型结构特征，因此典型性属于中等水平。 He had some plastic surgery done. 第12题，D 虽然句子不长、没有从句，但它在主干识别和补足语判断上有明确训练价值，适合用来夯实基础结 构分析。对结构和时态入门训练来说，值得优先掌握。 It seemed to make up for his physical defects. 第14题，D 形式主语结构在四六级和考研阅读中频繁出现，是常考句式之一。"It seems/appears/happens + 不定式/that 从句" 这类模式具有较高的迁移价值。但本句结构相对简单，没有更复杂的嵌套或修饰 成分，因此典型性中等偏上，但不算高度典型的复杂真题句式。 An animal might make 10 different sounds, but an adult human knows more than 20,000 words. 第1段，第2句 并列转折句（"but" 连接）是四六级和考研中的高频句式，情态动词加动词原形的谓语结构也很常 见。掌握本句后，学生可将并列转折的分析方法迁移到大量类似句子中。 Additionally, we're the only animal that expresses thoughts in full sentences. 第1段，第3句 “主句 + 名词后置限定修饰”是阅读里非常常见的基本句式，尤其适合练习识别“that”引出的修饰结 构。掌握这种看法后，可迁移到大量类似句子。 Researchers don't think language was invented; instead, they think it evolved. 第1段，第4句 并列句加宾语从句的组合在四六级和考研阅读中非常常见,尤其是表达对比观点的转折并列结构,以 及think等动词后跟省略that的宾语从句,都是高频句式,典型性较强,值得掌握。 Eventually these gestures turned into a full sign language. 第3段，第2句 简单的主谓宾结构在考试中常见，句首状语修饰全句也是典型用法；但本句过于基础，缺少从句、 并列、特殊句式等高频考点结构，代表性处于中等水平。 This theory guesses that after developing sign languages, people eventually started making sounds along with their gestures. 第3段，第3句 "及物动词 + that 宾语从句" 是四六级和考研阅读中极为常见的句式，如 "研究表明 that..."、"专家 认为 that..." 等。掌握这种结构后可以快速识别大量类似句子，迁移价值高。 The reason they switched to making sounds, the theory goes, is that talking out loud lets you communicate with someone even when you can't see them. 第3段，第5句 覆盖成分丰富：主语含同位语从句、系动词、表语从句、宾语补足语、时间状语从句；同时涉及动 名词作主语 "talking out loud"、"let sb do sth" 结构、情态动词谓语等多个易错点；特别是同位语 questions.passage:
A) Recently, a leading design federation in the UK warned that the UK could face a creative skills shortage, after the latest figures revealed a drop of almost 10 percent in students studying Design and Technology. These figures showed that the number of pupils that sat exams in Design and Technology fell 10 percent from 204,788 to 185,279 last year.
B) Chief executive John Kampfner of the Creative Industries Federation thinks that this drop in figures has worrying implications for the skills pipeline in Britain's hugely successful arts and creative industries. He said, "We already have skills shortages in many jobs such as animation(动画制作) and special effects." He added: "Engineering, which requires a similar mix of creative and technical skills, also has recruitment problems."
C) Many other designers and architects have expressed concern over the future supply of home-grown talent for UK firms, and industry bodies have pointed out that there has been a lack of roots-level support. However, if these designers had visited the Design Museum shop in London earlier this year their fears may have been eased. With £10 to spend, they could have bought a fascinating children's toy called "Dazzle Racer". An automotive cylinder(圆柱体), it included a wind-up, elastic(有弹性的)- band-powered mechanism, minimal parts, all 100 percent recycled, and lots of stickers. It was good fun, simple, eye-catching and very original.
D) Well, you'd expect the Design Museum to commission and make some interesting items, but this one was different. Designed by a group of six Year 9 and Year 10 boys from Finchley Catholic High School, the toy was the winning entry in the museum's 2015 Design Ventura competition, which brings the business of design to life for students aged 13 to 16 by challenging them to develop a new creative, sustainable and commercially feasible product for the Design Museum shop and attracts hundreds of entries nationwide.
E) "We did Design Ventura in my previous school," says Liam Hourican, Finchley Catholic High School's design technology curriculum leader. "Then when I changed schools four years ago, I introduced it here because it helps to develop so many skills."
F) The theme for last year's competition was "Move", and Hourican began with three groups working in lunch breaks and after school before selecting the group with the most innovative idea. Each participating school may submit just one proposal. "It's the taking part and doing the work which is important," he says. "And I never dreamt we'd win."
G) Catherine Ritman Smith, head of learning at the Design Museum, is expecting around 10,000 participants aged 13 to 16 to take part this year and says that the project—funded by Deutsche Bank as part of its youth engagement programme Born To Be—is the biggest event in the museum's calendar. "We started Design Ventura with around 800 young people in 2010 and it has grown steadily since," she says. "Teachers like it because the skills are all transferable and it helps to validate the value of design as a subject," she explains, telling me that nearly 600 schools have taken part so far.
H) So how does the competition work? A single-word theme is announced in the summer. This year it is "Change". Schools work with groups to produce imaginative design ideas for a product in simple materials that could sell for £10 in the Design Museum shop. Participating schools then register by November and eventually submit their design idea. Along the way there is training and support for teachers and tutoring for students from designers. An additional bonus is when the winners see their design on sale in the spring of the following year.
I) Hourican and his pupils have happy memories of spending a whole day at the museum, having been selected as one of 10 shortlisted schools to present their idea to a panel of judges, including designer Jasper Conran. Then they worked with the Kin Design Studio in Shoreditch, met designers at their school and attended a lunch with Deutsche Bank employees. The students helped to make decisions and there were plenty of discussions—they changed the product's name, for example.
J) "One of the really useful things about this competition," says Hourican, "is that there's a commercial element because the product is going on sale for real and the boys had to learn about budgeting and marketing, as well as designing their game." Profits go to charity. "The winning team chooses where it wants the profits to go," says Ritman Smith. "The Finchley Catholic High School product raised about £1,000 for Great Ormond Street Hospital." Winning entries in past years have included a make- your-own cloth kit called Dove Bunting and a threefold, wallet-sized travel game with goals at each end, called Badoiiing.
K) It costs the schools nothing to participate in Design Ventura; the professional designers provide their services for free. Among them are architect Asif Khan, a Design Museum trustee who has worked as designer-in-residence at the museum, helping emerging architects. He has recently been commissioned to design the new Museum of London building in Smithfield.
L) Another is television presenter and interior designer Naomi Cleaver, who is one of the competition's judges. "I'm very keen to encourage young people," she says, observing that design brings together other subjects such as literature, art, history, geography and science. "Now that design education is
M) Ritman Smith adds: "Design technology has become a tricky subject to make a case for, and we've heard of departments closing in some schools. We find that if pupils take part in Design Ventura in Year Nine it can be the trigger which leads them to opt for it at General Certificate of Secondary Education, so we are helping to keep alive something which is crucial to industry and entrepreneurship."

"We started Design Ventura with around 800 young people in 2010 and it has grown steadily since," she says. "Teachers like it because the skills are all transferable and it helps to validate the value of design as a subject," she explains, telling me that nearly 600 schools have taken part so far.

Winning entries in past years have included a make- your-own cloth kit called Dove Bunting and a threefold, wallet-sized travel game with goals at each end, called Badoiiing.

Among them are architect Asif Khan, a Design Museum trustee who has worked as designer-in-residence at the museum, helping emerging architects. He has recently been commissioned to design the new Museum of London building in Smithfield.
L) Another is television presenter and interior designer Naomi Cleaver, who is one of the competition's judges. "I'm very keen to encourage young people," she says, observing that design brings together other subjects such as literature, art, history, geography and science. "Now that design education is
M) Ritman Smith adds: "Design technology has become a tricky subject to make a case for, and we've heard of departments closing in some schools. We find that if pupils take part in Design Ventura in Year Nine it can be the trigger which leads them to opt for it at General Certificate of Secondary Education, so we are helping to keep alive something which is crucial to industry and entrepreneurship."

questions.passage:
P1 New research suggests that pandas may be at risk of dying out because they are too comfortable. Experts say too much happiness can stop the bears from searching for new mates.

P2 Environmentalists have long believed that building roads or homes near the bears may threaten their survival by "reducing or fragmenting their natural: habitats", The Times reported. But the new research suggests that a "modest degree of discomfort and fragmentation" may actually help preserve panda populations.

P3 The research was conducted by scientists from Michigan State University. It concluded that pandas fail to wander off in search of new mates if they find their habitat too comfortable, resulting in a lack of vital genetic diversity.

P4 For their study—outlined in a paper in the journal Conservation Biology—the team looked at genetic diversity and spread among a Chinese panda population. The ideal level of perfectly livable habitat was found to be only 80% of an area, with the remainder either too harsh or too affected by human activity.

P5 The experts concluded that pandas should ideally "be happy enough to thrive, but not so content that they don't want to move around and find new mates".

P6 Their conclusions about what The Guardian described as this "sweet spot" are in line with the so-called Goldilocks principle: that there can be just the right amount of something. The concept has been applied to a wide range of disciplines, from developmental psychology to economics and engineering.

P7 Claudio Sillero, a professor of conservation biology at Oxford University, told the newspaper that the new findings could have implications beyond panda conservation.

P8 "Most large animals that eat meat live in increasingly fragmented landscapes," said Sillero, who was not involved in the research. "It may well be that the messy nature of their relationship with human efforts induces more animals to scatter or travel further, and might result in greater genetic connectivity and enhanced population persistence."

P9 The most recent count of pandas found that there were more than 1,800 left in the wild, putting them on the list of vulnerable, but not endangered, species.

P7 Claudio Sillero, a professor of conservation biology at Oxford University, told the newspaper that the new findings could have implications beyond panda conservation.

P8 "Most large animals that eat meat live in increasingly fragmented landscapes," said Sillero, who was not involved in the research. "It may well be that the messy nature of their relationship with human efforts induces more animals to scatter or travel further, and might result in greater genetic connectivity and enhanced population persistence."

P9 The most recent count of pandas found that there were more than 1,800 left in the wild, putting them on the list of vulnerable, but not endangered, species.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about people born with natural talents?
questions.stemZh: 文章对天生具有才能的人有何评价?
options: They seem to outdo others without hard work.
They appear to know all the secrets to success.
They feel it only too logical to succeed.
They are bound to excel effortlessly.
optionsZh: 他们似乎不用努力就能超越他人。
他们似乎知道所有成功的秘诀。
他们觉得成功是理所当然的。

explain.判型: What does the passage say about people born with natural talents 直接问文章对一个 具体对象的陈述，没有 infer/imply/mainly about 这类字眼，是典型细节复述题。
explain.拆句: 主干是 What does the passage say about people，过去分词短语 born with natural talents 作后置定语修饰 people，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。 51. What does the passage say about people born with natural talents? A) They seem to outdo others without hard work. B) They appear to know all the secrets to success. C) They feel it only too logical to succeed. D) They are bound to excel effortlessly.
explain.定位: With those born with natural talents, it feels as if they excel without really trying. 对于那些天生有才的人，看上去就好像他们不太费力就能出类拔萃。
explain.选项: A) ✓ 正确 it feels as if they excel without really trying ↔ They seem to outdo others without hard work 预判的「看似/不费力/胜过别人」三个语义点在 A 中一一落位，无增项无漏项，A 是定 位句的同义改写。 B) 无中生有 原文只说他们看似不费力就出色，没说他们 know all the secrets to success——「掌 握所有成功秘诀」是凭空添加的内容。 C) 偷换概念 原文是「看上去毫不费力就成功」，选项却说 They feel it only too logical to succeed ——「他们觉得自己成功理所当然」是从他们的主观视角描写，与原文「旁观者眼中显 得轻松」不一致。 D) 过度推断 原文只用 it feels as if（似乎）表达印象，选项却用 are bound to（必然、注定）把可 能性写成必然性，过度推断。 Duckworth 对才能有何看法? A) 这是一个被过分高估的新概念。 B) 它被证明对于重大成就是必要的。 C) 它在一个人的成功中起较小的作用。 D) 它是人生真正成功的保证。

questions.passage:
P1 With those born with natural talents, it feels as if they excel without really trying. But what about those of us who don't have a natural talent? We've been told all our lives that if you work hard, you too can succeed. But with the release of Angela Duckworth's Grit, we are given a new key to success.

P2 "As much as talent counts, effort counts twice," says Duckworth in Grit. She introduces a new concept that talent may be overrated, and if you want real success, what you need is grit, the perfect combination of passion and persistence. Even if you have natural talent, it's nothing without grit.

P3 Duckworth says grit is the difference between success and failure. A person who has grit is more likely to succeed than a person who does not. When we think about attaining success—whether it's landing that job or learning that new skill—our thoughts are immediately burdened by all the things we must first learn. If you want that new job, you have to learn the job skills, then the interview skills, then the dress part—and you must be perfect at all of them. Grit is different because it tells us that perfection isn't the goal.

P4 Grit lifts the unreasonable expectations off our shoulders. Grit tells us that the door is open wider than we first thought possible. Grit allows us to redefine our goals. Think about it: what's something you've always wanted to do, but gave up because you "don't have the skills for it"? What's something you love but aren't good at?

P5 The real workings of grit are to have sustainable passion and continue to try. Effort means more than your natural ability. Even if you haven't mastered a skill, grit tells you that you can still succeed if you can transform your passion into action. In a way, Duckworth is giving new hope to people who have shut the doors on their dreams. She is saying it is possible that you can accomplish anything. If at first you fail, then try one more time with grit.

questions.stem: What does Duckworth say about talent?
questions.stemZh: Duckworth 对才能有何看法?
options: It is a new concept much too overrated.
It proves necessary for big achievements.
It plays a lesser role in one's success.
It is a guarantee for real success in life.
optionsZh: 这是一个被过分高估的新概念。
它被证明对于重大成就是必要的。
它在一个人的成功中起较小的作用。
它是人生真正成功的保证。

explain.判型: What does Duckworth say about talent 问的是特定人物对特定对象的陈述，是细节题。
explain.拆句: 结构与 51 题平行：What does Duckworth say about talent，主谓宾完整，无修饰 从句。
explain.定位: As much as talent counts, effort counts twice. 虽然才能很重要，但努力的重要性是它的两倍。 52. What does Duckworth say about talent? A) It is a new concept much too overrated. B) It proves necessary for big achievements. C) It plays a lesser role in one's success. D) It is a guarantee for real success in life.
explain.选项: A) 张冠李戴 It is a new concept much too overrated 把 She introduces a new concept 中「新 概念」的所指对象——其实是 grit——硬安到 talent 头上；原文说的「新概念」指 grit，而非 talent。 B) 与原文相反 原文反复说 talent 不够、需 grit 加持（Even if you have natural talent, it's nothing without grit）；选项却说 talent proves necessary for big achievements，是反向 陈述。 C) ✓ 正确 As much as talent counts, effort counts twice ↔It plays a lesser role in one's success talent may be overrated ↔plays a lesser role 预判的「才能不如努力重要、被高估」与 C 的「作用较小」在比较义上完全等值，C 正确。 D) 与原文相反 原文称 grit 才是 real success 的关键（if you want real success, what you need is grit），选项却说 talent is a guarantee for real success，把被弱化的对象说成「保 证」，方向与程度同时反了。 文章对想要获得成功的人有何评价? A) 他们困惑于如何向雇主展示自己最好的一面。 B) 他们被自己对完美的期望所困扰。 C) 他们会努力找到最适合自己技能的工作。 D) 他们会发现自己缺乏所需的所有技能。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about people thinking of attaining success?
questions.stemZh: 文章对想要获得成功的人有何评价?
options: They are puzzled how to present their best to the employer.
They are burdened by their expectation of perfection.
They will try hard to land a job that fits their skills best.
They will find themselves lacking in all the skills they need.
optionsZh: 他们困惑于如何向雇主展示自己最好的一面。
他们被自己对完美的期望所困扰。
他们会努力找到最适合自己技能的工作。
他们会发现自己缺乏所需的所有技能。

explain.判型: What does the passage say about people thinking of attaining success 仍是 say 句 型，针对一个具体场景，是细节题。
explain.拆句: 主干仍是 What does the passage say about people，现在分词短语 thinking of attaining success 作后置定语修饰 people；其中 attaining 是动名词作 of 的宾语，整体 「想着去获得成功的人」。 53. What does the passage say about people thinking of attaining success? A) They are puzzled how to present their best to the employer. B) They are burdened by their expectation of perfection. C) They will try hard to land a job that fits their skills best. D) They will find themselves lacking in all the skills they need.
explain.定位: When we think about attaining success—whether it's landing that job or learning that new skill—our thoughts are immediately burdened by all the things we must first learn. If you want that new job, you have to learn the job skills, then the interview skills, then the dress part—and you must be perfect at all of them. 当我们考虑获得成功时——不管是拿下那份工作还是学会某项新技能——我们的思绪立刻被 「必须先学会的所有东西」压得沉甸甸的。如果你想要那份新工作，你得学工作技能，然后 学面试技巧，再学穿衣得体——而且你必须在每一项上都做到完美。
explain.选项: A) 以偏概全 They are puzzled how to present their best to the employer 把原文里「找工作」举 例中的「dress part/interview skills」放大成全部困扰，且把 burdened 改成 puzzled ——既缩小到一例又改写状态词。 B) ✓ 正确 our thoughts are immediately burdened by all the things we must first learn ↔ They are burdened by their expectation of perfection 预判要求「负担 + 完美」两点齐备，B 正好同时命中——burdened 锁住「负担」， expectation of perfection 锁住「完美主义」。 C) 与原文相反 原文是「想成功的人感到被各种要求压垮」，选项却说他们 will try hard to land a job that fits their skills best——把焦虑负担改写成积极行动，方向反了。 D) 过度推断 原文说他们意识到要学很多东西，选项却说他们 lacking in all the skills they need ——把「要学的东西多」推到「所有技能都欠缺」，all 是绝对化程度词，原文未明说 欠缺。 作者认为毅力如何对我们有帮助? A) 它让我们知道自己擅长什么。 B) 它为我们打开了新机会的眼界。 C) 它使我们的注意力集中在所做的事情上。 D) 它让我们重新考虑要实现的目标。

questions.stem: How does the author think grit can be helpful to us?
questions.stemZh: 作者认为毅力如何对我们有帮助?
options: It allows us to know what we are good at.
It opens our eyes to new opportunities.
It focuses our attention on what we do.
It lets us reconsider the goals to achieve.
optionsZh: 它让我们知道自己擅长什么。
它为我们打开了新机会的眼界。
它使我们的注意力集中在所做的事情上。
它让我们重新考虑要实现的目标。

explain.判型: How does the author think grit can be helpful to us 问的是 grit 的具体作用，不是隐含 推断，是细节题。
explain.拆句: How does the author think grit can be helpful to us 是宾语从句嵌套结构：think 后接 省略 that 的从句 grit can be helpful to us，how 修饰整个 think 的方式逻辑——实际问 的是「作者认为 grit 以何种方式有帮助」。 54. How does the author think grit can be helpful to us? A) It allows us to know what we are good at. B) It opens our eyes to new opportunities. C) It focuses our attention on what we do. D) It lets us reconsider the goals to achieve.
explain.定位: Grit lifts the unreasonable expectations off our shoulders. Grit tells us that the door is open wider than we first thought possible. Grit allows us to redefine our goals. grit 把不合理的期待从我们肩上卸下来。grit 告诉我们这扇门比我们最初以为的开得更宽。 grit 允许我们重新定义自己的目标。

questions.stem: What message does Duckworth try to convey in her book Grit?
questions.stemZh: Duckworth 在她的《坚毅》一书中试图传达什么信息?
options: We should perfect ourselves to ensure success.
We should stay persistent even in face of failures.
We can never master a skill without constant practice.
We can never expect to reach our goals without passion.
optionsZh: 我们应该完善自己以确保成功。
我们应该即使面对失败也要坚持不懈。
没有持续练习,我们永远无法掌握一项技能。
没有热情,我们永远无法期望达到目标。

explain.判型: What message does Duckworth try to convey in her book Grit 问的是整本书的核心信 息，是典型主旨题。
explain.拆句: What message does Duckworth try to convey in her book Grit：宾语前置 What message，主干 Duckworth try to convey，介词短语 in her book Grit 作地点状语，无 难点。 55. What message does Duckworth try to convey in her book Grit? A) We should perfect ourselves to ensure success. B) We should stay persistent even in face of failures. C) We can never master a skill without constant practice. D) We can never expect to reach our goals without passion.
explain.选项: A) 与原文相反 原文反复说 perfection isn't the goal、Grit lifts the unreasonable expectations off our shoulders，明确否定完美主义；选项却让我们 perfect ourselves to ensure success，方向反了。 B) ✓ 正确 If at first you fail, then try one more time with grit ↔ We should stay persistent even in face of failures grit, the perfect combination of passion and persistence ↔stay persistent continue to try ↔stay persistent B 同时命中预判的两大语义点——「失败」和「坚持」，是把全文主线压缩到一句话的 最佳改写。 C) 以偏概全 Even if you haven't mastered a skill, grit tells you that you can still succeed 恰恰 说「没掌握技能也能成」；选项却把全书主旨说成 never master a skill without constant practice——把「关于 grit 的人生观」缩成「学技能要练习」，既偏题又用了 never 这种绝对化词。 D) 以偏概全 原文虽说 grit = passion + persistence，但全书主旨是「坚持着再试一次」，而非「没 激情就达不到目标」；选项 can never expect to reach our goals without passion 用 never 把 passion 描述为达成目标的「唯一条件」，把成对要素中的一个单独绝对化。
